l4_steps.output: Demand time-series per O&D × cabin × day-of-week × season band
l4_steps.kpi: Segment granularity covers ≥ 95% of revenue-bearing O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin O&D markets (< 200 observations per departure) produce statistically unstable booking curves; SkyCAST defaults to network-level priors which can over-smooth volatile new-route ramp-ups

l4_steps.name: Identify constrained booking observations
l4_steps.input: Segmented demand series + historical AU and sell limit records
l4_steps.output: Flagged constrained observations (departures where AU was binding at close)
l4_steps.kpi: Constrained-observation detection rate ≥ 90% vs manual audit sample
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM does not retain intra-day AU change history at sufficient granularity; when AUs were changed multiple times within a day, the system only logs end-of-day state, causing the unconstraining algorithm to miss intermediate constraints

l4_steps.name: Apply EM unconstraining to constrained series
l4_steps.input: Constrained observation flags + observed booking counts
l4_steps.output: Unconstrained demand estimate per O&D × fare class × departure date
l4_steps.kpi: Unconstraining variance (CV) ≤ 5% on routes with ≥ 90% load factor
l4_steps.pain_point: Expectation-Maximisation unconstraining can diverge on very high-load routes (LF > 95%) where almost every observation is constrained — NRM falls back to simple censored-mean imputation which understates true demand by 8–15%

l4_steps.name: Validate unconstrained demand estimates
l4_steps.input: Unconstrained demand series from step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Validated unconstrained demand series approved for model input
l4_steps.kpi: Unconstrained mean ≤ 1.5× constrained mean on non-peak markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Overly aggressive unconstraining inflates unconstrained demand estimates, causing the optimiser to open excess inventory and erode yield on near-full flights — requires manual override on seasonal peak routes

l4_steps.name: Select forecasting model type per market
l4_steps.input: Validated unconstrained demand series, market volatility scores
l4_steps.output: Model configuration file: additive vs multiplicative per O&D × cabin
l4_steps.kpi: Model selection logic applied to 100% of active O&D pairs within 1 hour of data readiness
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST model selection heuristics default to additive models for thin markets regardless of demand variability; high-leisure volatile routes on short-haul thin sectors are systematically misconfigured, requiring manual analyst overrides each cycle

l4_steps.name: Apply special-event & seasonality overlays
l4_steps.input: Model config + airline event calendar (holidays, conventions, sports, disruptions)
l4_steps.output: Seasonality-adjusted demand series with event uplift / suppression factors
l4_steps.kpi: Special-event adjustment coverage: ≥ 85% of Top-100 events per quarter captured before forecast run
l4_steps.pain_point: Event calendar maintenance is manual and decentralised — network RM team and regional market managers each maintain separate lists, causing duplicate or conflicting adjustments when the same event spans multiple O&D pairs

l4_steps.name: Run O&D demand forecast in SkyCAST
l4_steps.input: Seasonality-adjusted unconstrained demand series + model config
l4_steps.output: Point and probabilistic demand forecasts per O&D × cabin × booking horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast MAPE ≤ 12% across all O&D pairs; P90 forecast coverage ≥ 80% of actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST batch forecast runs for a large network (500+ daily departures) can exceed the available processing window on peak planning days, causing downstream NRM optimisation to run on partially stale forecasts

l4_steps.name: Disaggregate O&D forecast to fare-class level
l4_steps.input: O&D demand forecasts from step 3.3 + fare class demand share curves
l4_steps.output: Fare-class level demand forecast input for EMSRb optimisation
l4_steps.kpi: Fare-class forecast disaggregation completed within 30 min of O&D forecast publish
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare-class demand share curves are estimated from historical booking curves; when airlines reprice aggressively (e.g. adding or retiring fare classes mid-season), the share curves become stale and misdirect inventory allocation toward retired buckets

l4_steps.name: Analyst review of system-generated forecasts
l4_steps.input: Fare-class demand forecasts from step 3.4, booking pace actuals
l4_steps.output: Reviewed forecast report with analyst annotations and override candidates
l4_steps.kpi: Analyst review completed within 4 hours of forecast publication; < 15% of O&D pairs require manual override
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM forecast review UI surfaces only summary metrics per market; analysts cannot drill to individual booking-curve segments without exporting to Excel, slowing root-cause investigation and increasing override latency

l4_steps.name: Apply market-level manual forecast adjustments
l4_steps.input: Override candidate list from step 4.1, competitive intelligence, sales intelligence
l4_steps.output: Adjusted demand forecast with analyst override log
l4_steps.kpi: Override accuracy (post-departure MAPE for overridden markets) ≤ 10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual overrides are not systematically back-tested; analysts who override frequently cannot tell whether their interventions improve or degrade forecast accuracy versus the unmodified system forecast, making governance of override behaviour impossible

l4_steps.name: Publish approved demand forecast to NRM
l4_steps.input: Approved fare-class demand forecast (system + analyst overrides)
l4_steps.output: Active demand forecast loaded into NRM for EMSRb optimisation cycle
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast publish latency ≤ 30 min from analyst sign-off; 100% of departures within 330-day booking window covered
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM forecast publish is a full-replace operation — partial updates are not supported; if a publish job fails mid-run (e.g. network timeout), the system may hold a mix of new and prior-cycle forecasts, causing inconsistent AU recommendations until the next full cycle

l4_steps.name: Track post-departure forecast accuracy
l4_steps.input: Departed flight actuals (load factor, revenue, fare-class mix) vs forecast
l4_steps.output: Forecast accuracy scorecard: MAPE, bias, coverage by O&D, cabin, horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Rolling 30-day network MAPE ≤ 12%; bias (mean signed error) within ±2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-departure actuals are available only after PSS ticket coupon reconciliation (typically T+2 days), creating a 48-hour blind spot between departure and accuracy reporting that delays identification of systematic forecast failures on new routes

l4_steps.name: Detect systematic bias or model drift
l4_steps.input: Forecast accuracy scorecard from step 5.1
l4_steps.output: Bias / drift diagnostic report with affected O&D segments identified
l4_steps.kpi: Bias alert triggered when mean signed error exceeds ±3% for ≥ 5 consecutive departures on same O&D
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards for RM forecast tracking are maintained by a separate analytics team; model drift alerts depend on manual dashboard reviews rather than automated statistical process control, meaning bias can persist for 2–3 weeks before analyst intervention

l4_steps.name: Trigger model recalibration & parameter update
l4_steps.input: Bias / drift diagnostic report + recalibration threshold breach flags
l4_steps.output: Updated model coefficients and booking-curve parameters deployed to SkyCAST
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration cycle completed within 48 hours of bias-alert trigger; post-recalibration MAPE improvement ≥ 2 percentage points
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST model parameter updates require a full re-training run on the rolling 2-year history window; on large networks this can take 6–8 hours, blocking the daily forecast cycle if recalibration is triggered mid-day rather than during the overnight batch window

l4_steps.name: Receive Group Booking Request
l4_steps.input: Group booking request via SWABIZ portal, GDS, travel agency, or direct sales channel
l4_steps.output: Logged group enquiry record with O&D, travel dates, pax count, and contact details
l4_steps.kpi: Request acknowledgement within 4 business hours; ≥95% SLA compliance
l4_steps.pain_point: Requests arriving via multiple channels (email, GDS PNR, SWABIZ) require manual consolidation into Altéa — no single intake API across all channels

l4_steps.name: Validate Group Size Eligibility
l4_steps.input: Passenger count stated in group request
l4_steps.output: Eligibility determination: group (≥10 pax) or retail redirection
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of sub-threshold requests correctly redirected to retail within 1 business hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Groups splitting into sub-10 clusters to access retail fares while exploiting group seat release policies — requires cross-PNR duplicate-name detection

l4_steps.name: Check Blackout & Peak Period Restrictions
l4_steps.input: Travel date range from group request; current peak calendar in NRM
l4_steps.output: Date eligibility flag; alternate date suggestions if blocked
l4_steps.kpi: Blackout date check completed in <10 minutes; alternate date acceptance rate ≥40%
l4_steps.pain_point: Peak calendars maintained manually in NRM and not automatically synced with marketing/events calendar — agents may quote blocked dates before checking

l4_steps.name: Confirm O&D, Routing & Itinerary
l4_steps.input: Validated group request with confirmed dates and pax count
l4_steps.output: Structured group itinerary record with flight segments and class of service
l4_steps.kpi: Itinerary confirmed and filed in PSS within 2 hours of initial request
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-segment itineraries require manual linking of PNRs across codeshare or interline partners — slow process for international group bookings

l4_steps.name: Query Real-Time O&D Inventory Availability
l4_steps.input: Group itinerary with specific flight segments, dates, and fare class requirement
l4_steps.output: Current availability by booking class for each segment; load factor snapshot
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory query response in <30 seconds; data freshness lag ≤5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM availability data can lag real-time PSS inventory by up to 5 minutes during high-volume periods — group blocks booked on stale data risk overbooking

l4_steps.name: Run Displacement Cost Analysis
l4_steps.input: Requested seat block size; current booking curve; O&D demand forecast from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Displacement cost per seat (value of individual bookings that would be displaced); net revenue impact estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Displacement model accuracy ≥88% vs. actual realised revenue; analysis completed in <15 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Displacement models rely on NRM booking curves that may not fully account for last-minute premium fare uplift potential — groups in high-demand markets routinely under-priced

l4_steps.name: Assess Net Revenue Impact of Group Block
l4_steps.input: Displacement cost analysis; proposed group fare; seat block size
l4_steps.output: Net revenue positive/negative determination; RM recommendation (accept / reject / counter-date)
l4_steps.kpi: Group acceptance rate ≥65% of qualified requests; average group yield ≥85% of displacement cost
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales teams operate under volume targets that incentivise accepting revenue-negative groups — tension between group sales quota and RM yield discipline

l4_steps.name: Calculate Block Fare Using Group Pricing Model
l4_steps.input: Net revenue impact assessment; group discount policy matrix; fare class availability
l4_steps.output: Proposed group fare per pax; total block revenue estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Group fare ≥95% of minimum acceptable yield threshold; pricing turnaround ≤30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Group pricing model does not natively integrate with ATPCO filed fares — group quotes are manual overrides that must be cross-checked against published fare rules to avoid BSP/ARC audit exceptions

l4_steps.name: Validate Fare Against Discount Authority Matrix
l4_steps.input: Proposed group fare; discount authority thresholds by market tier and season
l4_steps.output: Authority level determination: standard approval, RM manager review, or director escalation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of quotes validated against authority matrix before issue; zero out-of-authority quotes issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Discount authority matrices are updated quarterly in spreadsheets and manually imported into NRM — stale thresholds lead to incorrect authority-level routing

l4_steps.name: Generate Formal Group Quote Document
l4_steps.input: Approved group fare; name release schedule; deposit terms; ticketing deadline
l4_steps.output: Formal group quote with fare, seat block, deposit amount, name release dates, and ticketing deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Quote issued within 24 hours of request receipt; quote acceptance rate ≥55%
l4_steps.pain_point: Quote templates are maintained outside PSS in Word/PDF — manual population risks errors in fare amounts, deadlines, and contract terms; no audit trail within the booking system

l4_steps.name: Conduct Sales Negotiation with Group Organiser
l4_steps.input: Formal group quote; organiser counter-proposal (if any); competitive market rates
l4_steps.output: Agreed terms or revised counter-offer; negotiation log entry
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle ≤3 rounds to final agreement; average concession depth ≤5% below initial quote
l4_steps.pain_point: Sales managers lack real-time competitive fare visibility during negotiation — competitors' group rates not available in PRISM, forcing reliance on OAG or manual fare searches

l4_steps.name: Obtain Final RM Approval for Confirmed Terms
l4_steps.input: Final agreed group terms; revenue impact recalculation at agreed fare
l4_steps.output: RM approval stamp; booking authority granted to sales team
l4_steps.kpi: Approval response within 4 business hours; ≤10% of groups requiring director-level escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflow is email-based with no system-enforced audit trail — SOX compliance reviews frequently flag missing RM sign-offs on large group bookings

l4_steps.name: Confirm Group Booking & Collect Deposit
l4_steps.input: RM approval; signed group contract; deposit payment from organiser
l4_steps.output: Confirmed group PNR with seat block held; deposit receipt; booking confirmation to organiser
l4_steps.kpi: Deposit collection rate ≥98% of confirmed bookings; booking confirmation issued within 2 hours of receipt of signed contract
l4_steps.pain_point: Deposit processing via bank transfer requires manual reconciliation against PNR in SAP S/4HANA Finance — 2-3 day lag between payment receipt and booking confirmation causes organiser escalations

l4_steps.name: Create Seat Block in PSS Inventory
l4_steps.input: Confirmed group PNR; approved seat block size; fare class assignment
l4_steps.output: Hard-blocked seat inventory removed from open sale; group booking class activated
l4_steps.kpi: Seat block created within 1 hour of booking confirmation; zero inventory discrepancy vs. PNR
l4_steps.pain_point: Hard blocks in Altéa reduce sellable capacity visible to GDS channels immediately — premature blocking of large groups in advance of name submission increases unsold seat risk

l4_steps.name: Monitor Name Release & Ticketing Deadlines
l4_steps.input: Name release schedule from group contract; automated deadline alerts from PSS
l4_steps.output: Name submission status updates; reminder communications to group organiser
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of names submitted by first release deadline; ticketing deadline breach rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS deadline alerts are not integrated with CRM or email workflows — coordinators manually track deadlines in spreadsheets, leading to missed release dates and last-minute seat block management failures

l4_steps.name: Release Unsold Seats to Open Inventory
l4_steps.input: Final name count at ticketing deadline; remaining unoccupied seats in block
l4_steps.output: Released seats returned to NRM availability; booking class reopened for retail sale
l4_steps.kpi: Unsold seats released ≥72 hours before departure; recaptured revenue from released seats ≥60% of displacement cost on released units
l4_steps.pain_point: Late seat release (within 72 hours of departure) significantly reduces recapture probability — NRM booking curves flatten below T-3 days, leaving released group seats unsold and generating direct revenue loss

l4_steps.name: Process Final Passenger Manifest & Settlement
l4_steps.input: Final confirmed passenger names; actual tickets issued; deposit and balance payment records
l4_steps.output: Closed group PNR; final invoice; payment settled in SAP S/4HANA Finance
l4_steps.kpi: Final settlement completed within 5 business days post-travel; payment reconciliation accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Name changes and no-shows on group bookings trigger penalty fee calculations that must be manually computed and re-invoiced — no automated penalty engine in Altéa for group contracts

l4_steps.name: Calculate Revenue Variance vs. Forecast
l4_steps.input: Actual group revenue from SAP FI; forecast revenue from NRM displacement model; seat block utilisation data
l4_steps.output: Revenue variance report; yield performance vs. plan; group booking contribution analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast vs. actual variance ≤8%; group contribution to total flight revenue ≥12% on applicable routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue data from SAP FI and NRM actuals must be joined manually in Redshift — no automated group P&L dashboard; variance analysis delayed by 2-3 days post-travel

l4_steps.name: Update RM Demand Forecasting Model with Actuals
l4_steps.input: Revenue variance report; actual load factor contribution from group block; group yield data
l4_steps.output: Updated demand coefficients in NRM forecasting model; group segment historical database entry
l4_steps.kpi: Model update completed within 10 business days post-travel; forecast accuracy improvement of ≥0.5% per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM group booking actuals are not automatically tagged separately from retail bookings — group demand is blended into overall O&D forecasts, distorting unconstrained demand estimates and causing systematic over-forecasting on high-group-volume routes

l4_steps.name: Extract PNR data for upsell candidate pool
l4_steps.input: Confirmed bookings within 72-hour pre-departure window
l4_steps.output: Upsell candidate PNR list with cabin class, fare basis, and loyalty tier
l4_steps.kpi: Candidate pool coverage ≥95% of eligible bookings extracted
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PNR data exports can lag up to 15 min during peak schedule periods, narrowing the actionable upsell window for close-in departures

l4_steps.name: Score passengers using willingness-to-pay model
l4_steps.input: PNR list, historical upsell acceptance data, loyalty tier, booking channel
l4_steps.output: WTP score (0–100) and predicted upgrade revenue per passenger
l4_steps.kpi: WTP model accuracy ≥82% (lift vs. random baseline on holdout set)
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM WTP models trained on pre-COVID data can overestimate premium-cabin demand for leisure-heavy route clusters; requires quarterly recalibration

l4_steps.name: Check premium cabin inventory for upgrade availability
l4_steps.input: Flight departure date, cabin class inventory snapshot, current load factor by cabin
l4_steps.output: Available upgrade seats per cabin class per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Premium cabin upgrade seat availability query response time <2 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time seat availability from AltéaRM can conflict with GDS inventory counts when passive segments are not cancelled promptly, creating ghost-availability errors

l4_steps.name: Segment eligible passengers by WTP tier and route
l4_steps.input: WTP scores, available upgrade inventory, route premium demand index
l4_steps.output: Prioritised upsell target list segmented into High / Medium / Low WTP tiers
l4_steps.kpi: High-WTP tier (score ≥70) constitutes ≥30% of total candidate pool
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty programme members in lower fare classes are frequently misclassified as low-WTP due to sparse ancillary purchase history in PROS RM

l4_steps.name: Generate dynamic upgrade offer price per passenger
l4_steps.input: WTP score, fare differential (booked fare vs. premium cabin fare), route load factor
l4_steps.output: Personalised upgrade offer price in local currency
l4_steps.kpi: Average upgrade offer price within 15% of O&D revenue maximisation model output
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM dynamic pricing engine does not natively ingest competitor same-day premium fare data, requiring manual competitive adjustment for price-sensitive O&D markets

l4_steps.name: Apply ATPCO fare floor and ceiling constraints
l4_steps.input: Generated offer price, filed fare rules (Rule 010 / 015), minimum fare differentials
l4_steps.output: Validated upgrade offer price compliant with ATPCO fare rules
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of published upgrade offers compliant with ATPCO Cat 25 negotiated fare rules
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 25 rule interpretation varies across PSS implementations; non-compliant upgrade offers can trigger GDS mis-pricing alerts and require emergency fare recall

l4_steps.name: Bundle ancillary services with upgrade offer
l4_steps.input: Validated upgrade price, ancillary catalogue (lounge, extra baggage, priority boarding)
l4_steps.output: Bundled upsell offer package with itemised ancillary pricing
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attach rate per upgrade offer ≥40% on applicable routes
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway bundle assembly fails when ancillary inventory systems (lounge access, seat maps) return timeout errors, forcing fallback to offer-only pricing with no bundle

l4_steps.name: Publish upgrade offers via web check-in and mobile app
l4_steps.input: Bundled upgrade offer packages, passenger contact details from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Live upsell offer presented in web check-in and airline mobile app
l4_steps.kpi: Offer display latency <3 sec for ≥98% of web check-in sessions
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API retries during high-volume check-in peaks (T-24h departure) cause duplicate offer display or blank offer panels, degrading conversion rate

l4_steps.name: Send targeted upsell email and push notifications
l4_steps.input: Segmented passenger list with personalised offer price, departure T-48h and T-24h triggers
l4_steps.output: Email and push notification delivered with personalised upgrade CTA
l4_steps.kpi: Email open rate ≥28%; push notification click-through rate ≥12%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa CRM notification engine does not suppress duplicate messages when passengers have both web and mobile sessions active, leading to over-communication complaints

l4_steps.name: Display upgrade prompts at airport check-in and kiosk
l4_steps.input: Passenger check-in event, remaining upgrade inventory from AltéaRM
l4_steps.output: Upgrade upsell prompt displayed to agent and self-service kiosk
l4_steps.kpi: Airport upgrade conversion rate ≥8% of prompted passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: SITA AMS kiosk software version lag (often 2+ major releases behind) causes offer display failures on older kiosk hardware at smaller outstations

l4_steps.name: Process upgrade payment via preferred channel
l4_steps.input: Passenger acceptance of upgrade offer, payment card or loyalty points balance
l4_steps.output: Payment transaction record; EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) issued
l4_steps.kpi: Payment processing success rate ≥98.5%; transaction time <10 sec
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa EMD issuance for upgrade payments using loyalty currency (miles + cash) requires manual fare recalculation when the loyalty system API returns stale balance data

l4_steps.name: Reassign seat and update PNR cabin class
l4_steps.input: Authorised payment confirmation, available premium cabin seat map
l4_steps.output: PNR updated with new cabin class, seat assignment, and fare basis code
l4_steps.kpi: PNR update latency <5 sec; zero duplicate seat assignment errors per 10,000 upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent upgrade processing for the same flight can cause seat-map race conditions in Altéa when two agents process the last available premium seat simultaneously

l4_steps.name: Provision premium cabin services and lounge access
l4_steps.input: Updated PNR with premium cabin indicator, lounge contract entitlements
l4_steps.output: Lounge access pass issued; premium meal and amenity kit flagged for catering
l4_steps.kpi: Premium service provisioning lead time ≥45 min before departure for ≥95% of upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Catering uplift amendments post-upgrade are frequently missed when the upgrade is processed inside the catering finality window (T-2h), resulting in insufficient premium meals

l4_steps.name: Send upgrade confirmation and boarding pass to passenger
l4_steps.input: PNR update complete, new boarding pass data, passenger email / mobile
l4_steps.output: Updated boarding pass (mobile and printable) and upgrade confirmation email
l4_steps.kpi: Confirmation delivery within 60 sec of PNR update for ≥99% of upgrades
l4_steps.pain_point: Mobile boarding pass push fails for passengers using third-party wallet apps (non-Apple/Google Wallet) when Altéa PKPass API returns certificate validation errors

l4_steps.name: Aggregate upsell revenue and conversion metrics
l4_steps.input: EMD transaction records, PNR cabin upgrade events, offer impression logs
l4_steps.output: Daily upsell revenue report: impressions, conversions, revenue per upgrade, channel mix
l4_steps.kpi: Upsell revenue per available seat ≥$12 on applicable routes; daily report SLA <6h after day-end
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD revenue attribution in AWS Redshift is delayed by up to 4h due to batch ingestion from Altéa, preventing same-day intra-day optimisation of pricing parameters

l4_steps.name: Compare actuals vs. forecast upsell revenue targets
l4_steps.input: Daily upsell revenue report, budgeted upsell revenue targets by route cluster
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual vs. forecast with root-cause flags (pricing, inventory, channel)
l4_steps.kpi: Upsell revenue forecast accuracy within ±10% of actuals on rolling 7-day basis
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards pulling from AWS Redshift frequently timeout on full-network route-cluster queries, forcing analysts to run ad-hoc SQL instead of using governed reports

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate WTP model and pricing parameters
l4_steps.input: Variance report, offer acceptance/rejection data, competitor fare changes from OAG
l4_steps.output: Updated WTP model weights; revised pricing floor and ceiling parameters in PROS RM
l4_steps.kpi: WTP model recalibration cycle ≤7 days after conversion target miss; post-recalibration lift ≥5%
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM model retraining requires a minimum 90-day historical acceptance dataset; insufficient data on new routes or post-schedule-change periods degrades model quality for at least one quarter

l4_steps.name: Benchmark ancillary revenue vs. peer carriers
l4_steps.input: IATA annual ancillary revenue survey, peer carrier 10-K filings
l4_steps.output: Ancillary benchmark report with gap analysis by product category
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per passenger ≥ $35 (IATA LCC benchmark); report produced annually
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA benchmark data lags 12–18 months; ultra-LCC peers (Spirit, Frontier) distort averages, masking true FSC comparison group and overstating apparent gap

l4_steps.name: Analyse ancillary product mix by revenue category
l4_steps.input: Amadeus Altéa PSS booking records, ancillary sales transaction log
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue decomposition: baggage, seat selection, F&B, insurance, partner referrals
l4_steps.kpi: Top-3 categories contribute ≥70% of total ancillary revenue; data refresh ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS ancillary sales codes are inconsistently applied by airport agents, causing product misclassification in Redshift that distorts category-level P&L

l4_steps.name: Identify new ancillary product opportunities
l4_steps.input: Benchmark gap analysis, passenger demand segmentation, route O&D traffic data
l4_steps.output: Ancillary product roadmap with prioritised opportunities and revenue potential estimates
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum 3 new ancillary product candidates identified per annual review cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D segmentation is designed for seat demand forecasting, not ancillary willingness-to-pay; proxy metrics must substitute for direct demand estimation, reducing confidence

l4_steps.name: Configure ancillary service catalog in PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved ancillary product roadmap, IATA EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) standards
l4_steps.output: Active ancillary service catalog with SSR/OSI codes and EMD settlement rules configured
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of approved ancillaries configured and testable in Altéa within 5 business days of sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD issuance rules require coordination with Finance for BSP settlement alignment; misconfigured EMD types generate revenue accounting errors and trigger BSP dispute processes

l4_steps.name: Set dynamic pricing rules for seats and baggage
l4_steps.input: Historical ancillary demand elasticity data, booking curve by flight, load factor thresholds
l4_steps.output: Dynamic ancillary price ladders by product, route, and days-to-departure bucket
l4_steps.kpi: Elasticity model coverage ≥80% of O&D pairs; yield uplift ≥8% vs. static pricing baseline
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM dynamic ancillary pricing requires separate model training from core RM; data sparsity on thin routes produces unreliable elasticity estimates, defaulting to static fallback pricing

l4_steps.name: Design fare family bundles with ancillary inclusions
l4_steps.input: Fare family structure, ancillary cost-to-serve data, competitive bundle benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Defined fare family tiers (e.g. Basic / Standard / Flex) with ancillary inclusion matrix filed in ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: Bundle attach rate ≥40% of total bookings; bundle margin ≥ à la carte revenue equivalent
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 15 (Sales Restrictions) and Category 31 (Voluntary Changes) rules must be manually aligned with each bundle tier — a mismatch causes GDS display failures and customer refund claims

l4_steps.name: Validate ancillary offers in NDC API test environment
l4_steps.input: Configured ancillary catalog, fare family bundle definitions from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Validated NDC offer schema with ancillaries returned in AirShopping and OrderCreate responses
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of ancillary products surfaced in NDC AirShopping response; NDC API error rate < 0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC 21.3 schema requires ancillaries as ServiceDefinitionID objects; legacy Altéa ancillary codes must be manually mapped — mappings break on Altéa version upgrades requiring re-validation

l4_steps.name: Segment passengers for targeted ancillary offers
l4_steps.input: Loyalty programme profiles, booking history, route type (leisure/business), fare class
l4_steps.output: Passenger micro-segments with propensity scores for each ancillary product category
l4_steps.kpi: Propensity model AUC ≥0.72 for top-3 ancillary categories; segments refreshed ≤24 hours before departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Loyalty data is siloed from GDS bookings — indirect-channel passengers have sparse profiles, reducing propensity model accuracy for ~35% of bookings and defaulting to generic offers

l4_steps.name: Configure real-time ancillary offer engine
l4_steps.input: Passenger propensity scores, dynamic price ladders from PROS RM, inventory availability
l4_steps.output: Personalised ancillary offer sets ranked by revenue contribution per passenger segment
l4_steps.kpi: Offer generation latency < 200ms per PNR; personalised offer conversion rate ≥15%
l4_steps.pain_point: AltéaRM offer engine integration with PROS dynamic ancillary prices requires a custom middleware API; latency spikes during peak booking windows trigger offer timeouts and fallback to static pricing

l4_steps.name: Deploy personalised offers via direct and GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Ranked personalised offer sets, channel capability matrix (NDC Level 3, GDS, direct web)
l4_steps.output: Live ancillary offers served to all booking channels with channel-specific display logic
l4_steps.kpi: NDC channel ancillary attach rate ≥ direct channel within 6 months of launch; GDS ancillary display compliance ≥90% of enabled PCCs
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport and Sabre GDS ancillary merchandising varies by Point of Sale — not all TMC-configured PCC terminals display ancillary offers, suppressing B2B ancillary revenue from managed travel

l4_steps.name: Monitor ancillary attach rates by channel and product
l4_steps.input: Real-time ancillary sales feed from Altéa PSS, channel booking logs, budget targets
l4_steps.output: Live ancillary performance dashboard: attach rate, revenue per pax, channel mix, trend
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue as % of total revenue ≥15%; dashboard data latency < 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS real-time data feed to Tableau relies on an AWS Kinesis stream — stream failures during high-volume booking periods create data gaps that delay corrective pricing actions by 8–12 hours

l4_steps.name: Conduct ancillary price elasticity A/B testing
l4_steps.input: Current ancillary price points, candidate test prices, booking volume thresholds for statistical significance
l4_steps.output: A/B test results with elasticity coefficient and recommended price adjustment per product
l4_steps.kpi: A/B test significance ≥95% confidence interval; minimum 500 transactions per test cell
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM A/B testing for ancillaries is not natively integrated with Altéa PSS booking flows — test cell assignment is enforced via custom middleware, increasing build and maintenance overhead

l4_steps.name: Optimise ancillary offer placement and sequencing
l4_steps.input: A/B test results, channel conversion data, passenger journey stage (search / select / pre-check-in)
l4_steps.output: Updated offer sequencing rules: optimal placement by journey stage and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Incremental ancillary revenue uplift ≥5% per optimisation cycle; cycle cadence monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-booking ancillary upsell in the pre-check-in window is constrained by Altéa PSS notification infrastructure — push notification capability requires a third-party integration not yet fully deployed at most carriers

l4_steps.name: Generate ancillary revenue performance report
l4_steps.input: Monthly ancillary sales data from Redshift, budget targets, prior-period actuals
l4_steps.output: Monthly ancillary revenue report: actuals vs. budget, trend analysis, category and channel breakdown
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered within 3 business days of month-end; forecast accuracy ≤5% variance vs. actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP S/4HANA Finance GL ancillary revenue codes do not always align with Altéa PSS ancillary sales codes — reconciliation requires a manual mapping table maintained by Finance that lags product catalog changes

l4_steps.name: Review portfolio and retire underperforming products
l4_steps.input: Monthly performance report, ancillary product P&L, customer NPS scores by ancillary category
l4_steps.output: Portfolio rationalisation decision per product: retain / reprice / discontinue with timeline
l4_steps.kpi: Products with <0.5% attach rate and negative NPS reviewed quarterly; discontinuation decision within 30 days of review
l4_steps.pain_point: Discontinuing an ancillary product in Altéa PSS requires reversal of EMD settlement rules, ATPCO filing withdrawal, and NDC schema update — cross-system coordination takes 4–6 weeks, extending underperformer lifecycles

l4_steps.name: Extract RM forecast accuracy metrics
l4_steps.input: Scheduled monthly calibration cycle or ad-hoc trigger from revenue variance alert
l4_steps.output: Forecast accuracy report: MAPE by market, booking class, and horizon
l4_steps.kpi: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) ≤15% across all O&D markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM MAPE reporting requires custom extract scripts; no native scheduled accuracy dashboard, increasing analyst effort and risk of metric inconsistency

l4_steps.name: Identify underperforming O&D markets
l4_steps.input: Forecast accuracy report from step 1.1; actuals from AWS Redshift booking data warehouse
l4_steps.output: Ranked list of O&D markets with MAPE >15% or revenue variance >3% vs. plan
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of O&D markets within MAPE threshold within 30 days of calibration cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-market comparison requires manual joins between Amadeus NRM outputs and AWS Redshift actuals; data latency of up to 24 hrs can mask intra-day booking pattern shifts

l4_steps.name: Assess booking curve deviations from expected pickup
l4_steps.input: Ranked O&D market list; historical booking curve profiles from NRM
l4_steps.output: Deviation analysis report flagging systematic early/late booking shifts and class-mix anomalies
l4_steps.kpi: Booking curve R² ≥0.92 across flagged markets; decision to proceed with recalibration if ≥3 markets fail threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: Structural demand shifts post-COVID (early leisure surge, late corporate recovery) have permanently altered booking curves; NRM baseline curves calibrated pre-2023 may no longer reflect current market behaviour

l4_steps.name: Extract historical booking and ticketing data
l4_steps.input: Calibration scope (markets, date range, booking classes) from deviation analysis report
l4_steps.output: Structured training dataset: O&D bookings, fares paid, cancellation rates, no-show rates — 24-month rolling window
l4_steps.kpi: Dataset completeness ≥98% of scheduled departures in scope; extract runtime <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS Redshift query performance degrades on unpartitioned historical tables; full 24-month O&D extracts for 100+ markets can exceed 4-hour SLA without query optimisation

l4_steps.name: Validate input data quality and completeness
l4_steps.input: Raw extract from AWS Redshift; data quality ruleset stored in S3
l4_steps.output: Data quality scorecard with pass/fail per validation rule; cleansed dataset or rejection notice
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality score ≥95% (null rate <2%, duplicate bookings <0.5%, fare outliers <1%)
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Altéa PSS ticket voids and exchanges frequently generate duplicate or partial booking records that inflate cancellation rate inputs to the NRM demand model, distorting recalibration outputs

l4_steps.name: Load competitive fare and capacity benchmarks
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare filing data from ATPCO; OAG Schedule Analyser capacity data for target O&D markets
l4_steps.output: Competitive context dataset: competitor fare ladder, capacity by carrier, schedule frequency
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive data coverage ≥85% of target O&D markets; data freshness within 48 hours of filing date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare data covers only filed public fares; negotiated corporate and NDC-only fares are not visible, creating a systematic blind spot in price elasticity model inputs for corporate-heavy routes

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate demand forecast model coefficients
l4_steps.input: Cleansed 24-month historical dataset; competitive context dataset; current NRM model parameter set
l4_steps.output: Updated demand model coefficients (seasonality indices, trend factors, day-of-week multipliers) staged in NRM test partition
l4_steps.kpi: Post-recalibration MAPE improvement ≥10% vs. baseline on hold-out validation set
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM parameter update interface requires batch file upload in proprietary format; no API-driven calibration workflow, increasing manual error risk and extending cycle time to 3–5 business days

l4_steps.name: Update price elasticity and WTP model curves
l4_steps.input: Updated demand model coefficients; ATPCO competitive fare ladder; passenger segment willingness-to-pay data
l4_steps.output: Revised price elasticity curves and class-specific bid price adjustments per O&D market cluster
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price accuracy: simulated revenue within ±2% of optimal on hold-out markets; elasticity curve R² ≥0.88
l4_steps.pain_point: WTP segmentation in Amadeus NRM is limited to cabin-level; lack of sub-segment granularity (e.g. loyalty tier, corporate account) reduces model precision for high-value O&D pairs with mixed traffic composition

l4_steps.name: Tune overbooking safety factors by route type
l4_steps.input: Updated elasticity curves; historical no-show and cancellation rates by route category (short-haul leisure, long-haul corporate, thin route)
l4_steps.output: Revised overbooking multipliers per route cluster; updated denied boarding risk scores
l4_steps.kpi: Denied boarding rate ≤0.05 per 1,000 passengers; seat spoilage rate ≤2% of available seats
l4_steps.pain_point: Denied boarding compensation exposure under EU261/2004 and DOT rules creates asymmetric financial risk; NRM overbooking model does not natively incorporate regulatory compensation cost as an optimisation constraint

l4_steps.name: Execute shadow-mode simulation on hold-out period
l4_steps.input: Updated NRM parameter set (demand model + elasticity curves + overbooking factors); hold-out historical period (most recent 90 days not used in training)
l4_steps.output: Shadow revenue report: simulated revenue and load factor for each O&D flight in hold-out period
l4_steps.kpi: Shadow simulation runtime ≤8 hours; simulated revenue variance vs. actuals ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM shadow mode does not replicate real-time competitor price reactions; static competitor assumptions in simulation overstate revenue uplift potential by an estimated 0.5–1.0% on competitive routes

l4_steps.name: Evaluate shadow revenue vs. actual revenue
l4_steps.input: Shadow revenue report; actual revenue actuals from AWS Redshift for the same hold-out period
l4_steps.output: Calibration validation dashboard: revenue lift by market cluster, load factor delta, booking class mix comparison
l4_steps.kpi: Simulated revenue uplift ≥1.0% vs. actuals across all market clusters; no individual cluster showing revenue degradation >0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue attribution between calibration changes and external demand factors (events, competitor capacity changes) is not automated; manual attribution analysis adds 1–2 days to the validation cycle

l4_steps.name: Run live A/B test on selected pilot markets
l4_steps.input: Validated calibration parameter set; pilot market selection (10–15 O&D pairs representative of route clusters)
l4_steps.output: A/B test results: revenue per available seat kilometre (RASK) and load factor for treatment vs. control group over 4-week period
l4_steps.kpi: A/B revenue uplift ≥1.5% in pilot markets over 4-week test window at 95% statistical confidence
l4_steps.pain_point: Selecting statistically valid control markets is difficult on thin-route network where few true analogues exist; contamination risk between test and control markets sharing connections distorts A/B results

l4_steps.name: Stage calibrated parameters in UAT environment
l4_steps.input: Approved calibration parameter set from A/B test; UAT deployment checklist
l4_steps.output: UAT environment loaded with new parameters; regression test results confirming no unintended impacts to adjacent processes (pricing, inventory, interline)
l4_steps.kpi: UAT regression test pass rate 100% on critical path; deployment staging completed within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM UAT environment is shared with pricing and ancillary revenue teams; uncoordinated deployments from parallel projects create parameter conflicts that require vendor support engagement to resolve

l4_steps.name: Present calibration results for RM leadership sign-off
l4_steps.input: Calibration validation dashboard; A/B test results; UAT regression summary; estimated annual revenue impact
l4_steps.output: Signed approval record or change request with required amendments; go/no-go decision for production deployment
l4_steps.kpi: Sign-off decision turnaround ≤2 business days; zero production deployments without documented approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Calibration approval process is undocumented in most carriers; absence of a formal change control board for RM model changes means deployments can proceed without revenue risk assessment, creating audit exposure

l4_steps.name: Deploy calibrated parameters to production NRM
l4_steps.input: Signed approval record; staged parameter set from UAT; deployment runbook
l4_steps.output: Production NRM updated with new demand model coefficients, elasticity curves, and overbooking factors; deployment confirmation log
l4_steps.kpi: Production deployment completed within 4-hour maintenance window; zero unplanned system downtime during deployment
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM production parameter updates require a maintenance window coordinated with Amadeus support; last-minute scheduling conflicts with Altéa PSS maintenance windows have caused deployment delays of up to 72 hours

l4_steps.name: Monitor live KPIs post-deployment
l4_steps.input: Live booking data from Amadeus NRM; post-deployment KPI dashboard; baseline metrics from pre-calibration period
l4_steps.output: 30-day post-deployment performance report; rollback recommendation if KPIs deteriorate beyond threshold
l4_steps.kpi: RASK improvement ≥1.0% vs. pre-calibration baseline within 30 days; no market showing load factor decline >2 percentage points
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-deployment monitoring relies on manual Tableau dashboard review; absence of automated anomaly detection means revenue degradation from a miscalibrated market cluster may go undetected for 3–5 days, compounding financial impact

l4_steps.name: Trigger post-departure PSS revenue extract
l4_steps.input: Flight departure confirmation signal from Altéa DCS
l4_steps.output: Raw booking & ticketing record extract per flight
l4_steps.kpi: Extract available within 30 min of block-in; ≥99.5% flight coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa extract latency spikes during high-frequency bank departures, delaying same-day reporting windows

l4_steps.name: Pull ancillary revenue feeds from ancillary platform
l4_steps.input: Completed flight leg; ancillary transaction logs
l4_steps.output: Per-flight ancillary revenue breakdown (bags, seat upgrades, extras)
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue captured per passenger ≥ airline target (e.g. USD 28/pax industry benchmark)
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary items sold via NDC API Gateway may not post to Altéa in real time, creating gaps in same-day reporting

l4_steps.name: Validate booking-to-flown passenger completeness
l4_steps.input: DCS final manifest; booking record extract
l4_steps.output: Reconciled flown passenger count with no-show & offload flags
l4_steps.kpi: Booking-to-manifest match rate ≥99.8% before proceeding
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute irregular operations (IROPs) create orphan booking records that misstate flown revenue

l4_steps.name: Reconcile ticketed revenue vs. flown revenue
l4_steps.input: Altéa ticketing extract; flown passenger manifest
l4_steps.output: Flight-level ticketed vs. flown revenue variance report
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance tolerance ≤1% of flight revenue before exception flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-coupon interline tickets generate partial-revenue allocations that SAP FI cannot auto-match without manual MITA settlement codes

l4_steps.name: Match BSP & interline settlement amounts
l4_steps.input: BSP billing files; interline prorate agreements
l4_steps.output: Settled interline revenue allocation per flight segment
l4_steps.kpi: BSP settlement matched within 48 hours of departure; dispute rate <0.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Prorate disputes with interline partners under MITA/BIMA can take 30–90 days to resolve, overstating interim revenue

l4_steps.name: Validate upgrade & no-show revenue capture
l4_steps.input: No-show records; upgrade transaction log from DCS
l4_steps.output: Confirmed no-show penalty revenue and upgrade delta postings
l4_steps.kpi: No-show revenue leakage <0.2% of total flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Oversold flights with denied boarding (IDB/VDB) generate compensation cost offsets that are frequently mis-posted against revenue rather than cost accounts

l4_steps.name: Aggregate O&D revenue by fare class & cabin
l4_steps.input: Reconciled flight revenue records; booking class mapping
l4_steps.output: O&D revenue matrix by fare class, cabin, and market pair
l4_steps.kpi: O&D attribution completeness ≥98% of total flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point carriers with connecting itineraries lack native O&D proration logic in Altéa; NRM must apply estimated prorate splits

l4_steps.name: Calculate RASM, PRASM, and load factor vs. forecast
l4_steps.input: O&D revenue matrix; capacity data from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Flight-level RASM, PRASM, load factor actuals vs. forecast delta
l4_steps.kpi: RASM actuals within ±3% of pre-departure NRM forecast; load factor ≥83%
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM forecast baseline uses O&D demand curves that require 12+ months of history — new routes show high forecast error in first two seasons

l4_steps.name: Identify revenue spoilage and dilution events
l4_steps.input: RASM/PRASM variance report; fare class booking curve
l4_steps.output: Spoilage flag (unsold high-yield seats) or dilution flag (over-discounted load)
l4_steps.kpi: Spoilage rate ≤4% of available seats on constrained routes; dilution rate ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated RM bid-price controls in NRM cannot retroactively explain spoilage caused by schedule irregularities or competitor fare wars without manual analyst annotation

l4_steps.name: Generate flight-level post-departure P&L report
l4_steps.input: Reconciled revenue; ancillary revenue; prorate settlements
l4_steps.output: Flight-level revenue P&L report with actuals vs. plan variance
l4_steps.kpi: Report generation within 4 hours of block-in for priority routes
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP FI cost allocations for fuel and crew are posted at cost-centre level, not flight level — flight P&L requires manual allocation keys that reduce accuracy

l4_steps.name: Publish variance dashboard for RM and Finance
l4_steps.input: Flight P&L report; RASM/PRASM variance data
l4_steps.output: Interactive revenue variance dashboard published to BI portal
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency ≤1 hour from report generation; stakeholder access rate ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau data extracts from SAP and NRM use separate ETL schedules, causing dashboard columns to reflect mixed reporting periods during refresh windows

l4_steps.name: Route significant variances to Revenue Director
l4_steps.input: Variance dashboard; threshold breach flags
l4_steps.output: Escalation notification with variance summary and root-cause annotation
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation triggered within 2 hours for variances ≥5% of planned flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated escalation workflow in SAP FI — analysts rely on manual email alerts, creating inconsistent escalation timing across regions

l4_steps.name: Distribute approved reports to RM and Finance teams
l4_steps.input: Approved flight-level revenue reports
l4_steps.output: Published report package to S3 data lake for downstream consumption
l4_steps.kpi: Distribution to all stakeholders within 6 hours of block-in for same-day flights
l4_steps.pain_point: S3 IAM access policies differ between Revenue Management and Finance teams, requiring duplicate report versions with different data masking levels

l4_steps.name: Feed actuals into NRM for forecast comparison
l4_steps.input: Finalised flight revenue actuals from S3 data lake
l4_steps.output: Actuals posted to NRM historical performance database
l4_steps.kpi: Actuals feed completed within 24 hours of departure; data completeness ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM actuals ingestion pipeline requires structured SSIM-aligned flight keys — IROPs-affected flights with revised flight numbers create orphan actuals that must be manually re-keyed

l4_steps.name: Assess forecast model error vs. recalibration threshold
l4_steps.input: Actuals vs. NRM forecast delta; rolling MAPE statistics
l4_steps.output: Recalibration decision flag: proceed or trigger model update
l4_steps.kpi: MAPE ≤8% on 30-day rolling basis; trigger recalibration if MAPE >10% for 5 consecutive days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM model recalibration jobs require 4–6 hour processing windows that temporarily freeze bid-price updates, creating yield management blind spots during peak booking periods

l4_steps.name: Trigger NRM demand model recalibration job
l4_steps.input: Recalibration trigger flag; accumulated actuals dataset
l4_steps.output: Updated NRM demand model parameters; recalibration completion log
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration job completes within 6-hour maintenance window; model improvement verified by ≥1% MAPE reduction
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM recalibration requires coordination with Amadeus managed services SLA (8-hour response window), delaying urgent corrections during high-yield periods such as holiday blocks

l4_steps.name: Archive finalised flight revenue record to data lake
l4_steps.input: Validated & reconciled flight revenue package
l4_steps.output: Immutable flight revenue archive record in S3 with audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of departed flights archived within 24 hours; retention compliance per IATA Resolution 787 (7-year minimum)
l4_steps.pain_point: S3 lifecycle policies must balance cost (Glacier transition) against ad-hoc audit retrieval SLAs — retrieval from Glacier takes 3–5 hours, conflicting with same-day audit requests

l4_steps.name: Ingest ATPCO competitor fare feed
l4_steps.input: Scheduled ATPCO Fare Update (FU) and Fare Distribution (FD) transmissions
l4_steps.output: Structured fare change dataset by O&D, booking class, and carrier
l4_steps.kpi: Feed latency ≤30 min from ATPCO publication; 100% O&D coverage on monitored routes
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch update cycles (typically 3× daily) create lag vs. real-time OTA price changes; competitor fares visible on GDS before ATPCO reflects them

l4_steps.name: Scrape OTA & metasearch displayed fares
l4_steps.input: Automated scrape schedule for key O&D markets; ATPCO baseline fare dataset
l4_steps.output: Displayed-price dataset including taxes, carrier surcharges, and ancillary bundling
l4_steps.kpi: Scrape coverage ≥95% of tier-1 competitive routes; data freshness ≤60 min
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC-sourced fares from competitors bypass ATPCO and are invisible to traditional monitoring tools; requires separate NDC channel scraping capability not standard in OAG

l4_steps.name: Detect and flag material fare changes
l4_steps.input: Combined ATPCO and OTA fare datasets; pre-configured alert thresholds by market tier
l4_steps.output: Prioritised alert queue: fare changes ≥10% on tier-1 routes, ≥15% on tier-2
l4_steps.kpi: False-positive alert rate ≤5%; mean time to analyst notification ≤15 min from ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold calibration is static; promotional fare launches by LCCs in thin markets trigger high false-positive volumes that overwhelm analyst queues

l4_steps.name: Analyse competitor O&D fare positioning
l4_steps.input: Flagged fare alert; historical competitor fare trend data from data lake
l4_steps.output: Competitive positioning report: own fare vs. competitor by cabin, booking class, and departure window
l4_steps.kpi: Analysis turnaround ≤2 hr for tier-1 alerts; ≤8 hr for tier-2
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM lacks a native competitor fare visualisation layer; analysts context-switch between NRM and Tableau dashboards, increasing error risk and analysis time

l4_steps.name: Assess impact on O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Competitive positioning report; current NRM demand forecast and booking curve
l4_steps.output: Demand sensitivity estimate: projected booking-curve shift under current and revised fare scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy within ±5% MAPE post-response on monitored O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM demand models have limited sensitivity to intraday competitor fare moves on ultra-short booking windows (<72 hr); last-minute price wars require manual forecast override

l4_steps.name: Classify response urgency and route tier
l4_steps.input: Demand impact estimate; route revenue contribution ranking; days-to-departure
l4_steps.output: Urgency classification: Immediate (≤4 hr), Same-day, Scheduled review
l4_steps.kpi: Immediate-class alerts actioned within 4 hr in ≥90% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue contribution rankings in Tableau are refreshed nightly; intraday revenue shifts on high-value routes are not reflected in urgency scoring during the same business day

l4_steps.name: Evaluate inventory availability and load factor
l4_steps.input: Urgency classification; current fare bucket availability by flight and departure date
l4_steps.output: Inventory health snapshot: available seats by fare bucket, current load factor, revenue-per-available-seat-mile (RASM)
l4_steps.kpi: Load factor target ≥83% on relevant departure; RASM ≥ route budget
l4_steps.pain_point: Opening low fare buckets to match competitor on near-full flights cannibalises higher-yield bookings already in the pipe; NRM bid-price guardrails may not prevent this on short notice

l4_steps.name: Model fare response scenarios in NRM
l4_steps.input: Inventory health snapshot; competitor fare structure; elasticity parameters from historical data
l4_steps.output: 3–5 response scenario outputs: match, undercut, hold, selective open/close by booking window
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario modelling completed within 1 hr of escalation; ≥3 scenarios produced per alert
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM scenario engine requires clean elasticity inputs; thin-route O&Ds with <12 months of data produce unreliable price-sensitivity curves, forcing analyst judgment over model output

l4_steps.name: Review and approve response strategy
l4_steps.input: Modelled response scenarios; route revenue budget; commercial policy guardrails
l4_steps.output: Approved response strategy with rationale, fare targets, booking-class assignments, and validity period
l4_steps.kpi: Approval cycle ≤2 hr for immediate-class alerts; sign-off documented in NRM audit trail
l4_steps.pain_point: Commercial policy guardrails (minimum fare floors, allotment restrictions for corporate accounts) are maintained separately in ATPCO and not surfaced within NRM approval workflow, risking policy violations

l4_steps.name: File revised fares via ATPCO submissions
l4_steps.input: Approved response strategy; current fare tariff record for affected O&Ds
l4_steps.output: ATPCO fare submission batch: new or amended fare basis codes, amounts, and effective dates
l4_steps.kpi: ATPCO filing completeness 100% for approved O&Ds; filing-to-effective lag ≤3 hr (next ATPCO update cycle)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO update cycles constrain real-time parity; competitors using direct NDC filing can respond 2–3 hr faster, creating a temporary price-visibility disadvantage in GDS

l4_steps.name: Configure fare rules, restrictions, and RBDs
l4_steps.input: Approved response strategy; existing rule categories (Cat 2, 3, 5, 14, 15, 35)
l4_steps.output: Updated fare rules: advance purchase, minimum stay, combinability, blackout dates, refund conditions
l4_steps.kpi: Zero ATPCO rule validation errors on submission; rules audit-compliant with IATA Resolution 024
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex combinability rules (Cat 10) for interline itineraries require manual review against partner agreements; errors result in GDS pricing rejections and customer-visible mispricing

l4_steps.name: Verify fare distribution across GDS channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO effective fare update notification; test O&D city pairs
l4_steps.output: GDS distribution verification report: fare visible and correctly priced in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Fare parity confirmed across ≥3 GDS within 60 min of ATPCO effective time; zero pricing discrepancies on spot-check O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport GDS cache refresh lags Sabre by up to 45 min post-ATPCO update; customers on Travelport-connected TMCs see stale competitor fares, causing booking leakage during the gap

l4_steps.name: Activate fares in PSS inventory and NDC
l4_steps.input: GDS verification sign-off; NDC API Gateway configuration
l4_steps.output: Live fare availability confirmed in Altéa inventory and NDC API offer response
l4_steps.kpi: NDC offer response includes new fare within 30 min of Altéa activation; booking class availability aligned with approved strategy
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS inventory bucket mapping to ATPCO booking class codes requires manual reconciliation when new fare basis codes are introduced; mapping errors cause sell-up failures

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking velocity post-response
l4_steps.input: Live booking stream from Altéa PSS; pre-response booking curve baseline
l4_steps.output: Booking velocity dashboard: actual vs. forecast bookings by fare bucket, hourly cadence for 24 hr post-activation
l4_steps.kpi: Booking pace recovery to baseline curve within 24 hr on ≥80% of actioned O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM booking-curve comparison uses historical same-departure-day data that may not account for week-of-year seasonality shifts; recovery signals can be misread on holidays or event periods

l4_steps.name: Assess revenue impact against route budget
l4_steps.input: 48-hr post-response booking and revenue data from Redshift data lake; route budget targets
l4_steps.output: Revenue impact report: incremental revenue vs. estimated dilution cost; net yield delta
l4_steps.kpi: Net yield delta ≥0% vs. pre-response baseline within 48 hr; RASM maintained ≥ route budget
l4_steps.pain_point: Dilution cost from opening low fare buckets is not automatically calculated in NRM; analysts must manually query Redshift to isolate response-attributable revenue changes from organic demand shifts

l4_steps.name: Conduct post-action review and update playbook
l4_steps.input: Revenue impact report; response timeline audit trail from ATPCO and NRM
l4_steps.output: Post-action review record: strategy effectiveness score, lessons learned, and updated competitive response playbook entry
l4_steps.kpi: Post-action review completed within 5 business days for tier-1 alerts; playbook updated within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitive response playbooks are maintained as unstructured documents outside RM systems; institutional knowledge of effective response patterns is lost when analysts rotate, and playbook entries are rarely linked to outcome data

l4_steps.name: Receive & log corporate RFP in CRM
l4_steps.input: RFP submission from corporate buyer or TMC (email / GBTA RFP tool)
l4_steps.output: Qualified lead record with travel volume, routes, and preferred travel dates
l4_steps.kpi: RFP response time ≤3 business days; 100% RFPs logged in Salesforce within 24 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: RFPs arrive via multiple untracked channels (email, broker portals, GBTA RFP Hub); manual logging causes duplicates and missed responses

l4_steps.name: Assess historical travel volume & route overlap
l4_steps.input: Salesforce CRM opportunity record; prior booking history if existing account
l4_steps.output: Volume assessment report: annual passenger yield, top 10 routes, seasonality profile
l4_steps.kpi: Volume data pull completed within 4 hours of RFP receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: New corporate accounts have no booking history; reliance on self-reported volume figures that may be overstated by 20–40% to secure deeper discounts

l4_steps.name: Qualify account against minimum volume threshold
l4_steps.input: Volume assessment report from step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Qualification decision: proceed to negotiation or decline/redirect to SME program
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum qualifying threshold: 200 segments/year or $150K annual spend
l4_steps.pain_point: Sub-threshold accounts consuming senior sales capacity; no automated triage in Salesforce to enforce volume floors consistently across regions

l4_steps.name: Model discount tiers against NRM inventory
l4_steps.input: Qualified account route/volume profile; current O&D bid-price curves from Amadeus NRM
l4_steps.output: Discount tier matrix (3–5 tiers) with revenue impact per tier at projected volume
l4_steps.kpi: Modelled revenue dilution <3% vs. unconstrained mix; analysis completed within 2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM bid-price data is point-in-time; discount tiers fixed at contract signing may become revenue-dilutive during high-demand periods without dynamic override capability

l4_steps.name: Benchmark proposed rates vs. ATPCO published fares
l4_steps.input: Discount tier matrix from step 2.1; ATPCO fare tariff for relevant O&D markets
l4_steps.output: Competitive rate benchmark showing proposed negotiated fare vs. lowest published fare and competitor filing
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiated rate within 5–15% below lowest unrestricted published fare for target markets
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO tariff data has a 48-hour publication lag; competitor last-minute fare reductions not captured, causing negotiated rates to inadvertently undercut market

l4_steps.name: Validate revenue impact against load factor targets
l4_steps.input: Benchmark report from step 2.2; route load factor targets from network plan
l4_steps.output: Revenue impact sign-off: approved discount tier set with floor rates per O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Approved rates must preserve projected route load factor ≥83% and RASK within 2% of unconstrained forecast
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM does not natively model corporate volume displacement of leisure inventory; manual override required to test scenarios on constrained peak departures

l4_steps.name: Draft contract terms and route coverage schedule
l4_steps.input: Approved discount tier set; legal contract template; blackout date calendar
l4_steps.output: Draft corporate travel agreement: discount schedule, route coverage, blackout dates, minimum commitment, audit rights
l4_steps.kpi: Contract draft delivered to corporate buyer within 5 business days of rate approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Contract templates not version-controlled in Salesforce; legal redlines handled via email, creating misalignment between signed terms and fare filing parameters in ATPCO

l4_steps.name: File private negotiated fares in ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Signed corporate travel agreement; approved discount tier set
l4_steps.output: Private fare codes filed in ATPCO with account-specific fare basis codes, routing rules, and booking class restrictions
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing completed within 24 hours of contract execution; zero filing errors on first submission
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO private fare filing requires precise fare basis code structuring; errors in Rule 15 (Sales Restrictions) or Rule 35 (Negotiated Fares) cause incorrect TMC access or public leakage of private rates

l4_steps.name: Configure Sabre PRISM access for TMC booking
l4_steps.input: ATPCO private fare codes; TMC agency IATA codes from contract
l4_steps.output: Sabre PRISM corporate account record with pseudo-city codes, negotiated fare credentials, and booking class availability
l4_steps.kpi: PRISM configuration active and tested within 48 hours of ATPCO filing; TMC confirmation of successful test booking
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM configuration requires manual pseudo-city mapping for each TMC location; large corporates with 50+ TMC offices create significant setup overhead with no bulk-load API

l4_steps.name: Set up NDC private offer for NDC-enabled corporates
l4_steps.input: Corporate account ID; approved discount tier set; NDC-capable TMC flag from contract
l4_steps.output: NDC private offer configured with corporate token, ancillary bundle inclusions, and fare eligibility rules
l4_steps.kpi: NDC offer live within 72 hours for NDC-enabled accounts; ancillary attach rate target ≥35% on NDC-booked itineraries
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC adoption among corporate TMCs remains below 30%; ATPCO and NDC offer parameters must be maintained in parallel, creating dual-maintenance risk and version drift between channels

l4_steps.name: Validate fare accessibility across all booked channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO private fares; Sabre PRISM config; NDC offer (if applicable)
l4_steps.output: Channel validation report confirming fare availability in Amadeus GDS, Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and NDC
l4_steps.kpi: 100% fare accessibility in contracted channels before contract activation date; zero public display of private fares
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare display inconsistencies across Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport due to differing cache refresh cycles (up to 4-hour lag); corporate bookers may see incorrect rates during the window

l4_steps.name: Track monthly booking volume vs. contracted commitment
l4_steps.input: GDS booking data feed; Amadeus Altéa PSS ticketing records; contract commitment thresholds
l4_steps.output: Monthly corporate account scorecard: booked segments, revenue, yield vs. target, commitment attainment %
l4_steps.kpi: Volume commitment attainment reported by 5th business day of following month; data completeness ≥99% across all channels
l4_steps.pain_point: Booking data from NDC channel not consistently flowing into Redshift reconciliation pipeline; NDC-booked corporate trips may be excluded from volume commitment tracking, understating attainment

l4_steps.name: Generate quarterly corporate performance report
l4_steps.input: Monthly scorecard data from AWS Redshift; account-level revenue and yield benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Quarterly business review (QBR) deck: volume trend, route penetration, yield analysis, missed booking analysis
l4_steps.kpi: QBR delivered to corporate buyer within 15 business days of quarter close; 100% of tier-1 accounts receive QBR
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual extraction from Redshift to Tableau for QBR preparation takes 2–3 days per account; no automated QBR generation for the long tail of mid-market accounts (typically 200+ accounts per analyst)

l4_steps.name: Assess volume commitment attainment threshold
l4_steps.input: Quarterly performance report; contract minimum commitment clause
l4_steps.output: Attainment decision: compliant (≥85%), at-risk (70–84%), or non-compliant (<70%) classification
l4_steps.kpi: ≥85% of tier-1 accounts maintaining contracted commitment; non-compliant accounts actioned within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Contracts with volume commitment clauses rarely include enforceable penalties; non-compliant accounts may retain full discount tier without commercial consequence, eroding revenue quality

l4_steps.name: Trigger rate adjustment or incentive review
l4_steps.input: Non-compliant or at-risk account classification; current route load factor data from NRM
l4_steps.output: Rate adjustment proposal: discount tier reduction, incentive bonus offer, or remediation plan submitted to corporate buyer
l4_steps.kpi: Rate adjustment applied within 30 days of non-compliance trigger; targeted return to ≥85% commitment attainment within 1 quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM does not have a corporate account module; rate adjustment modelling must be done manually outside the system, with no automated link between attainment tracking in Salesforce and NRM inventory controls

l4_steps.name: Initiate contract renewal 90 days before expiry
l4_steps.input: Contract expiry date alert from Salesforce; account performance history
l4_steps.output: Renewal opportunity record opened in Salesforce; renewal kick-off meeting scheduled with corporate buyer
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active contracts have renewal opportunity opened ≥90 days before expiry; zero lapsed contracts due to missed renewal trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce contract expiry alerts not configured for all accounts due to inconsistent contract record hygiene; lapsed contracts default to published fares, triggering reactive re-negotiation with weakened leverage

l4_steps.name: Re-model renewal rates using updated RM forecast
l4_steps.input: Updated O&D demand forecast from NRM; account performance history; competitor rate intelligence from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Renewal rate proposal with updated discount tiers, revised route coverage, and projected revenue impact
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal rates modelled to deliver ≥2% RASK improvement vs. expiring contract; analysis completed 60 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: 12-month forward NRM forecasts used for renewal modelling have ±8% accuracy on thin routes; locking renewal rates to inaccurate forecasts on marginal routes risks over-discounting into peak periods

l4_steps.name: Approve renewal, renegotiate, or exit account
l4_steps.input: Renewal rate proposal; account strategic value score; competitive RFP comparison
l4_steps.output: Renewal decision: signed contract renewal, counter-proposal issued, or account exit with fare code deactivation notice
l4_steps.kpi: Tier-1 account renewal rate ≥90%; tier-2 renewal rate ≥75%; exit decision documented in Salesforce within 5 business days of final negotiation
l4_steps.pain_point: No systematic strategic value scoring model in Salesforce; renewal decisions on borderline accounts rely on relationship judgment rather than data, leading to inconsistent discount policy across the portfolio

l4_steps.name: Load authorized capacity & fleet config
l4_steps.input: Fleet assignment output, aircraft subtype capacity tables
l4_steps.output: Authorized capacity record per flight-date with cabin split
l4_steps.kpi: Capacity load accuracy 100% before sales open
l4_steps.pain_point: Late fleet swaps from network planning trigger manual capacity corrections in AltéaRM; no automated re-sync with SkyMAX fleet assignment module

l4_steps.name: Initialize fare class booking buckets
l4_steps.input: ATPCO fare class definitions, historical booking curve by O&D
l4_steps.output: Booking class hierarchy (Y, B, M, H, Q, K, L, U, T, X) with initial seat counts
l4_steps.kpi: All booking classes live ≥14 days before departure; 0 missing bucket errors at booking open
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare class proliferation (20+ classes on competitive routes) increases bucket management complexity; AltéaRM UI does not support bulk bucket edits

l4_steps.name: Apply overbooking factors by flight segment
l4_steps.input: Historical no-show rates, cancellation curves, load factor targets
l4_steps.output: Authorized booking limit (ABL) per flight exceeding physical capacity
l4_steps.kpi: Target involuntary denied boarding rate ≤0.05 per 10,000 passengers
l4_steps.pain_point: No-show model degrades on routes with recent schedule changes or post-event demand spikes; manual recalibration required in AltéaRM — no auto-retraining trigger

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time booking pace vs forecast
l4_steps.input: Live booking transactions from Amadeus Altéa PSS, SkyCAST demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Booking pace index (actual/forecast ratio) per flight per class
l4_steps.kpi: Pace variance alert triggered within 15 minutes of threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: AltéaRM polling interval from Altéa PSS is near-real-time but not event-driven; sudden group bookings or flash sales can spike pace index before alert fires

l4_steps.name: Evaluate booking pace deviation threshold
l4_steps.input: Booking pace index, departure date proximity, current load factor
l4_steps.output: Availability action flag: accelerated close, hold, or open lower class
l4_steps.kpi: System recommendation generated within 5 minutes of threshold breach; analyst review SLA ≤30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold calibration is static per route cluster — unusual demand patterns (e.g. redirected traffic, airline irregular operations) generate false positive alerts requiring analyst intervention

l4_steps.name: Flag flight for priority availability review
l4_steps.input: Availability action flag from automated pace evaluation
l4_steps.output: Flight placed in analyst work queue with recommended action and revenue impact estimate
l4_steps.kpi: ≥90% of flagged flights actioned within analyst SLA; <5% false-positive escalation rate
l4_steps.pain_point: High-frequency flagging on congested departure banks (e.g. Monday AM banks) overwhelms analyst queues; PROS RM AI prioritisation not yet integrated at this carrier

l4_steps.name: Generate availability adjustment recommendation
l4_steps.input: Current bucket availability, forecast demand, competitive fare filings from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Recommended bucket open/close action with projected revenue impact delta
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue uplift from accepted recommendations ≥1.5% per adjusted flight vs control group
l4_steps.pain_point: AltéaRM recommendations do not factor competitor real-time availability in Sabre/Travelport GDS; ATPCO fare data lags competitor filing by up to 2 hours

l4_steps.name: Validate recommendation against RM policy bounds
l4_steps.input: System recommendation, RM policy rules (minimum bucket sizes, blackout dates, alliance blocks)
l4_steps.output: Approved or overridden availability action
l4_steps.kpi: Policy override rate ≤8% of system recommendations; override reason coded for feedback loop
l4_steps.pain_point: RM policy rules are maintained in AltéaRM configuration tables — change request lead time is 5 business days, creating misalignment during rapid competitive responses

l4_steps.name: Apply manual override with documented reason
l4_steps.input: Out-of-bounds recommendation, analyst market intelligence, competitive intelligence feed
l4_steps.output: Manually adjusted bucket availability with override reason code logged
l4_steps.kpi: Manual override revenue outcome tracked: ≥60% of overrides must outperform system recommendation at T+7 days post-departure
l4_steps.pain_point: Override audit trail in AltéaRM is flight-level only — no automatic post-departure outcome attribution; manual tracking in spreadsheets introduces error

l4_steps.name: Broadcast availability updates to all channels
l4_steps.input: Approved bucket availability changes from AltéaRM
l4_steps.output: Updated availability published to Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, Amadeus GDS, and NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.kpi: Availability propagation to all GDS channels within 60 seconds of AltéaRM commit; NDC API latency ≤5 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre and Travelport GDS availability caching can delay display of closed classes by up to 90 seconds — undercuts intended revenue protection window on high-demand flights

l4_steps.name: Receive and assess group booking request
l4_steps.input: Group booking request (pax count, travel date, origin/destination, fare requirements)
l4_steps.output: Group inventory assessment report: available seats, impact on individual yield
l4_steps.kpi: Group quote turnaround ≤4 hours for ≤50 pax; ≤24 hours for >50 pax
l4_steps.pain_point: Group bookings bypass normal availability controls in Altéa PSS — large groups (>30 pax) can displace higher-yield individual bookings if allotment limits not enforced in real time

l4_steps.name: Validate group request against allotment policy
l4_steps.input: Group assessment report, flight allotment policy (max % of capacity per group), current availability
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected group allotment decision with conditional availability hold
