l4_steps.kpi: Group allotment approval rate within policy: ≥95% handled without senior escalation; group revenue mix target ≤20% of total flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: AltéaRM group allotment module requires manual entry of allotment limits per flight — no automated inheritance from network-level group policy, causing inconsistency across the system

l4_steps.name: Confirm group block and adjust net inventory
l4_steps.input: Approved group allotment decision, group fare agreement
l4_steps.output: Group PNR block confirmed; individual booking class availability reduced by block size
l4_steps.kpi: Group block confirmation rate ≥85% within quoted hold period; no-show rate on confirmed groups ≤12%
l4_steps.pain_point: Group blocks held without deposit reduce effective inventory for individual revenue-maximising bookings — Altéa PSS release rules must be manually configured per group record

l4_steps.name: Conduct T-72h pre-departure inventory review
l4_steps.input: Current booking count, remaining availability, forecast final load factor, waitlist count
l4_steps.output: Pre-departure availability strategy: sell-up, open low classes, or hold current position
l4_steps.kpi: Final load factor target ≥83%; revenue per available seat kilometre (RASK) vs budget reviewed at T-72h
l4_steps.pain_point: T-72h review is manual and sequential per flight — on banks of 80+ departures, analyst capacity limits force triage; lower-revenue routes reviewed last or skipped entirely

l4_steps.name: Evaluate unsold inventory against threshold
l4_steps.input: Current load factor, departure proximity, unsold seat count, waitlist queue depth
l4_steps.output: Decision flag: open lower fare classes or maintain current availability strategy
l4_steps.kpi: Unsold seat recovery via last-minute availability opening: target ≥65% of exposed seats sold at ≥breakeven yield
l4_steps.pain_point: Static threshold rules for opening lower classes do not account for connecting passenger itinerary value — opening cheap last-minute classes may dilute O&D revenue on competitive routes

l4_steps.name: Open lower fare classes and clear waitlist
l4_steps.input: Availability action flag, waitlist passenger queue from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Lower classes opened in AltéaRM; waitlist passengers auto-confirmed via Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Waitlist clearance rate ≥90% within 2 hours of class opening; confirmed waitlist pax CSAT ≥4.2/5
l4_steps.pain_point: Waitlist auto-confirmation in Altéa PSS sends immediate ticketing deadline — passengers who do not respond within 2 hours forfeit the seat, requiring manual re-processing by reservations agents

l4_steps.name: Freeze availability at check-in cutoff
l4_steps.input: Departure time, check-in cutoff rule (route-specific: 45–90 min before departure)
l4_steps.output: Availability closed to all booking channels; final booked load factor locked for departure
l4_steps.kpi: Check-in cutoff applied accurately on 100% of departures; overbooking resolution (VDB/IDB) initiated within 30 minutes of cutoff if overbooked
l4_steps.pain_point: Irregular operations (IROPS) delay departures after availability freeze — stranded passengers rebooked on alternate flights consume inventory already frozen for those flights, requiring emergency availability unlocks in Altéa PSS

l4_steps.name: Scan bookings approaching ticketing time limit
l4_steps.input: All PNRs with ticketing time limits (TTL) set by fare rules or agent override
l4_steps.output: List of PNRs within 2-hour TTL warning threshold
l4_steps.kpi: TTL breach rate ≤0.5% of daily ticketed bookings
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa queue refresh latency can delay TTL alerts by 15–30 min, causing bookings to lapse before analysts act

l4_steps.name: Flag PNRs with expired ticketing time limits
l4_steps.input: TTL warning list from step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Exception queue of TTL-breached PNRs routed to Queue 8
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of expired TTL PNRs queued within 5 min of breach
l4_steps.pain_point: Agents in GDS (Sabre/Travelport) may rebook on new PNR to circumvent TTL, requiring cross-GDS deduplication

l4_steps.name: Validate fare basis code against booked RBD
l4_steps.input: Ticketed fare basis code and booked reservation booking designator (RBD) from PSS
l4_steps.output: Fare validity confirmation or mismatch alert
l4_steps.kpi: Fare-RBD mismatch detection rate ≥99% within 24 hrs of ticketing
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 25 private fare rules are not always loaded in GDS displays, causing agents to ticket on incorrect public fare basis

l4_steps.name: Verify fare construction rules and routing compliance
l4_steps.input: Ticketed itinerary, fare basis, and routing map from ATPCO
l4_steps.output: Routing compliance flag (pass / fail) attached to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Routing violation cases referred to recovery ≤0.3% of international tickets
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex Round-the-World or multi-carrier journeys with published interline fares lack automated combinability validation in NRM

l4_steps.name: Investigate and classify integrity exception
l4_steps.input: Exception queue from steps 1.2 and 1.3
l4_steps.output: Exception classification: TTL breach / fare mismatch / routing violation
l4_steps.kpi: Mean time to classify exception ≤30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: High exception queue volume during schedule irregularity events (IRROP) overwhelms 2-analyst teams, risking revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Decide to extend TTL or cancel non-compliant booking
l4_steps.input: Classified exception, agent history, and booking value
l4_steps.output: Decision: TTL extension granted or PNR cancelled
l4_steps.kpi: TTL extension approval rate ≤15% of breached PNRs (excess indicates agent abuse)
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated scoring model to rank extension worthiness — decisions rely on analyst judgement, creating inconsistency across markets

l4_steps.name: Cancel non-ticketed PNRs and release inventory
l4_steps.input: Approved cancellation list from step 2.2
l4_steps.output: Cancelled PNRs; seat inventory returned to Amadeus NRM availability
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory released within 15 min of cancellation decision; recapture rate ≥60% on high-demand flights
l4_steps.pain_point: Seat release timing relative to NRM availability update cycle can delay recapture on flights within 72 hrs of departure

l4_steps.name: Process ticket void within 24-hour BSP window
l4_steps.input: Void request from agent or internal ticketing team within same-day BSP reporting period
l4_steps.output: Void transaction recorded in BSP/ARC; ticket value reversed
l4_steps.kpi: Same-day void processing rate ≥98%; zero late voids submitted outside BSP cut-off
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP cut-off times vary by country (midnight local vs. UTC), causing agents to miss the void window on international sales

l4_steps.name: Assess refund eligibility against fare rules
l4_steps.input: Refund request, original ticket details, and ATPCO Cat 16/33 fare rules
l4_steps.output: Refund eligibility decision: full / partial / non-refundable
l4_steps.kpi: Fare rule compliance on refund decisions ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 31 ticket changes rules for bundled ancillaries (seats, bags) are not consistently interpreted by Altéa auto-refund module

l4_steps.name: Process involuntary refund for schedule change or IRROP
l4_steps.input: Schedule change notification; passenger refund waiver code from Operations
l4_steps.output: Full involuntary refund issued; refund record filed with BSP/ARC
l4_steps.kpi: Involuntary refund processing ≤72 hrs of passenger request; DOT 24-hr refund rule compliance = 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT 24-hour refund rule (14 CFR 259.5) requires next-business-day processing; Altéa batch refund jobs occasionally miss the SLA during high-IRROP periods

l4_steps.name: Reissue ticket for voluntary fare exchange
l4_steps.input: Passenger change request; original ticket, new itinerary, and applicable fare difference
l4_steps.output: Reissued ticket with correct fare differential and penalty collected
l4_steps.kpi: Exchange error rate ≤0.8% of reissued tickets; penalty collection accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Complex multi-carrier reissues on interline itineraries require manual fare recalculation — Altéa auto-reissue module not triggered for codeshare segments

l4_steps.name: Review incoming Agency Debit Memos from GDS
l4_steps.input: ADM notices generated by airline for agency ticketing errors (waiver abuse, fare mismatch, commission errors)
l4_steps.output: ADM register with validity assessment for each memo
l4_steps.kpi: ADM review completion within 15 days of issuance (IATA resolution deadline); ADM recovery rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA ADM resolution deadlines (15 days) are tight; Sabre and Amadeus GDS present ADM data in different formats, requiring manual normalisation

l4_steps.name: Dispute or accept ADM within IATA resolution window
l4_steps.input: ADM validity assessment from step 4.1
l4_steps.output: Dispute filed or ADM accepted; agency account debited
l4_steps.kpi: Dispute win rate ≥70% of contested ADMs; zero ADMs missed past IATA 15-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines cannot dispute ADMs if original error was due to their own fare filing omission in ATPCO — requires internal root-cause log to differentiate

l4_steps.name: Escalate fraudulent booking patterns for recovery
l4_steps.input: Patterns of repeated TTL abuse, duplicate bookings, or fictitious PNRs detected in NRM
l4_steps.output: Agency fraud alert; blocked IATA number referral to BSP compliance team
l4_steps.kpi: Fraud pattern detected within 48 hrs of first occurrence; zero undetected churned-inventory incidents per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM does not natively flag cross-GDS duplicate booking patterns — requires manual cross-referencing of Sabre, Amadeus, and Travelport PNR exports

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP/ARC sales data against PSS ticket log
l4_steps.input: Daily BSP/ARC billing file and Altéa ticket transaction log
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation report identifying matched, unmatched, and disputed items
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completion by T+3 business days; unmatched items ≤0.1% of gross ticket revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP billing files use IATA Standard Numeric Code (SNC) which must be mapped to SAP cost centre hierarchy — mapping table breaks when new routes are added without finance notification

l4_steps.name: Resolve settlement discrepancies and post corrections
l4_steps.input: Unmatched items list from step 5.1
l4_steps.output: Corrected journal entries posted in SAP; debit/credit notes issued to agencies
l4_steps.kpi: Discrepancy resolution rate ≥98% within 10 business days of identification
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-currency settlement discrepancies on BSP billings (e.g., EUR vs. USD) create FX rounding differences that accumulate to material amounts over high-volume periods

l4_steps.name: Generate revenue integrity KPI dashboard
l4_steps.input: Reconciled settlement data, exception counts, ADM register, and refund log
l4_steps.output: Weekly revenue integrity scorecard published to RM leadership
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by Monday 09:00 each week; data freshness ≤24 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Data pipeline from Altéa PSS to Tableau uses nightly batch export — intraday exceptions are invisible until next morning, delaying management response

l4_steps.name: Audit agency ticketing compliance and escalate violations
l4_steps.input: KPI dashboard from step 6.1; agency-level error rate trends
l4_steps.output: Agency compliance rating; escalation to Distribution Management for repeat violators
l4_steps.kpi: Agencies with error rate >2% flagged for remediation within 30 days; systemic non-compliance resolved within 90 days
l4_steps.pain_point: PRISM data covers ARC (US/Canada) only — non-ARC international agency compliance monitoring requires separate BSP market-by-market data pull with no consolidated view

l4_steps.name: Extract O&D booking history from data lake
l4_steps.input: Daily booking feed from Amadeus Altéa PSS (12-month rolling window)
l4_steps.output: Cleaned O&D demand dataset segmented by cabin, point-of-sale, and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness ≥99%; extraction latency <2 hours from departure day-close
l4_steps.pain_point: Connecting itineraries booked via GDS often log leg-level data only; O&D reconstruction requires custom passenger name record (PNR) stitching logic that breaks during irregular operations

l4_steps.name: Segment O&D demand by fare class and channel
l4_steps.input: Cleaned O&D demand dataset from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: Demand segments by fare class (Y/B/M/H/Q/V/W/L/K/G), booking channel, and travel purpose (leisure/business)
l4_steps.kpi: Segment classification accuracy ≥92%; misclassified itineraries <5% of O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Carriers without seat assignment (open-boarding models) lack seat-map signals for travel-purpose inference, reducing segmentation accuracy vs. assigned-seat competitors

l4_steps.name: Generate 90-day O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.input: Segmented demand history, seasonal indices, special-events calendar
l4_steps.output: 90-day O&D demand forecast by fare class and day-of-week; confidence intervals at 80% and 95%
l4_steps.kpi: Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) ≤8% at 60-day horizon; ≤12% at 90-day horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST demand models require minimum 18 months of stable history per O&D; new routes or routes disrupted by major events (e.g., network collapse, weather) cause cold-start forecast degradation

l4_steps.name: Validate forecast against booking pace signals
l4_steps.input: 90-day O&D demand forecast; live booking-curve actuals from Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Validated forecast or rework flag with variance root-cause note
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast validation cycle <4 hours; >95% of O&D pairs accepted without manual override
l4_steps.pain_point: Sudden demand spikes driven by flash sales or competitor capacity withdrawal are not captured by statistical models, requiring analyst intervention outside automated tolerance bands

l4_steps.name: Calculate network contribution per itinerary
l4_steps.input: Validated O&D demand forecast; filed fare inventory from ATPCO; connection rules from Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.output: O&D contribution matrix: revenue yield, spill cost, and recapture probability per itinerary
l4_steps.kpi: Network revenue contribution accuracy within ±3% of post-departure actuals; matrix refresh latency ≤6 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point network topology limits connecting itinerary combinations available for O&D value netting; contribution calculation must account for high-frequency same-city multi-flight options

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitive fares by O&D market
l4_steps.input: Competitor schedule data (OAG), ATPCO published fares, Sabre GDS fare feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitive gap analysis: own-fare vs. lowest available competitor fare by O&D and booking lead time
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive fare index maintained within ±5% of market median for top-50 revenue O&D pairs
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitor dynamic pricing and NDC fare products are not consistently visible through ATPCO filings; private corporate fares and carrier-direct channel fares create persistent blind spots in competitive benchmarking

l4_steps.name: Assess O&D contribution validity
l4_steps.input: O&D contribution matrix; competitive gap analysis
l4_steps.output: Approved contribution matrix or rework instruction with adjustment rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Gate review cycle ≤2 hours; <10% of O&D pairs requiring manual contribution override
l4_steps.pain_point: High-frequency thin markets (routes with <5 flights/week) produce contribution estimates with wide confidence intervals; analysts must apply manual floors to prevent bid price collapse on low-frequency O&Ds

l4_steps.name: Run LP network optimisation for bid prices
l4_steps.input: Approved O&D contribution matrix; 90-day demand forecast; current flight leg capacities from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Shadow prices (bid prices) per leg-class combination for each active departure window
l4_steps.kpi: Optimisation solve time ≤45 minutes for full network; bid price solution feasibility ≥99.5% of legs
l4_steps.pain_point: LP model size grows quadratically with O&D pairs; large banks of short-haul turns can exceed solver memory limits, requiring network partitioning that degrades optimality

l4_steps.name: Review bid price reasonableness
l4_steps.input: Generated bid prices; prior-day bid prices; yield targets by O&D
l4_steps.output: Validated bid prices or escalation to RM Manager with variance explanation
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price variance vs. prior day flagged if >20%; analyst review cycle ≤90 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated bid prices occasionally produce outliers on O&Ds with thin history or solver anomalies; without mandatory review thresholds, outlier prices can suppress availability on high-demand markets

l4_steps.name: Publish approved bid prices to inventory
l4_steps.input: Validated bid prices
l4_steps.output: Bid prices committed to Altéa PSS availability engine; audit log entry with timestamp and analyst sign-off
l4_steps.kpi: Bid price publication latency <15 minutes from approval; 100% of active departures covered within the 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability cache refresh is asynchronous; published bid prices may not be visible to GDS availability queries for up to 10 minutes, creating a transient window where under-priced availability is sold

l4_steps.name: Apply O&D class controls to Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Published bid prices; authorisation levels (AU) per fare class from NRM
l4_steps.output: Updated fare class open/close status in Altéa inventory; availability snapshot distributed to GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.kpi: Class control accuracy ≥99.8% (no misapplied open/close); distribution sync to all GDS channels <5 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa virtual class nesting requires correct AU configuration per booking class; misconfigured inheritance rules cause availability bleed-through where higher-value classes sell below bid price

l4_steps.name: Monitor intraday booking pace vs. forecast
l4_steps.input: Real-time bookings from Altéa PSS; validated O&D demand forecast
l4_steps.output: Intraday booking pace report; pace-vs-forecast variance by O&D and fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Monitoring refresh interval ≤30 minutes; pace deviation alerts triggered at ±10% threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: Bulk GDS batch bookings (travel agency group uploads) cause instantaneous pace spikes that trigger false-positive alerts; lack of booking intent signals before ticketing makes proactive controls difficult

l4_steps.name: Evaluate booking pace deviation trigger
l4_steps.input: Intraday pace report; alert flags for O&Ds exceeding ±10% deviation
l4_steps.output: Decision: hold current controls, tighten availability, or open additional classes
l4_steps.kpi: Override response time <60 minutes from alert; revenue impact of late override <0.5% of flight revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Intraday override authority is often limited to Senior Analysts; escalation to RM Manager during off-hours (night departures, weekend shifts) delays response and allows continued mis-pricing

l4_steps.name: Execute manual availability override
l4_steps.input: Override instruction (tighten or open classes); fare class control screen in Altéa
l4_steps.output: Revised class availability posted to Altéa; override action logged with business justification
l4_steps.kpi: Override-to-publish latency <10 minutes; 100% of overrides logged with analyst ID and rationale
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual override in Altéa bypasses NRM optimisation logic; overrides that remain in place beyond the intended window lock in suboptimal availability and are difficult to detect without dedicated override-expiry workflow

l4_steps.name: Capture post-departure O&D revenue actuals
l4_steps.input: Final departure manifest from Altéa; ticketing revenue records from BSP / ARC settlement
l4_steps.output: Post-departure O&D revenue report: RASM, yield, load factor, spill, and spoilage by fare class
l4_steps.kpi: Report availability ≤24 hours post-departure; O&D revenue reconciliation variance vs. settlement <0.2%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP/ARC settlement files arrive 48–72 hours post-departure; provisional revenue figures used in day-1 reporting may differ materially from final settled amounts, inflating apparent yield performance

l4_steps.name: Evaluate demand model accuracy
l4_steps.input: Post-departure actuals; corresponding pre-departure forecasts
l4_steps.output: Model accuracy scorecard (MAPE by O&D, phase, and departure horizon); recalibration flag if accuracy <85%
l4_steps.kpi: Model accuracy review completed within 5 business days of departure; ≥85% of O&D pairs meeting MAPE target
l4_steps.pain_point: Forecast accuracy degrades systematically for new O&Ds, seasonal routes restarted after winter suspension, and markets affected by competitor schedule changes — all require manual baseline resets that the NRM auto-calibration does not trigger

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate O&D demand models
l4_steps.input: Recalibration flag; post-departure actuals; external demand signals (GDP, events, competitor changes)
l4_steps.output: Updated model parameters committed to NRM; change log with effective date and recalibration rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration turnaround ≤3 business days; post-recalibration MAPE improvement ≥15% on flagged O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM model recalibration requires analyst SQL access to Redshift parameter tables; access provisioning delays during analyst onboarding leave new team members unable to execute recalibrations independently

l4_steps.name: Ingest LCC published fares from ATPCO feed
l4_steps.input: Daily ATPCO fare-change notification feed across all GDS-filed LCC fares
l4_steps.output: Structured LCC fare dataset by O&D pair, cabin, booking class, and advance purchase tier
l4_steps.kpi: Fare update latency ≤4 hours from ATPCO filing; coverage ≥80% of LCC-filed fares
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC carriers increasingly use direct-channel-only fares not filed via ATPCO; ACI feed misses 20–35% of actual LCC selling prices on contested routes

l4_steps.name: Scrape LCC direct-channel fares via fare shopping
l4_steps.input: LCC-overlap route list and 90-day departure date range
l4_steps.output: LCC web-fare matrix by route, departure date, and fare class including ancillary fee schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Shopping coverage ≥95% of LCC-overlap routes completed within 24 hours; intraday refresh on routes with >50 weekly LCC departures
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC carriers revise fares multiple times per day; bot-detection mechanisms on Spirit and Frontier websites block automated scraping, requiring manual supplementation that introduces 12–24h lag

l4_steps.name: Flag routes exceeding LCC penetration threshold
l4_steps.input: LCC fare matrix combined with OAG Traffic Analyser market share data
l4_steps.output: Priority route list with LCC threat tier classification (High / Medium / Low) for current and next 90-day window
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of routes with LCC market share >25% flagged and tier-assigned within 48 hours of data refresh
l4_steps.pain_point: MIDT-sourced market share data lags 60–90 days; real-time share is modelled, not measured, creating tier misclassification risk on recently-entered LCC markets

l4_steps.name: Calculate fully-loaded fare differential vs LCC
l4_steps.input: Own lowest available fare per O&D; LCC base fare plus published ancillary fee schedule from Step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Net fare gap report showing base-fare delta and fully-loaded delta (bag + seat assignment + change fee) per route
l4_steps.kpi: Fully-loaded fare gap calculated within 2 hours of trigger event; model accuracy ±5% vs actual LCC checkout price
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC ancillary fee schedules are not available via any standardised data feed and change without notice; manual fee updates lag by up to one week, overstating or understating the real passenger cost differential

l4_steps.name: Assess LCC seat capacity deployment on overlap routes
l4_steps.input: LCC published schedules from OAG; own schedule from Amadeus SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Capacity share report showing seats, weekly frequencies, and ASK split by carrier for each contested O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Capacity share delta vs prior 4-week period reported weekly; >10% capacity increase by any LCC triggers immediate alert
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC carriers file schedule placeholders with inflated frequencies to hold airport slot positions; published seats overstate committed capacity by up to 15%, inflating perceived competitive threat and driving unnecessary yield dilution responses

l4_steps.name: Classify route competitive response mode
l4_steps.input: Fare gap report from Step 2.1; capacity share report from Step 2.2; route RASM from Amadeus SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Route-level response mode classification: MATCH / STIMULATE / DIFFERENTIATE / IGNORE, with documented rationale and RASM impact estimate
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of High-tier LCC routes assigned response mode within 72 hours; response mode reviewed every 21 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Differentiation strategy (premium service, schedule convenience) is difficult to sustain on short-haul routes under 500 miles where LCC price advantage exceeds perceived product differential — risks revenue dilution without stimulation benefit materialising

l4_steps.name: Define route fare floor against unit cost recovery
l4_steps.input: Route-level CASM (cost per available seat mile) from finance cost allocation module; load factor target from SkyCAST forecast
l4_steps.output: Minimum acceptable fare floor per route and cabin class, approved by Finance
l4_steps.kpi: Fare floor covers variable cost per seat at target load factor ≥100% on 100% of routes; floor breach rate <2% of all filed competitive fares
l4_steps.pain_point: Short-haul CASM on thin regional routes can exceed the LCC's total all-in fare — matching requires contribution-negative seat sales; VP Revenue sign-off required for any floor breach, creating decision bottleneck during fast-moving LCC fare wars

l4_steps.name: Construct ATPCO fare basis codes and rule conditions
l4_steps.input: Approved fare level and floor from Step 3.1; target O&D pairs; advance purchase and change fee structure
l4_steps.output: Draft fare record with Fare Basis Code and complete ATPCO Category 3, 5, 14, 15, and 16 rule set
l4_steps.kpi: Fare rule filing completeness ≥98% (zero missing ATPCO categories); internal peer review completed within 4 hours of draft creation
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 15 (Sales Restrictions) mis-filings create GDS display errors that misdirect competitive fares to wrong markets or channels; full audit trail mandatory on all competitive-response fares to support regulatory review

l4_steps.name: Configure NRM inventory availability and bid-price thresholds
l4_steps.input: Approved fare record; booking class assignment; O&D demand forecast from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Updated booking class authorization levels (AU) and bid-price thresholds in NRM for all affected O&D pairs
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory control update applied within 2 hours of fare approval; AU accuracy ±2 seats vs modelled optimum at D-90
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM bid-price recalibration for competitive fares risks cannibalising higher-yield bookings if LCC-stimulated demand does not materialise as forecast; demand signal validation required before activation on routes with >60% business-travel mix

l4_steps.name: Apply channel-specific fare availability configuration
l4_steps.input: Approved fare record; channel distribution matrix (GDS / NDC / direct web)
l4_steps.output: Channel-differentiated fare availability configuration in NDC API Gateway and Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.kpi: NDC-exclusive fares available within 4 hours of ATPCO filing; GDS display parity ≥95% across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus within 8 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC fare surfacing in Sabre and Travelport requires bilateral API certification agreements not yet in place with all TMC partners; competitive fares may be invisible to managed-travel corporate buyers, ceding LCC-contested bookings to direct channels only

l4_steps.name: File competitive fare in ATPCO and validate GDS mirror
l4_steps.input: Peer-reviewed fare record and complete rule set from Step 3.2
l4_steps.output: ATPCO filing confirmation with batch-processing timestamp; GDS mirror latency report across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus
l4_steps.kpi: Fare live in all three GDS within 8 hours of ATPCO filing; zero Category 15 validation errors; filing confirmed in ATPCO audit log
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch processing runs only three times daily (0200, 1000, 1800 ET); up to 8 hours may elapse before GDS visibility is restored, during which the LCC has already captured price-sensitive bookings that cannot be recovered

l4_steps.name: Activate competitive fare in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation from Step 4.1; NRM authorization levels from Step 3.3
l4_steps.output: Fare live in Altéa PSS for direct and indirect bookings; PSS-NRM inventory sync confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: PSS activation within 1 hour of ATPCO confirmation; zero inventory sync discrepancies between Altéa and NRM authorization levels
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS-NRM inventory sync misalignment during high-traffic booking periods can result in seats sold below NRM bid price; monitored via NRM exception queue with 30-minute reconciliation cycle during peak booking windows

l4_steps.name: Issue pricing action bulletin to sales and accounts
l4_steps.input: Activated fare details; competitive context briefing from Step 2.3 response mode classification
l4_steps.output: Pricing action bulletin distributed via Salesforce CRM to Sales, Agency Relations, and Corporate Account teams
l4_steps.kpi: Bulletin issued within 2 hours of fare activation; 100% of key account managers and top-50 agency contacts notified; read-receipt tracked in Salesforce
l4_steps.pain_point: Corporate account managers frequently learn of competitive price changes from TMC partners before receiving internal notification, creating a trust deficit and triggering premature contract renegotiation requests that consume revenue management bandwidth

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking velocity on LCC-contested routes
l4_steps.input: Daily booking curves by route, fare class, and departure date from NRM booking pace module
l4_steps.output: Booking velocity report versus LCC-free baseline curve; stimulation delta by departure date and O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Booking pace ≥95% of target curve by D-14; seat load factor ≥83% at D-7 on High-tier LCC routes
l4_steps.pain_point: LCC carriers routinely run flash sales 7–10 days prior to departure that distort historical pace curves; NRM demand models trained on non-LCC-disrupted data underestimate last-minute demand spikes and trigger premature availability closures

l4_steps.name: Compare RASM and PRASM against LCC benchmark
l4_steps.input: Booked revenue and ASMs flown per route; LCC benchmark fares from ATPCO ACI prior-period dataset; Amadeus SkyCAST RASM actuals
l4_steps.output: RASM versus benchmark scorecard with revenue gain or loss attribution by route and competitive response mode
l4_steps.kpi: RASM on contested routes within 5% of network average; PRASM improvement >2% versus pre-strategy baseline after 21-day observation window
l4_steps.pain_point: Attribution of RASM movement to pricing strategy versus macro demand shifts requires multivariate regression not available natively in NRM or SkyCAST; AWS Redshift custom model has a 3–5 day build latency that delays actionable insight

l4_steps.name: Trigger strategy review or escalate to pricing committee
l4_steps.input: RASM scorecard from Step 5.2; booking velocity report from Step 5.1; updated LCC fare intelligence from Step 1.1
l4_steps.output: Strategy continuation approval, or pricing committee escalation package with revised response mode recommendation and fare adjustment proposal
l4_steps.kpi: Strategy review cycle completed within 21 days of activation; escalated routes resolved by pricing committee within 5 business days; route RASM restored to within 5% of network average within 45 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Monthly pricing committee cadence is too slow to counter LCC tactical fare moves that shift daily; airlines with weekly governance cycles capture 3–5% more revenue on contested routes by responding before LCC-stimulated demand is fully absorbed

l4_steps.name: Extract Competitive Fare Data from GDS
l4_steps.input: GDS published fares, OAG Schedule Analyser competitive feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitor fare matrix by O&D, cabin, and advance purchase window
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive data refresh latency ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare data excludes NDC-only offers from competitors; pricing team has blind spots on ~15% of market fares filed outside ATPCO

l4_steps.name: Analyse O&D Demand & Price Elasticity
l4_steps.input: Historical booking curves, O&D traffic reports, demand signal matrix
l4_steps.output: Price elasticity model by market segment and booking window
l4_steps.kpi: Elasticity model R² ≥0.85
l4_steps.pain_point: Thin O&D markets with <500 passengers/month produce statistically unreliable elasticity estimates; models default to network averages, masking micro-market dynamics

l4_steps.name: Confirm Market Opportunity & Pricing Mandate
l4_steps.input: Elasticity model, competitive fare matrix, revenue target by route
l4_steps.output: Pricing mandate document — target position vs. market (premium, match, or undercut)
l4_steps.kpi: Time-to-mandate ≤2 business days from competitive trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Pricing mandate approval chains across Revenue Management, Sales, and Network Planning frequently exceed 5 days, delaying competitive response windows

l4_steps.name: Define Fare Basis Codes & Fare Families
l4_steps.input: Pricing mandate, existing fare basis code library
l4_steps.output: Fare basis code list per cabin with fare family mapping (Economy Light, Standard, Flex, Business)
l4_steps.kpi: Fare basis code uniqueness — zero duplicate FBC conflicts per filing batch
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy fare basis code libraries carry hundreds of inactive codes; proliferation causes look-up errors in PSS and downstream revenue accounting mis-allocation

l4_steps.name: Set Fare Ladder by Cabin & Booking Class
l4_steps.input: Fare family definitions, RM booking class inventory map, target revenue contribution
l4_steps.output: Fare ladder table — fare amounts by booking class (Y/B/M/H/Q/V/L/G/W) for each O&D
l4_steps.kpi: Average fare premium over lowest competitor ≥5% in protected markets
l4_steps.pain_point: Misalignment between pricing booking class ladder and RM availability controls causes revenue dilution; PROS RM overrides manual fare ladders without automated reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Validate Fare Ladder Against RM Inventory
l4_steps.input: Proposed fare ladder, current RM class availability settings
l4_steps.output: Reconciled fare-to-class mapping; conflict report if misalignment detected
l4_steps.kpi: Zero booking class conflicts at time of filing; reconciliation completed within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: RM system re-optimises availability every 15 minutes; static fare ladder snapshots become stale quickly, requiring intra-day reconciliation loops

l4_steps.name: Code Advance Purchase & Minimum Stay Rules
l4_steps.input: Approved fare structure, regulatory requirements, market seasonality calendar
l4_steps.output: ATPCO Category 5 (Advance Purchase) and Category 6 (Minimum Stay) rule records
l4_steps.kpi: Rule coding error rate ≤0.5% per 1,000 fare rule records filed
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 5/6 rule logic requires manual coding in legacy field-based interface; high error rate on complex multi-sector rules requires rework averaging 2.3 hours per filing

l4_steps.name: Define Change & Cancellation Fee Structures
l4_steps.input: Commercial policy (fee schedule), fare family service attribute matrix
l4_steps.output: ATPCO Category 16 (Penalties) rule records; fee table by fare family
l4_steps.kpi: Fee structure consistency — 100% of fare families have documented penalty rules before filing
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-pandemic regulatory pressure (EU Regulation 261/2004, DOT refund rules) requires frequent penalty rule updates; manual ATPCO recoding averages 3–5 days per policy change cycle

l4_steps.name: Set Combinability & Routing Rules
l4_steps.input: Interline agreements, codeshare partner list, ticketing authority records
l4_steps.output: ATPCO Category 10 (Combinations) and Category 25 (Fare by Rule) records
l4_steps.kpi: Routing rule coverage — 100% of marketed O&Ds with codeshare have valid combination rules
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines without alliance membership have limited combinability — standalone routing rules limit interlining revenue recovery and increase mispricing risk on complex itineraries

l4_steps.name: Submit Fare Records to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Validated fare basis codes, amounts, and rule records; effective date schedule
l4_steps.output: ATPCO filing batch confirmation; fare record IDs
l4_steps.kpi: Filing lead time: fares effective ≥T+24 hours from ATPCO submission; zero rejected records per batch
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch submission windows run at fixed intervals (00:00 and 12:00 UTC); missed windows delay fare activation by up to 12 hours, ceding pricing windows to competitors

l4_steps.name: Distribute Fares to GDS Channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO fare records (published), Travelport and Amadeus GDS distribution agreements
l4_steps.output: GDS fare tables populated in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; EDIFACT ATPCO push confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: GDS distribution lag ≤2 hours post-ATPCO publication
l4_steps.pain_point: EDIFACT-based GDS distribution is batch-driven and cannot support real-time fare updates; airlines using NDC face dual-stack maintenance (ATPCO + NDC API) with no automated synchronisation

l4_steps.name: Publish NDC Offers via API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Fare structure JSON, fare family service attributes, ancillary offer catalogue
l4_steps.output: NDC Offer Response payload; fare published in NDC-connected OTA and TMC channels
l4_steps.kpi: NDC offer availability within 1 hour of ATPCO activation; API error rate ≤0.1%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC offer construction requires separate fare attribute mapping not present in ATPCO records; pricing teams maintain parallel NDC content files — duplication risk is high and divergence causes fare parity violations

l4_steps.name: Execute End-to-End Fare Shopping Test
l4_steps.input: Filed fare effective date, test O&D pairs, booking class list
l4_steps.output: Fare shopping test report — fare display, priceable itineraries, tax calculation
l4_steps.kpi: QA pass rate ≥99.5% of tested fare/class combinations before go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS fare calculation engine applies complex proration and tax logic; errors in Category 25 Fare by Rule records produce incorrect taxes that only surface during test and cause passenger refund exposure

l4_steps.name: Validate Fare Display Across All GDS Channels
l4_steps.input: Fare shopping test results, GDS fare display screens (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus)
l4_steps.output: Cross-channel fare parity report; exception list for mis-displayed fares
l4_steps.kpi: Fare parity across all three GDS channels within 2 hours of ATPCO activation; zero parity breaches at go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare display logic applies proprietary fare selection algorithms (lowest logical fare rules); correctly filed ATPCO fares may display incorrectly due to GDS-side rule interpretation, which the airline cannot directly control

l4_steps.name: Monitor Filed Fare Performance vs. Revenue Targets
l4_steps.input: Live booking data, fare mix report, yield-per-passenger by fare family
l4_steps.output: Fare performance dashboard; revenue alert if yield drops >5% below target
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue per available seat mile (RASM) within ±3% of plan at T+7 post-filing
l4_steps.pain_point: RM system optimises inventory in real time but does not feed back fare performance signals to ATPCO — pricing re-filing decisions are based on lagged weekly reports rather than live yield data

l4_steps.name: Track Competitor Fare Changes & Trigger Re-filing
l4_steps.input: Competitor ATPCO fare change alerts, GDS fare monitor feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitive response recommendation; re-filing ticket if action required
l4_steps.kpi: Competitive response time ≤4 hours for primary O&Ds; ≤24 hours for secondary markets
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO competitive alert services notify of filed fares but not NDC-only prices; carriers increasingly filing competitive fares exclusively via NDC bypass ATPCO monitoring, creating systematic intelligence gaps

l4_steps.name: Extract approved fare constructs from RM system
l4_steps.input: Approved fare change request from Pricing Strategy team
l4_steps.output: Fare constructs with cabin, booking class, and route scope ready for tariff formatting
l4_steps.kpi: Fare extraction accuracy ≥99.5%; extraction completed ≥48 hrs before effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM fare constructs occasionally contain rule exceptions (e.g. negotiated corporate overrides) not natively expressible in ATPCO Category 15 — requires manual tariff analyst workaround adding 2–4 hrs

l4_steps.name: Map fares to ATPCO fare basis codes & rule categories
l4_steps.input: Approved fare constructs, existing tariff structure and fare family definitions
l4_steps.output: ATPCO-formatted fare records covering Categories 1–35 (advance purchase, min stay, penalties, sales restrictions)
l4_steps.kpi: Fare basis code mapping accuracy ≥99%; Category rule coverage ≥95% automated
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 25 (penalty) and Category 15 (sales restriction) rules require manual authoring — automation covers only ~70% of rule types, increasing tariff analyst workload during peak fare events

l4_steps.name: Validate rule consistency, combinability & blackout dates
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Automated Pricing and Quality Assurance (APQC)
l4_steps.input: Mapped ATPCO fare records
l4_steps.output: Pre-submission validation report; list of rule conflicts or blackout date clashes
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-submission validation error rate <2%; all errors resolved before ATPCO filing cutoff
l4_steps.pain_point: Blackout date conflicts with advance purchase minimum rules cause ATPCO pre-validation rejection — affects ~5% of seasonal filings and forces same-day reruns against tight submission deadlines

l4_steps.name: Submit fare tariff records to ATPCO before cutoff
l4_steps.input: Validated ATPCO fare records; applicable effective and discontinue dates
l4_steps.output: ATPCO submission receipt with transaction IDs and filing timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Submission success rate ≥99%; filed ≥24 hrs before effective date; zero late filings during peak sale events
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO submission cutoff (typically 0001Z day prior to effective date) is frequently missed during peak pricing events (holiday flash sales, competitor matching) — missed cutoff delays fare availability by 24 hrs, ceding revenue to competitors

l4_steps.name: Monitor ATPCO acknowledgment and error correction queue
l4_steps.input: ATPCO submission receipt and transaction IDs
l4_steps.output: Clean acknowledgment confirmation or itemised error correction list for resubmission
l4_steps.kpi: ATPCO acknowledgment received within 2 hrs of submission; error correction resubmitted within 1 hr of error receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch processing delays during high-volume industry filing periods (US public holidays, IATA fare sales coordination windows) push acknowledgment beyond 4 hrs — creates uncertainty on whether fares will be live for next-day sale open

l4_steps.name: Verify fare pickup and display in Sabre GDS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO acknowledgment confirmation and effective date/time
l4_steps.output: Sabre GDS fare availability test confirmed; mismatches logged for escalation
l4_steps.kpi: Sabre fare pickup within 4 hrs of ATPCO effective time; display accuracy ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre GDS fare filing propagation latency can exceed 6 hrs during high-volume pricing events — creates booking windows where incorrect legacy fares are sold, triggering ADM disputes and customer compensation claims

l4_steps.name: Verify fare pickup in Travelport GDS channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO acknowledgment confirmation
l4_steps.output: Fare availability confirmed across Travelport Apollo and Galileo subscriber segments
l4_steps.kpi: Travelport fare pickup within 4 hrs of ATPCO effective time; consistent display across Apollo and Galileo ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport Apollo/Galileo dual-GDS architecture creates inconsistent fare display between subscriber segments — TMC agents on Apollo may see different fares than Galileo agencies for the same O&D pair during propagation window

l4_steps.name: Verify fare pickup in Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO acknowledgment confirmation
l4_steps.output: Fare availability confirmed in Amadeus GDS; cache refresh status noted
l4_steps.kpi: Amadeus fare pickup within 4 hrs of ATPCO effective time; zero stale-cache bookings at effective date boundary
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus GDS fare cache refresh intervals can suppress newly filed fares for up to 30 min post-effective time — during midnight effective-date rollovers this window produces bookings at wrong fare levels that require involuntary refunds

l4_steps.name: Activate fares for live sale across all GDS channels
l4_steps.input: Pickup confirmations from Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.output: Fares activated for live booking across all GDS channels; channel activation log created
l4_steps.kpi: Channel parity — all GDS channels display identical fares within 30 min of activation; activation completion ≥99.8%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS inventory sync with GDS availability responses can lag up to 15 min — agents see a quoted fare but receive a no-availability response at booking, increasing call centre contacts and reducing conversion rate

l4_steps.name: Publish approved fares via NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Approved fare constructs; GDS activation confirmation; NDC offer schema mapping
l4_steps.output: NDC AirShopping and AirPrice offer responses reflecting new fares with branded fare family attributes
l4_steps.kpi: NDC offer response latency <500ms at p99; NDC fare coverage parity with GDS ≥98%; NDC go-live within 2 hrs of GDS activation
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC 21.3 schema does not natively support all ATPCO rule category expressions — Category 15 sales restrictions require custom mapping that adds 4–6 hrs of integration work per fare family change and creates divergence risk between ATPCO-filed rules and NDC offer terms

l4_steps.name: Validate fare display on direct.com and mobile app
l4_steps.input: NDC offer API responses; direct channel pricing engine configuration
l4_steps.output: Validated fare display on airline website and mobile app with correct ancillary bundling
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel fare accuracy ≥99.9%; page load including fare display <2 seconds; zero ghost-fare bookings post-filing
l4_steps.pain_point: Direct channel pricing engine caches fare offers aggressively — cache invalidation lag of 5–10 min causes brief display of superseded fares immediately after a filing goes live, resulting in customer confusion and potential obligation to honour incorrect prices

l4_steps.name: Run automated fare audit against ATPCO live filing
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Automated Pricing and Quality Assurance (APQC)
l4_steps.input: Live GDS fare quotes from Sabre/Travelport/Amadeus; NDC offer responses; ATPCO filed tariff records
l4_steps.output: Fare audit report with pass/fail by O&D pair; mismatch list with severity classification
l4_steps.kpi: Fare audit pass rate ≥99.8% of sampled O&D pairs; P1 mismatch detection within 30 min of effective time
l4_steps.pain_point: APQC automated audit covers only ~85% of fare rule combinations — complex combinability rules (ATPCO Category 10) and through-fare constructs require manual sampling, leaving a 15% blind spot that has historically surfaced as customer complaints rather than internal detection

l4_steps.name: Resolve fare display or combinability errors and refile
l4_steps.input: Fare audit mismatch report; GDS error details
l4_steps.output: Corrected ATPCO filing or GDS override instruction; incident log with root cause
l4_steps.kpi: P1 fare display error resolution within 4 hrs; P2 within 24 hrs; zero repeat errors from same root cause within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Combinability errors between published fares and add-on/through fares (ATPCO Cat 10) are notoriously difficult to diagnose without GDS vendor support — escalation tickets to Sabre or Amadeus typically add 24–48 hrs to resolution, during which incorrect fares may continue to be sold

l4_steps.name: Monitor real-time fare parity across distribution channels
l4_steps.input: Real-time fare quotes from GDS, NDC, OTA scrape feeds, and metasearch platforms
l4_steps.output: Channel parity dashboard; automated parity breach alerts with breach severity and channel identified
l4_steps.kpi: Best Available Rate (BAR) parity compliance ≥97% across all monitored channels; parity breach alert-to-resolution SLA <2 hrs for P1 breaches
l4_steps.pain_point: OTA and metasearch caching of superseded fares causes parity breaches that are invisible to airline distribution systems — detected only through mystery shopping, customer complaints, or third-party parity monitoring tools, with resolution dependent on OTA cache TTL (typically 4–24 hrs)

l4_steps.name: Archive fare filing records to data lake for compliance
l4_steps.input: All filed ATPCO records, GDS activation logs, NDC publication logs, and audit reports from current cycle
l4_steps.output: Archived fare filing records with timestamp, version history, and channel confirmation — retained 7 years per DOT and IATA requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Audit trail completeness 100% per filing cycle; archive job SLA <1 hr post-activation; retrieval latency <15 min for DOT audit requests
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare filing history is fragmented across ATPCO archives, GDS history logs, and internal NRM exports — DOT or IATA audit requests require manual aggregation from 3+ source systems, typically taking 2–3 business days and exposing the airline to compliance risk if records are incomplete

l4_steps.name: Extract revenue shortfall signals by route
l4_steps.input: Current booking pace reports, load factor actuals, revenue-per-ASM trend
l4_steps.output: Ranked list of routes with revenue shortfall vs. target
l4_steps.kpi: Routes identified with load factor <75% at 60-day departure horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM O&D data aggregation latency of 24 hrs can mask intra-day demand shifts on thin routes

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor promotional fares
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare filings, OAG schedule data, ATPCO tariff feeds
l4_steps.output: Competitive fare landscape report by market and travel window
l4_steps.kpi: Competitor fare monitoring coverage ≥95% of target markets
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO feed refresh lag up to 4 hours means recently filed competitor promos may be missed

l4_steps.name: Validate demand gap and competitive case
l4_steps.input: Revenue shortfall list, competitive fare landscape report, demand elasticity model
l4_steps.output: Approved target market list or no-action record
l4_steps.kpi: Decision cycle time <2 business days from trigger
l4_steps.pain_point: Demand elasticity coefficients in SkyCAST may not reflect post-COVID traveller behaviour shifts

l4_steps.name: Define target markets and travel windows
l4_steps.input: Approved target market list, historical promo booking curve data
l4_steps.output: Promotion scope document: routes, travel dates, sale window, fare class targets
l4_steps.kpi: Scope document completed within 1 business day of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Point-to-point booking data cannot quantify connecting-itinerary stimulus for carriers with hub overlap

l4_steps.name: Model promotional fare levels and AP rules
l4_steps.input: Promotion scope document, demand elasticity curves, competitor fare benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Draft fare ladder with advance purchase, minimum stay, and cap rules
l4_steps.kpi: Modelled incremental revenue uplift ≥8% over base forecast
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM fare optimisation models require minimum 18 months booking history; thin routes yield unreliable elasticity estimates

l4_steps.name: Simulate revenue and load factor impact
l4_steps.input: Draft fare ladder, current seat inventory allocation, booking pace baseline
l4_steps.output: Scenario simulation report: projected load factor, RASM, yield dilution estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Projected system load factor ≥83%; projected RASM ≥ current period RASM
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM scenario runs do not model real-time competitor reaction; simulation may overstate incremental demand

l4_steps.name: Draft detailed fare rules and blackout dates
l4_steps.input: Approved fare ladder, simulation report, peak-period calendar
l4_steps.output: Complete fare rule set: Cat 2 (Day/Time), Cat 5 (Advance Purchase), Cat 6 (Min Stay), Cat 14 (Blackouts)
l4_steps.kpi: Fare rule completeness: all ATPCO mandatory categories populated before submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual blackout date entry is error-prone; misaligned peak dates cause revenue leakage during holidays

l4_steps.name: Submit fare package to Pricing Committee
l4_steps.input: Fare rule set, simulation report, revenue impact summary
l4_steps.output: Pricing Committee review submission with financial P&L impact
l4_steps.kpi: Submission to decision cycle ≤3 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee quorum requirements can delay approval by 3–5 days during peak planning seasons

l4_steps.name: Conduct DOT advertising compliance review
l4_steps.input: Approved fare rules, proposed marketing copy, sale and travel date windows
l4_steps.output: DOT compliance sign-off or revision request
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of promotional fares reviewed against DOT 14 CFR Part 399 before publication
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT rules require all fees to be disclosed in advertised price; dynamic ancillary bundles create disclosure complexity

l4_steps.name: Issue formal fare design approval record
l4_steps.input: Pricing Committee approval, DOT compliance sign-off
l4_steps.output: Fare design approval record with authorisation timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Approval record issued within 1 business day of final compliance clearance
l4_steps.pain_point: Audit trail stored in disconnected email systems; no integrated workflow between legal review and pricing execution tools

l4_steps.name: File promotional fare records in ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Fare design approval record, complete fare rule set
l4_steps.output: ATPCO tariff records filed; transaction IDs logged
l4_steps.kpi: Filing-to-distribution latency <4 hours; ATPCO error-free submission rate ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 25 (fare by rule) errors are common when promotional fares inherit base fare conditions incorrectly

l4_steps.name: Verify fare pickup in all GDS channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO transaction IDs, Travelport and Amadeus GDS access
l4_steps.output: GDS fare availability confirmation across Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus
l4_steps.kpi: GDS pickup verified within 6 hours of ATPCO filing; parity across all 3 GDS ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport fare pickup latency can exceed Sabre by 2+ hours; delayed availability causes agent-quoted fare mismatches

l4_steps.name: Publish fare via NDC API Gateway and direct.com
l4_steps.input: GDS-confirmed fare records, direct channel pricing API configuration
l4_steps.output: Promotional fare live on direct.com, mobile app, and NDC-connected OTA partners
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel price parity with GDS ≥99.9%; NDC offer publication latency <2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC offer schema versioning between airline and OTA partners frequently causes display errors for complex rule fares

l4_steps.name: Activate promotional fare and initiate sale
l4_steps.input: Confirmed channel activation record, marketing launch confirmation
l4_steps.output: Promo fare live status confirmed; booking class availability open in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Sale activation within 30 minutes of planned launch time; zero mismatch between advertised and bookable fare
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa inventory class configuration must align with ATPCO filed booking codes; manual misalignment causes zero-sell errors

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking pace and load factor daily
l4_steps.input: Real-time booking transactions, load factor dashboard, pace vs. forecast
l4_steps.output: Daily promo performance report: bookings, load factor, revenue vs. target
l4_steps.kpi: Daily booking pace within ±15% of forecast; load factor trajectory toward ≥83% at departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM bid price recalculation triggered by promo booking surge can inadvertently close higher-yield inventory on peak flights

l4_steps.name: Adjust inventory caps based on pace signal
l4_steps.input: Daily promo performance report, pace vs. forecast variance
l4_steps.output: Revised booking class caps or sale window extension decision
l4_steps.kpi: Intervention decision time <4 hours from pace alert; yield dilution contained to <3% of base fare RASM
l4_steps.pain_point: Real-time cap adjustments in NRM can conflict with GDS cached availability, creating over-sell risk on thin-gauge aircraft

l4_steps.name: Pull post-campaign revenue and yield report
l4_steps.input: Closed booking records, promo fare transaction logs, flight departure actuals
l4_steps.output: Post-campaign report: total incremental revenue, load factor achieved, RASM vs. baseline
l4_steps.kpi: Report generated within 5 business days of sale close; variance from projection documented
l4_steps.pain_point: Attribution of incremental revenue vs. organic demand is methodologically complex without a clean control group

l4_steps.name: Assess yield dilution and cannibalisation
l4_steps.input: Post-campaign revenue report, base-fare RASM pre-promo, cabin mix actuals
l4_steps.output: Cannibalisation assessment: dilution %, affected routes, net revenue verdict
l4_steps.kpi: Net revenue positive vs. no-promo scenario at ≥95% confidence; cannibalisation rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: SkySYM counterfactual modelling depends on baseline demand stability; external shocks (weather, competitor sale) confound results

l4_steps.name: Archive campaign benchmarks to data lake
l4_steps.input: Post-campaign report, cannibalisation assessment, fare rule set
l4_steps.output: Campaign record persisted in data lake; benchmarks available for future promo calibration
l4_steps.kpi: Campaign record available in data lake within 2 business days of analysis sign-off
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent campaign tagging taxonomy across pricing and RM teams reduces future query accuracy

l4_steps.name: Initiate fare rule design from revenue strategy
l4_steps.input: Revenue strategy directives, competitive fare analysis from OAG Schedule Analyser
l4_steps.output: Fare rule design brief with scope, markets, and effective dates
l4_steps.kpi: Rule design brief turnaround ≤3 business days from strategy directive
l4_steps.pain_point: Pricing strategy changes arrive without lead time, forcing reactive rule authoring that increases first-pass error rates above 5%

l4_steps.name: Define advance purchase and ticketing time limits
l4_steps.input: Fare rule design brief, competitor AP restriction benchmarks from OAG
l4_steps.output: Draft ATPCO Category 5 (Advance Purchase) and Category 7 (Ticketing) rule parameters
l4_steps.kpi: AP/TTL restriction accuracy ≥99.5% match to approved design brief
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 5 and Category 7 interactions are not validated automatically; misconfiguration creates phantom availability windows or incorrect fare displays across all three GDS channels

l4_steps.name: Set minimum stay, blackout dates, and seasonality
l4_steps.input: Revenue management seasonality directives, Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM) demand curves
l4_steps.output: Draft ATPCO Category 6 (Minimum Stay), Category 2 (Day/Time), and blackout date rule set
l4_steps.kpi: Seasonal restriction accuracy ≥99%; blackout date coverage = 100% of designated periods
l4_steps.pain_point: Aligning ATPCO Category 6 with Amadeus NRM inventory controls requires manual coordination — no automated sync exists between the RM system and ATPCO rule records

l4_steps.name: Define change, cancellation, and refund rules
l4_steps.input: Commercial policy directives, DOT 14 CFR Part 259 refund regulation requirements
l4_steps.output: Draft ATPCO Category 16 (Penalties), Category 31 (Voluntary Changes), and Category 33 (Voluntary Refunds) parameters
l4_steps.kpi: DOT 24-hour hold/refund rule compliance = 100%; change fee accuracy ≥99.8%
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT 14 CFR Part 259 requires 24-hour hold or refund capability; ATPCO rule coding must precisely match website policy or exposes the airline to DOT enforcement action and reputational risk

l4_steps.name: Code fare rules in ATPCO category format
l4_steps.input: Approved fare rule design brief with all restriction parameters
l4_steps.output: Coded ATPCO fare rule record covering applicable Categories 2–35
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass coding accuracy ≥97%; coding cycle time ≤4 hours per rule set
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO's 35-category structure requires deep specialist knowledge; errors in Category 10 (Combinability) cause fare construction failures in GDS that are difficult to isolate and trace post-publication

l4_steps.name: Validate rule combinability and fare construction logic
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Online (Validator) / Amadeus Altéa PSS (test environment)
l4_steps.input: Coded ATPCO rule record
l4_steps.output: Combinability validation report; list of rule conflicts requiring recode
l4_steps.kpi: Zero Category 10 combinability errors at filing; validation first-pass rate ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline combinability checks are not fully automated — manual cross-referencing against partner airline Category 10 entries is required; gaps cause booking failures on connecting itineraries and trigger agency debit memos

l4_steps.name: Simulate fare rule impact across booking scenarios
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS (test environment) / PROS RM
l4_steps.input: Validated ATPCO rule record, sample booking scenarios across all active fare classes
l4_steps.output: Rule impact simulation report; revenue effect estimate by market
l4_steps.kpi: Simulation coverage ≥90% of active fare class/market combinations; revenue deviation from target ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: PSS test environments may lag production by 24–48 hours, meaning simulation results may not reflect current inventory state or recently published competitor fares

l4_steps.name: Obtain commercial sign-off on rule parameters
l4_steps.input: Rule impact simulation report and validated ATPCO rule record
l4_steps.output: Approved rule set with digital sign-off record and effective date authorisation
l4_steps.kpi: Approval turnaround ≤1 business day; escalation rate <5% of submissions
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval bottlenecks during peak retailing periods (holiday schedule filing) can delay time-sensitive competitive fare responses by 24+ hours, eroding revenue capture

l4_steps.name: Submit fare rules to ATPCO for publication
l4_steps.input: Commercially approved and validated fare rule record with effective date
l4_steps.output: ATPCO submission confirmation with effective date/time stamp
l4_steps.kpi: On-time filing rate ≥98%; filing lead time ≥4 hours before effective time (ATPCO minimum)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing windows have hard deadlines; rejected records or late submissions leave new fares without valid rules in GDS, causing tickets issued without rules to trigger agency debit memos

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS fare rule uptake and display accuracy
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO publication confirmation; effective date and time
l4_steps.output: GDS display verification report across all three distribution channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS rule display accuracy ≥99.5% within 2 hours of ATPCO effective time
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache refresh cycles vary from 15 minutes to 4 hours across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus — rule updates display inconsistently during the refresh window, generating agent calls and booking errors

l4_steps.name: Validate NDC channel fare rule presentation
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Airline direct booking engine
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO rule record, NDC offer/order API response
l4_steps.output: NDC rule compliance report; GDS/NDC parity assessment
l4_steps.kpi: NDC rule display accuracy ≥99%; NDC-to-GDS rule parity ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC offer construction logic does not fully consume all ATPCO rule categories — partial rule implementation in NDC channels creates parity gaps that confuse travel agents and generate customer complaints and potential DOT scrutiny

l4_steps.name: Monitor fare rule adherence in issued tickets
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / Revenue Integrity module
l4_steps.input: Issued ticket records from BSP/ARC settlement data
l4_steps.output: Rule violation exception report with ticket-level detail
l4_steps.kpi: Fare rule violation rate <0.5% of issued tickets; ADM (Agency Debit Memo) rate <0.1% of BSP transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue integrity tools process violations in batch cycles, meaning violations are identified post-issuance; late detection increases ADM management cost and agency relationship friction

l4_steps.name: Audit ATPCO rule records against published policy
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Online (retrieval) / internal pricing policy database
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO rule records, current commercial policy documentation
l4_steps.output: Compliance audit report; prioritised list of rule-to-policy discrepancies
l4_steps.kpi: Rule accuracy vs. policy ≥99.8%; monthly audit cycle; critical discrepancy resolution ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Policy changes communicated via email or informal channels may not trigger ATPCO rule updates — misalignment is often discovered only during BSP audit or customer dispute, by which point revenue leakage has already occurred

l4_steps.name: Receive and triage waiver and override requests
l4_steps.input: Customer or agency waiver request; IROPS or operational disruption notification
l4_steps.output: Triaged waiver request with approval recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Waiver triage time ≤4 hours; auto-approval rate for standard waivers ≥70%
l4_steps.pain_point: Mass waiver events during IROPS or weather disruptions generate hundreds of simultaneous override requests — Altéa PSS manual queue processing becomes a critical bottleneck without automated mass-waiver tooling

l4_steps.name: Apply approved rule override and document exception
l4_steps.input: Approved waiver decision record
l4_steps.output: Rule override applied to PNR; exception record created in ServiceNow
l4_steps.kpi: Override processing time ≤2 hours for approved waivers; 100% of exceptions documented in ServiceNow within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual PNR-level overrides in Altéa are not linked back to the originating fare rule — tracking waiver volume and financial impact requires manual reconciliation against BSP settlement data

l4_steps.name: Analyse exception patterns and update rule parameters
l4_steps.input: Exception records, waiver volume reports from ServiceNow, ADM data from BSP
l4_steps.output: Rule optimisation recommendation; updated rule design brief if exception threshold exceeded
l4_steps.kpi: Exception pattern review cycle = quarterly; rule update trigger = >2% waiver rate on any single rule
l4_steps.pain_point: Exception data is fragmented across Altéa, ServiceNow, and BSP with no unified dashboard — manual aggregation delays pattern recognition and allows suboptimal rule parameters to persist, increasing waiver costs

l4_steps.name: Ingest competitor fare data via ATPCO feed
l4_steps.input: Daily ATPCO Type A/B/C fare change transactions
l4_steps.output: Competitor fare matrix by O&D pair and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: Feed ingestion latency ≤15 min from ATPCO publication window
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filings lag real-time competitor NDC-direct pricing by 20-40 min, creating competitive blind spots on 20-30% of market fares during high-demand windows

l4_steps.name: Load demand signals and booking pace from NRM
l4_steps.input: Booking curve data, load factor forecasts, O&D demand segmentation
l4_steps.output: Demand signal dataset per flight-date-cabin combination
l4_steps.kpi: Demand signal refresh cycle ≤4 hrs for departures within 0–14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM demand forecasts calibrated on historical booking patterns underweight demand spikes from social media trends or flash sales by competitors, skewing price recommendations

l4_steps.name: Validate data completeness and quality gate
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare matrix and NRM demand signal dataset
l4_steps.output: Data quality scorecard; ingestion batch approved or rejected
l4_steps.kpi: Data completeness score ≥95% before optimization run proceeds
l4_steps.pain_point: Missing competitor fare data on thin routes (sub-daily frequency) triggers default pricing rules that undercut yield targets by 10–15% on marginal markets

l4_steps.name: Configure fare class elasticity parameters
l4_steps.input: Historical booking data, price-response curves, market segment definitions
l4_steps.output: Elasticity parameter set by market, segment, and season
l4_steps.kpi: Parameter review cycle ≤30 days; elasticity model R² ≥0.85 per market cluster
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM elasticity models require minimum 12 months of booking history — new or thin routes lack sufficient data for reliable calibration, requiring manual overrides that degrade model integrity

l4_steps.name: Set fare floor and ceiling guardrail rules
l4_steps.input: Approved tariff schedule, cost floor benchmarks, revenue targets
l4_steps.output: Min/max fare bounds per booking class and market pair
l4_steps.kpi: Guardrail coverage 100% of active markets before each daily optimization run
l4_steps.pain_point: Cost floor benchmarks require coordinated input from Finance (SAP S/4HANA FI/CO) but finance data latency averages 24–48 hrs, creating risk of stale floor values during fuel price volatility

l4_steps.name: Review and approve pricing model configuration
l4_steps.input: Elasticity parameter set and guardrail rule configuration
l4_steps.output: Approved pricing model configuration; version-tagged snapshot in audit log
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration approval cycle ≤4 hrs for routine updates; ≤24 hrs for structural changes
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM configuration lacks automated rollback capability — a misconfigured elasticity parameter can propagate to thousands of published fares before detection, requiring manual ATPCO correction filings

l4_steps.name: Run dynamic pricing optimization engine
l4_steps.input: Approved model configuration, demand signals, competitor fare matrix
l4_steps.output: Optimized fare recommendation set per flight-date-cabin
l4_steps.kpi: Optimization run completion ≤20 min for full network; recommendation coverage ≥98% of active O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM compute time exceeds SLA during IROPS events when demand signals are highly volatile, delaying fare updates during the highest-yield recovery window by 30–60 min

l4_steps.name: Apply business rules overlay and sanity checks
l4_steps.input: Raw optimization output from pricing engine
l4_steps.output: Rule-adjusted fare set with full audit log of modifications
l4_steps.kpi: Business rule violation rate ≤0.5% of recommended fares per optimization run
l4_steps.pain_point: Automated ceiling rules set for normal demand periods suppress legitimately high fares during demand surges, capping revenue on peak routes by an estimated 3–5% during holiday windows

l4_steps.name: Validate fare recommendations against guardrails
l4_steps.input: Rule-adjusted fare set from business rules overlay
l4_steps.output: Validated fare set approved for filing; exception list flagged for manual review
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-approval rate ≥90% of recommendations; manual review queue cleared within 30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing windows (20-min cycles) create time pressure that incentivises skipping manual review of exception fares, increasing risk of erroneous public fares reaching GDS and NDC channels

l4_steps.name: File approved fare set to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Validated fare set with booking classes, rules, and effective dates
l4_steps.output: ATPCO fare transaction records; filed fare effective timestamps
l4_steps.kpi: Filing-to-live latency ≤20 min (ATPCO standard distribution cycle)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing errors (invalid rule codes, tariff mismatches) trigger rejection queues requiring manual re-filing, delaying competitive fare responses by 40–60 min during time-sensitive price match windows

l4_steps.name: Distribute fares across GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Amadeus GDS / Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO fares and NDC dynamic offer parameters
l4_steps.output: Published fares active across all indirect and direct distribution channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS channel sync latency ≤30 min; NDC direct channel sync ≤5 min post-filing
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare synchronisation lags behind NDC direct channels by 20–25 min, creating temporary price disparities that trigger OTA parity violation claims under distribution agreements

l4_steps.name: Confirm fare availability in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Distribution confirmation messages from GDS and NDC channels
l4_steps.output: Fare availability audit report; PSS-confirmed live status
l4_steps.kpi: PSS availability confirmation within 35 min of ATPCO filing; availability accuracy ≥99.9%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa availability caching can serve stale fares to agents for up to 15 min after updates, causing booking conflicts and involuntary re-pricing that generates customer service escalations

l4_steps.name: Monitor live fare performance and revenue metrics
l4_steps.input: Booking transactions, yield actuals, load factor by flight-date
l4_steps.output: Real-time pricing performance dashboard; automated alert triggers
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance vs. forecast ≤±5%; alert response time ≤15 min from threshold breach
l4_steps.pain_point: AWS Redshift analytics pipeline has 5–10 min data latency, insufficient to detect and correct pricing errors on high-frequency short-haul routes before significant booking volume accumulates at wrong fares

l4_steps.name: Detect pricing anomaly and trigger override review
l4_steps.input: Performance dashboard alerts and deviation threshold breaches
l4_steps.output: Override recommendation; escalation decision to Pricing Manager
l4_steps.kpi: Anomaly-to-action cycle ≤30 min; false positive alert rate ≤10%
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM anomaly detection thresholds tuned for normal operations generate excessive false positives during promotional events, causing alert fatigue and delayed response to genuine pricing errors

l4_steps.name: Apply manual fare override and document rationale
l4_steps.input: Approved override decision with business justification
l4_steps.output: Override fare filed to ATPCO; audit trail record; model feedback flag
l4_steps.kpi: Override filing completion ≤20 min; override documentation rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual overrides not fed back as PROS RM training signals cause the engine to repeatedly recommend the same suboptimal fares, creating a costly correction loop that accounts for 15–20% of analyst override volume

l4_steps.name: Assess model performance and revenue uplift
l4_steps.input: Monthly revenue actuals vs. RM optimization recommendations
l4_steps.output: Model performance scorecard; recalibration flag with supporting analysis
l4_steps.kpi: Dynamic pricing revenue uplift ≥3% vs. static pricing baseline; model MAPE ≤8%
l4_steps.pain_point: Attributing revenue uplift to dynamic pricing vs. schedule changes, competitor capacity, or ancillary revenue requires controlled experiment design that lacks standardised methodology at most carriers

l4_steps.name: Recalibrate model and release updated configuration
l4_steps.input: Performance scorecard and recalibration recommendations
l4_steps.output: Updated model configuration; version-tagged release with change log
l4_steps.kpi: Recalibration cycle ≤30 days; post-recalibration uplift improvement ≥1% within 14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM model recalibration requires a 2–4 week data stabilisation period post-change, during which the system operates with lower confidence scores, increasing override frequency and analyst workload by 25–30%

l4_steps.name: Monitor ATPCO tax circulars and government notices
l4_steps.input: ATPCO Circular alerts, IATA Tax Monitor notifications, government tax authority bulletins
l4_steps.output: Change alert log with effective dates, affected markets, and change type classification
l4_steps.kpi: Alert intake within 2 hrs of ATPCO circular publication; 100% circular coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Tax Information System does not auto-push alerts to the PSS — manual monitoring is required, creating risk of missed effective dates on government-mandated tax changes

l4_steps.name: Classify surcharge/tax change type and geographic scope
l4_steps.input: Change alert log
l4_steps.output: Classified change record: government tax (TC3), fuel surcharge YQ (TC35), carrier surcharge YR (TC36), or airport levy
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥99%; misclassification rate <1 per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ vs. YR distinction is frequently misclassified under IATA Resolution 728, triggering incorrect tax calculation in Amadeus Altéa PSS and downstream GDS fare builds

l4_steps.name: Assess effective date urgency and regulatory deadline
l4_steps.input: Classified change record, regulatory effective date
l4_steps.output: Filing priority flag: emergency (<24 hrs), standard (3–7 days), or scheduled (>7 days)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of government-mandated tax changes filed before regulatory effective date; zero late filings
l4_steps.pain_point: Government tax changes in high-growth markets (e.g., APAC airport levies, EU ETS surcharges) often arrive with <48 hrs notice, requiring emergency ATPCO filing protocols that bypass the standard 3-day review cycle

l4_steps.name: Model fuel surcharge (YQ) rates by sector distance band
l4_steps.input: Jet fuel price index (IATA Fuel Monitor), sector distance bands, current YQ rate table
l4_steps.output: Proposed YQ rate schedule by sector range (short/medium/long-haul) and cabin class
l4_steps.kpi: YQ cost recovery rate ≥95% of actual fuel surcharge exposure per sector
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel price volatility (±15% intra-quarter) makes static YQ tables misaligned with actual cost within weeks of filing; PROS RM lacks native YQ recalculation — analysts must run Excel models outside the system

l4_steps.name: Calculate carrier-imposed surcharge (YR) per market and cabin
l4_steps.input: Operating cost variance report, competitor YR benchmarks from ATPCO Airfare Insight
