l4_steps.output: Proposed YR rate schedule by market pair, cabin class, and booking class
l4_steps.kpi: YR revenue contribution maintains ≥8% of total ticket revenue per long-haul market
l4_steps.pain_point: YR surcharges are commercially discretionary but are often misread by consumers as government taxes, generating EU Regulation 1008/2008 fare transparency complaints and compliance team workload

l4_steps.name: Benchmark proposed rates against ATPCO peer submissions
l4_steps.input: Proposed YQ/YR rate schedule, competitor published rates from ATPCO database
l4_steps.output: Benchmark comparison report: proposed rate vs. market range (min/median/max per sector)
l4_steps.kpi: Proposed rates within ±10% of market median for ≥90% of benchmarked sectors
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Airfare Insight competitor data lags 24–48 hrs, so benchmarking is retrospective; carriers can undercut within hours of filing, invalidating the benchmark before the rate is published

l4_steps.name: Obtain VP Pricing and revenue management sign-off
l4_steps.input: Benchmark comparison report, finance impact analysis, fuel cost exposure data
l4_steps.output: Approved surcharge rate schedule with authorisation record and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Sign-off cycle time <24 hrs for standard changes; <4 hrs for emergency filings
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP Finance approval workflows are not integrated with ATPCO filing system — approval is documented in SAP but filing is manual in ATPCO, creating audit gaps when approval and filing timestamps differ

l4_steps.name: Configure government tax codes in ATPCO Tax Engine (TC3)
l4_steps.input: Approved tax change record, regulatory bulletin, affected market list
l4_steps.output: ATPCO TC3 tax records configured for correct tax code, rate, currency, and effective date
l4_steps.kpi: TC3 record accuracy rate ≥99.9%; zero miscoded tax records in quarterly ATPCO audit
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO TC3 configuration for multi-tier tax structures (e.g., UK APD bands A/B, US segment fees + PFC + TSA) requires manual entry of up to 12 sub-records per market — high error risk with no built-in field validation in the ATPCO UI

l4_steps.name: File YQ/YR surcharge records to ATPCO (TC35/TC36)
l4_steps.input: Approved YQ/YR rate schedule, effective and discontinue dates, geographic scope
l4_steps.output: ATPCO TC35 (YQ) and TC36 (YR) records submitted with ATPCO confirmation reference
l4_steps.kpi: Filing submission within 2 hrs of sign-off approval; 100% of records submitted before effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO TC35/TC36 records do not support conditional logic (e.g., 'YQ applies only if fuel index exceeds threshold') — dynamic fuel surcharges must be manually re-filed each time the fuel index crosses a rate band boundary

l4_steps.name: Validate ATPCO filing acceptance and record integrity
l4_steps.input: ATPCO submission confirmation, filing reference number
l4_steps.output: Validation report: all records accepted, no rejection codes, effective dates confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: Filing rejection rate <0.5%; all rejections resolved and resubmitted within 1 hr
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO validation errors are returned as cryptic rejection codes requiring specialist knowledge to decode; documentation is maintained in offline PDFs not integrated with the filing UI, causing an average 45-minute resolution time per error

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS pick-up and cross-channel distribution lag
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation, effective date/time, GDS polling schedule
l4_steps.output: GDS pick-up confirmation for Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; distribution lag report
l4_steps.kpi: GDS distribution lag ≤4 hrs post ATPCO effective time for all three major GDS channels
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS poll ATPCO on different schedules (Sabre hourly, Travelport 2-hourly, Amadeus 4-hourly), creating distribution windows where channels display different total tax amounts — generating fare integrity complaints from OTAs and TMCs

l4_steps.name: Update surcharge and tax tables in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation, GDS distribution confirmation, approved rate schedule
l4_steps.output: Altéa PSS surcharge and tax tables updated; configuration change log created
l4_steps.kpi: Altéa configuration update completed within 2 hrs of ATPCO effective time; zero stale rate records in PSS
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS tax table updates are a manual configuration task — there is no automated sync from ATPCO filings to Altéa, requiring a separate maintenance window that can drift from GDS distribution timing and create channel pricing inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Update NDC API gateway tax calculation rules
l4_steps.input: Approved rate schedule, Altéa PSS configuration update confirmation
l4_steps.output: NDC API tax rules updated; API response test package generated
l4_steps.kpi: NDC API tax calculation matches ATPCO reference for 100% of test fare builds
l4_steps.pain_point: The NDC API gateway tax calculation is a separate microservice from Altéa PSS — version mismatches between PSS tax tables and NDC API rules produce pricing inconsistencies between indirect (GDS) and direct (NDC) channels, violating IATA NDC Standard Level 4 fare transparency requirements

l4_steps.name: Execute end-to-end fare build test across all channels
l4_steps.input: Test itinerary set (20 representative market pairs), ATPCO reference tax/surcharge totals
l4_steps.output: Channel test report: fare total vs. reference for GDS, NDC, and IBE channels
l4_steps.kpi: Test pass rate 100% across all 20 itineraries on first run; zero price discrepancies exceeding €0.01
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus Selling Platform test environment uses a 6-hr delayed ATPCO snapshot — post-filing tests on live-equivalent data require production credentials, increasing configuration change risk during the testing window

l4_steps.name: Audit post-effective-date fare calculations via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Live sold-fare sample (T+1 day), ATPCO reference tax and surcharge records
l4_steps.output: Audit report: percentage of sold fares with correct surcharge and tax applied by market and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Surcharge accuracy on sold fares ≥99.5% within 24 hrs of effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Airfare Insight audit is sample-based, not exhaustive — systematic miscalculation on low-volume markets can persist for weeks before appearing in the sample, leading to under-collection risk and potential regulatory penalties

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP/ARC settlement data against surcharge revenue
l4_steps.input: BSP/ARC settlement reports, ATPCO-expected surcharge revenue by market
l4_steps.output: Surcharge revenue reconciliation report: collected vs. expected, variance by market and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Surcharge revenue variance <1% of expected monthly collection; reconciliation completed within T+5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement data does not tag YQ and YR separately from base fare in all markets — revenue accounting must manually decompose settlement records, a process requiring 3–4 hrs per settlement cycle and prone to allocation errors

l4_steps.name: Investigate variance and initiate corrective ATPCO filing or ADM
l4_steps.input: Surcharge reconciliation report, variance-flagged markets and booking references
l4_steps.output: Root cause analysis, corrective ATPCO filing or PSS configuration patch, variance closure report
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance >1% resolved and corrected within 5 business days; zero repeat variances for same market within 90-day window
l4_steps.pain_point: Corrective ATPCO filings for past-ticketed fares require manual Agency Debit Memo (ADM) issuance via BSP/ARC for each affected booking — ADM processing cost can exceed the surcharge variance value for low-value corrections, forcing a commercial write-off vs. regulatory recovery trade-off

l4_steps.name: Load interline & SPA agreement terms into RA system
l4_steps.input: Signed interline agreement or Special Prorate Agreement (SPA) from commercial team
l4_steps.output: Active prorate factor set and SPA parameters loaded in ARA
l4_steps.kpi: Agreement setup lead time ≤5 business days from signature
l4_steps.pain_point: No standard digital handoff format for SPA terms — analysts manually transcribe flat-rate splits and minimum guarantees into ARA, introducing keying errors that cause systematic mis-proration

l4_steps.name: Ingest ATPCO prorate factor tables (PF Tables)
l4_steps.input: IATA Resolution 850 prorate tables published via ATPCO filing cycle
l4_steps.output: Validated prorate factor file loaded into ARA for IATA-standard interline tickets
l4_steps.kpi: Prorate table update cycle ≤24 hours after ATPCO publication date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO publishes 26 fare filing cycles per year; delayed ingestion causes mis-proration on interline tickets issued in the gap window — revenue impact typically discovered only at quarterly ICH reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Classify ticket as interline, codeshare, or hybrid
l4_steps.input: Issued electronic ticket (ET) with multi-carrier coupon segments and validating carrier code
l4_steps.output: Ticket classified with proration method assigned: IATA standard, SPA override, or codeshare split
l4_steps.kpi: Auto-classification rate ≥95% of interline tickets without manual intervention
l4_steps.pain_point: Codeshare tickets with separate operating vs marketing carrier codes require different proration logic than pure interline; misclassification routes codeshare revenue through ICH instead of bilateral settlement, triggering partner disputes

l4_steps.name: Extract OD fare components and fare basis codes
l4_steps.input: ET record with fare breakdown, applicable fare basis codes, and coupon sequence
l4_steps.output: Per-segment fare basis code, ticketed point mileage (TPM), and applicable fare component isolated per coupon
l4_steps.kpi: Fare extraction error rate <0.5% of processed interline tickets
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed class of service within a single ticket (e.g., J class on carrier A, Y class on carrier B) complicates fare basis assignment under IATA Resolution 762 — ARA auto-extraction fails on ~8% of mixed-cabin interline itineraries requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA mileage proration to derive carrier percentages
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Prorate Data + Amadeus Revenue Accounting (ARA)
l4_steps.input: Per-segment ticketed point mileage (TPM), total OD fare amount, ATPCO PF tables
l4_steps.output: Carrier-specific proration percentage and prorated revenue amount per segment
l4_steps.kpi: Mileage calculation accuracy ≥99.5% against IATA TACT reference data
l4_steps.pain_point: Mileage discrepancies between IATA TACT mileage tables and GDS-routed itineraries (reroutes, diversions) cause variance — airlines typically absorb or dispute the difference at quarterly ICH reconciliation rather than fixing source data

l4_steps.name: Apply Special Prorate Agreement overrides where eligible
l4_steps.input: SPA terms: flat-rate splits, percentage overrides, minimum/maximum guarantees per route and cabin
l4_steps.output: SPA-adjusted revenue allocation per carrier segment, superseding IATA mileage proration where SPA applies
l4_steps.kpi: SPA override application rate = 100% for all tickets on SPA-covered routes during SPA validity period
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines maintain 50–200+ active SPAs; no automated expiry alerting in ARA means analysts continue applying lapsed SPA terms, generating overpayments recovered only at annual SPA audit — average recovery lag is 14 months

l4_steps.name: Allocate taxes and YQ/YR surcharges per carrier rules
l4_steps.input: Tax and surcharge breakdown from ET record: government taxes, YQ fuel surcharge, YR carrier-imposed surcharge
l4_steps.output: Tax allocation per carrier — carrier-specific government taxes retained by respective carrier; YQ/YR allocated per agreement or IATA Resolution 728
l4_steps.kpi: Tax allocation error rate <0.1% of total ticket value across processed interline tickets
l4_steps.pain_point: YQ/YR fuel surcharge allocation rules vary by bilateral agreement and route — IATA Resolution 728 defaults are frequently overridden in SPAs, and smaller partner carriers often apply inconsistent rules, causing disputed tax remittance averaging $12–18 per ticket

l4_steps.name: Generate interline billing memo for ICH submission
l4_steps.input: Prorated revenue amounts per carrier, tax allocations, coupon status from GDS
l4_steps.output: Billing memo submitted to ICH for each partner carrier within IATA Resolution 743 deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Billing memo submission within T+30 days of travel date per IATA Resolution 743; late filing penalty avoidance rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Late coupon status reporting from GDS partners (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport) delays billing cycle — coupon voids and exchanges can arrive up to T+21 days, risking T+30 ICH deadline and triggering IATA Resolution 743 late-filing penalties

l4_steps.name: Validate billing memo against ET coupon at ICH
l4_steps.input: Submitted billing memo, original ET coupon data from issuing carrier, IATA prorate factor tables
l4_steps.output: ICH validation result: accepted billing memo or rejection with error code
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass ICH billing acceptance rate ≥92% of submitted memos
l4_steps.pain_point: Coupon status discrepancies (voided tickets, involuntary reroutes, ADMs already issued) between issuing and validating carrier cause ICH rejections — manual investigation averages 3 hours per rejected memo and ~2.4% of memos are rejected on first pass

l4_steps.name: Issue ADM or ACM to resolve billing discrepancy
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / Amadeus Revenue Accounting (ARA)
l4_steps.input: ICH rejection reason code, original ET data, partner airline's counter-claim if applicable
l4_steps.output: Agent Debit Memo (ADM) or Agent Credit Memo (ACM) issued to partner; revenue amount moved to suspense account pending resolution
l4_steps.kpi: ADM/ACM resolution within 45 days per IATA Resolution 850m; suspense account balance <0.5% of monthly interline revenue
l4_steps.pain_point: Partner carriers frequently contest ADMs citing different prorate factor versions — IATA Interline Dispute and Facilitation System (IDFS) resolution process can extend to 180 days, locking revenue in suspense accounts and distorting monthly revenue reporting

l4_steps.name: Submit net interline settlement to IATA Clearing House
l4_steps.input: Validated billing memos net of ADM/ACM, ICH monthly settlement calendar, partner net positions
l4_steps.output: Net settlement amount per partner airline forwarded to ICH for multilateral netting and disbursement
l4_steps.kpi: ICH settlement submission on-time rate = 100% (ICH settlement runs on fixed monthly calendar with no grace period)
l4_steps.pain_point: Errors in net calculation caused by parallel billing cycles for the same partner (current month billing + prior month ADM adjustments) generate short settlements — ICH charges 1% per month penalty on underpayment and requires supplemental submission

l4_steps.name: Post interline settlement to SAP General Ledger
l4_steps.input: ICH settlement confirmation file with net amounts per partner, tax allocation breakdown
l4_steps.output: Journal entries posted to GL — interline revenue recognition per IFRS 15, accounts receivable/payable updated per partner
l4_steps.kpi: GL posting within T+5 business days of ICH settlement confirmation; period-close accuracy = 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue recognition timing gaps between ARA settlement date and SAP posting cause interline revenue to be recognised in the wrong accounting period — reversals required on average for 3–5% of monthly interline revenue, distorting P&L and requiring CFO sign-off

l4_steps.name: Reconcile prorated actuals against RM interline forecast
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM) + SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO)
l4_steps.input: ICH settlement actuals by partner and route, RM system interline revenue forecast by O&D pair
l4_steps.output: Variance report: actual vs forecast interline yield per route and partner, flagging routes with structural mis-valuation
l4_steps.kpi: Interline yield variance ≤±3% of RM forecast; routes exceeding threshold reviewed within 10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: RM systems optimise for own-metal revenue and treat interline flows as residual — interline revenue attribution to O&D pairs is imprecise, causing systematic undervaluation of interline-dependent routes and suboptimal capacity allocation decisions

l4_steps.name: Audit SPA performance and flag renegotiation triggers
l4_steps.input: 12-month rolling SPA settlement actuals, guaranteed minimum revenue thresholds per SPA, partner traffic volumes
l4_steps.output: SPA performance scorecard per partner; renegotiation recommendation package for routes where guarantees are at risk or partner volumes have shifted >15%
l4_steps.kpi: SPA guarantee achievement rate ≥90% of active agreements; annual SPA review completion by Q1 for all agreements expiring in the calendar year
l4_steps.pain_point: No automated alerting when SPA minimum guarantees are trending below threshold — airlines detect shortfalls only at annual review, by which time the commercial window to renegotiate favourable terms has passed and the partner has already shifted volume to competing carriers

l4_steps.name: Monitor competitive fare environment
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare publications, market intelligence alerts
l4_steps.output: Competitive fare landscape report by market and direction
l4_steps.kpi: Monitoring cycle ≤24 hrs for all revenue-managed markets
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Insights carries a 24-hr lag vs real-time competitor GDS filings; analysts must cross-check Sabre FareManager for same-day changes, adding manual effort

l4_steps.name: Identify and classify fare change trigger
l4_steps.input: Competitive fare report, revenue performance dashboard
l4_steps.output: Fare change brief (market, direction, trigger type: reactive vs strategic)
l4_steps.kpi: Trigger-to-brief turnaround ≤4 hrs for urgent competitive matches
l4_steps.pain_point: Differentiating reactive (competitor match) vs strategic (sale/promo) triggers requires manual cross-referencing of RM inventory alerts and market briefs — no integrated triage workflow exists

l4_steps.name: Align fare strategy with revenue management
l4_steps.input: Fare change brief, NRM O&D inventory availability data
l4_steps.output: Approved fare strategy memo with booking class allocations and effective date window
l4_steps.kpi: RM alignment sign-off within 2 business hours of trigger brief submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Disconnect between NRM O&D inventory state and ATPCO-filed availability can cause short-lived promotional fares to sell out before retraction is processed, creating revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Define fare amounts, OD pairs, and basis codes
l4_steps.input: Approved fare strategy memo, existing tariff record extract
l4_steps.output: Fare amount table with FARE BASIS CODE, OD routing, currency, and cabin applicability
l4_steps.kpi: Fare basis code uniqueness validation pass rate 100% prior to rule coding
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO 8-character fare basis code limit constrains structured naming conventions for complex promotional fares with multiple conditions, forcing non-intuitive abbreviations that increase audit risk

l4_steps.name: Code ATPCO rule categories (Cat 3/5/6/7/14/15/25)
l4_steps.input: Fare amount table, booking conditions brief from commercial team
l4_steps.output: Coded ATPCO rule records for Categories 3 (Seasonality), 5 (Advance Purchase), 6 (Min Stay), 7 (Max Stay), 14 (Travel Restrictions), 15 (Sales Restrictions), 25 (Fare by Rule)
l4_steps.kpi: Rule coding accuracy ≥99.5% (errors per 1,000 rule records filed)
l4_steps.pain_point: Cat 25 (Fare by Rule) inheritance logic silently breaks when a parent tariff record is updated without cascading to child rules — causes undetected pricing errors across hundreds of derived markets

l4_steps.name: Build routing data and footnote records
l4_steps.input: Routing validation dataset, geographic applicability requirements, blackout date schedule
l4_steps.output: Filed routing record, footnote record with blackout dates and geographic exclusions
l4_steps.kpi: Routing validation pass rate ≥99% on first submission to ATPCO
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Routing Validator rejects non-IATA city pair combinations — LCC point-to-point networks with thin interline coverage frequently trigger routing exceptions requiring manual override justification

l4_steps.name: Validate rule completeness and conflict check
l4_steps.input: Complete fare record set (amounts, rules, routing, footnotes)
l4_steps.output: Pre-submission validation report — pass/fail with conflict flags and resolution notes
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-submission conflict rate ≤2%; zero records submitted with open blocking flags
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO pre-submission validator checks syntactic correctness but not cross-category semantic conflicts (e.g. Cat 5 advance purchase window exceeding Cat 6 min stay) — these pass technical validation but create unsellable fares in GDS

l4_steps.name: Submit fare transactions via ATPCO Fares Portal
l4_steps.input: Validated fare record package, effective date window, filing priority (standard T+2 or urgent T+0)
l4_steps.output: ATPCO submission receipt with transaction batch ID and filing timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Same-day filing completion for urgent competitive matches ≥95%
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO urgent filing (T+0) incurs a per-record surcharge — frequent reactive strategies against low-cost competitors inflate pricing operations costs, with no SLA guarantee on urgent processing times

l4_steps.name: Process ATPCO validation error report
l4_steps.input: ATPCO post-submission error and warning report
l4_steps.output: Corrected record set or documented error resolution log
l4_steps.kpi: Blocking error resolution turnaround ≤1 business hour; warning resolution ≤4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO error codes are non-self-explanatory (e.g. ERR 1078) — teams maintain internal error codebooks not derived from ATPCO official documentation, creating tribal knowledge dependency and onboarding risk

l4_steps.name: Confirm effective date sequencing and filing receipt
l4_steps.input: ATPCO submission receipt, intended sale open and travel date window
l4_steps.output: Confirmed effective date log; filing receipt stored in pricing operations tracker
l4_steps.kpi: Effective date accuracy 100% — zero same-day date conflicts or timezone mismatches
l4_steps.pain_point: Time-zone ambiguity in ATPCO effective dates (UTC vs local first/last point of departure) causes fares to go live or expire at unintended local times, particularly affecting international and trans-Pacific filings

l4_steps.name: Verify fare distribution across GDS channels
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing receipt, expected distribution timeline per GDS SLA
l4_steps.output: GDS distribution verification report across Sabre, Amadeus, and Travelport channels
l4_steps.kpi: GDS distribution lag ≤2 hrs post-ATPCO effective time; 100% coverage across all three major GDS channels
l4_steps.pain_point: Travelport GDS historically lags Sabre and Amadeus by 30–90 min on ATPCO fare updates — agencies on Travelport may sell at outdated fares during the distribution gap, triggering Agency Debit Memo (ADM) disputes

l4_steps.name: Perform live GDS pricing audit
l4_steps.input: Filed fare parameters, expected pricing rules, sample itinerary set
l4_steps.output: Pricing audit pass/fail report with 20+ sample itineraries per market and half-RT combinations
l4_steps.kpi: Pricing accuracy ≥99.8% across audit sample of ≥20 itineraries per market
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS combinability logic (Cat 10) can produce unintended through-fares when new local fares combine with existing through-fares — audit must include half-round-trip combinations, not only O&D pairs, or combinability errors reach ticketing queues

l4_steps.name: Activate NDC and direct channel fare distribution
l4_steps.input: GDS audit pass confirmation, NDC channel routing configuration
l4_steps.output: Activated fare set across all distribution channels including NDC and direct web
l4_steps.kpi: NDC channel parity with GDS fares ≤15 min lag; NDC fare availability ≥98% of filed itineraries
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC fare structures (IATA NDC 17.2+) do not natively support all ATPCO rule categories — ancillary-bundled and seat-inclusive fares require custom NDC offer mapping, adding 1–2 hrs to activation and creating parity gaps vs GDS

l4_steps.name: Monitor competitive matching and over-filing activity
l4_steps.input: Post-filing competitive feed, alert thresholds configured by market
l4_steps.output: Competitive response report with escalation flags for over-filed or under-cut markets
l4_steps.kpi: Competitor over-filing detection within 4 hrs; monitoring coverage ≥95% of revenue-significant markets
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Insights competitive feed does not cover NDC-only fares filed by competitors — LCC fare strategies distributed solely via NDC are invisible in ATPCO monitoring, creating a growing competitive intelligence gap

l4_steps.name: Execute periodic ATPCO tariff rule audit
l4_steps.input: Full tariff record export, quarterly audit schedule
l4_steps.output: Audit findings report with stale, expired, or conflicting rule flags and remediation plan
l4_steps.kpi: Stale rule ratio (>180 days since last review) ≤5% of active tariff records
l4_steps.pain_point: Accumulated legacy Cat 25 rules from prior sale campaigns create tariff bloat — stale rules still price in GDS if not explicitly expired, leading to unintended low-fare availability on high-demand travel dates and uncaptured revenue

l4_steps.name: File fare retraction or amendment as required
l4_steps.input: Audit findings report or RM/commercial retraction request
l4_steps.output: Filed retraction notice or amended tariff record; GDS depublication confirmation across all channels
l4_steps.kpi: Retraction-to-GDS-depublication lag ≤2 hrs via urgent ATPCO channel; zero open retraction requests >4 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO retraction does not immediately purge cached fare data in all GDS ticketing queues — tickets issued in the depublication window may be priced at retracted fares, requiring ADM recovery process and eroding agency trust

l4_steps.name: Ingest daily FX rate feed from Reuters Refinitiv
l4_steps.input: Daily FX rate file covering 150+ currency pairs
l4_steps.output: Raw FX rate dataset staged for validation
l4_steps.kpi: Rate feed received by 06:00 local time on 100% of trading days
l4_steps.pain_point: Reuters feed delays or gaps require fallback to Bloomberg Terminal; most legacy PSS integrations lack auto-failover, creating manual intervention risk on volatile trading days

l4_steps.name: Cross-validate rates against IATA published ROEs
l4_steps.input: Reuters Refinitiv FX dataset; IATA Resolution 024 ROE table
l4_steps.output: Variance report flagging deviations >0.5% from current IATA ROE
l4_steps.kpi: Variance detection accuracy 100%; processing time <30 minutes
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA ROE publication follows a monthly cycle while market rates move daily; EM currencies (ARS, TRY, NGN) can deviate 2-5% intraday, making IATA ROE structurally stale

l4_steps.name: Approve or escalate FX rate set for filing
l4_steps.input: Variance report; escalation threshold policy (>1% triggers Revenue Director review)
l4_steps.output: Approved rate set or formal escalation to Revenue Director
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation decision completed within 2 hours of rate receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: No system-enforced threshold in ATPCO Rate Desk; approval workflow is email-based, creating audit gaps and delay risk during high-volatility sessions

l4_steps.name: Submit ROE update to ATPCO Rate Desk
l4_steps.input: Approved FX rate set; IATA Resolution 024 ROE filing template
l4_steps.output: ATPCO ROE filing submission with Transaction Identification Number (TIN)
l4_steps.kpi: ROE filed ≥24 hours before effective date per IATA Resolution 024; 0 late filings per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing window closes at 23:59 ET; submissions after cutoff are auto-deferred 24-48 hours, causing pricing lag during currency crises

l4_steps.name: Confirm ROE acceptance and GDS distribution trigger
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filing confirmation; GDS distribution schedule
l4_steps.output: ROE effective date confirmed; GDS distribution job triggered
l4_steps.kpi: ROE active in all GDS channels within 4 hours of ATPCO acceptance
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache refresh latency (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport) can delay active ROE by up to 6 hours post-ATPCO acceptance, creating a window where agents book at stale rates

l4_steps.name: Distribute updated ROEs to NDC and direct channels
l4_steps.input: Confirmed ATPCO ROE; NDC offer/order schema for connected OTAs and TMCs
l4_steps.output: Updated ROE broadcast to all NDC-connected distributors; acknowledgement log
l4_steps.kpi: NDC distribution complete within 1 hour of ATPCO acceptance; 100% connected-channel coverage
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC ROE integration varies by OTA implementation — some require manual rate push via API; no universal real-time ROE feed standard causes parity gaps between GDS and NDC channels

l4_steps.name: Recalculate local-currency published fares in PSS
l4_steps.input: Updated ROE; published base fares in NUC/USD
l4_steps.output: Recalculated fare tables across 50+ local currencies
l4_steps.kpi: Fare recalculation completed within 2 hours of ROE update; 0 pricing calculation errors
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS fare recalculation runs as a nightly batch by default; intraday ROE changes require a manual override batch run, creating a ticketing window of up to 8 hours with stale local-currency fares

l4_steps.name: Validate converted fares against competitive price bands
l4_steps.input: Recalculated local fares; OAG Schedule Analyser competitive fare benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Fare validation report; outlier flags for commercially unviable currency conversions
l4_steps.kpi: <2% of fare basis codes flagged as outliers; validation cycle completed within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency devaluation events (e.g. ARS, TRY, NGN) render mechanical ROE-converted fares commercially unviable; NRM lacks automated local-market floor price rules, requiring manual intervention

l4_steps.name: Override floor/ceiling fares for distressed currencies
l4_steps.input: Outlier-flagged fares; local market floor price policy; SME sign-off
l4_steps.output: Manual fare floor/ceiling override filed in ATPCO; exception documented in audit log
l4_steps.kpi: Floor override filed within 4 hours of outlier flag; 100% of overrides carry documented SME approval
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO has no automated floor-price rule engine — every override requires a discrete manual tariff action; during hyperinflationary events this creates a filing backlog and inconsistent local pricing

l4_steps.name: Publish final fare tables to GDS channels and PSS
l4_steps.input: Validated and overridden fare tables; ATPCO distribution schedule
l4_steps.output: Live fare availability across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS; Altéa PSS fare cache refreshed
l4_steps.kpi: 100% GDS channel parity achieved within 6 hours of ROE effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: Three-GDS distribution (Sabre/Travelport/Amadeus) requires separate cache flush commands with no coordinated purge mechanism; partial updates cause GDS parity failures and agency ADM disputes

l4_steps.name: Revalue foreign-currency ticket revenue in SAP FI
l4_steps.input: Daily ticket settlement data from IATA BSP; current ROE
l4_steps.output: FX revaluation journal entries; updated AR balances in base currency
l4_steps.kpi: Revaluation completed by T+1 period close; FX variance <0.1% versus BSP settlement amount
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP settlement lag of up to 15 days creates a timing mismatch with daily SAP revaluation; hedged and unhedged positions must be tracked in separate GL accounts but airline chart of accounts often conflates them

l4_steps.name: Assess net FX exposure against Treasury hedge ratio
l4_steps.input: Net open FX exposure by currency pair; approved hedge ratio policy (60-80% of 12-month forward revenue)
l4_steps.output: Hedge gap analysis report; trigger notification if exposure outside approved band
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge ratio maintained within 60-80% for top-10 currency exposures; monthly review cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel and FX hedging compete for the same balance sheet capacity; treasury teams frequently lack dedicated FX analytics, relying on SAP TRM supplemented by Excel pivot tables that introduce manual error risk

l4_steps.name: Execute hedge adjustment via Treasury instruments
l4_steps.input: Hedge gap analysis; approved bank counterparties; ISDA master agreements
l4_steps.output: Forward contract or FX option trade booked in SAP TRM; IFRS 9 hedge effectiveness documentation
l4_steps.kpi: Hedge execution within 24 hours of gap identification; hedge effectiveness ≥80% per IFRS 9
l4_steps.pain_point: IFRS 9 hedge accounting documentation requirements are operationally burdensome; misclassification of FX derivatives as non-hedging instruments forces mark-to-market P&L volatility that cannot be offset

l4_steps.name: Identify tickets issued at superseded exchange rates
l4_steps.input: Ticketed transaction log; ROE change history with effective timestamps
l4_steps.output: Exception list of tickets priced at outdated ROE; total value-at-risk by currency
l4_steps.kpi: Exception identification completed within 24 hours of each ROE change; 100% ticket population audited
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS does not auto-flag tickets issued during the gap between ROE update and GDS cache refresh; full audit requires manual cross-referencing of ticketing timestamps against ROE effective times

l4_steps.name: Determine ADM issuance or waiver for out-of-rate tickets
l4_steps.input: Out-of-rate ticket list; FX variance threshold policy (>2% triggers ADM); agency relationship tier
l4_steps.output: Agency Debit Memo (ADM) issued or waiver granted per ticket; decision documented in audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: ADM issued or waiver granted within 5 business days of identification; affected ticket volume <0.5% of monthly issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: ADM disputes with travel agencies escalate to IATA resolution, which is time-consuming and costly; airlines routinely absorb sub-threshold FX variances rather than risk agency relationship damage

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly FX P&L impact dashboard
l4_steps.input: SAP FX revaluation journal entries; hedge effectiveness report; ADM totals; Altéa ticketing data
l4_steps.output: FX P&L dashboard by route and currency market; variance commentary for CFO pack
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by 5th business day of following month; FX impact reported to ±$100K accuracy
l4_steps.pain_point: FX P&L attribution across routes requires custom data joins between Altéa ticketing data and SAP GL — no native cross-system FX reporting; data pipeline maintenance creates monthly close bottleneck

l4_steps.name: Extract ATPCO fare inventory snapshot
l4_steps.input: Scheduled audit cycle trigger (daily or weekly batch)
l4_steps.output: Raw fare filing extract — basis codes, amounts, effective dates, markets
l4_steps.kpi: Data extract completeness ≥99.5% of active fare records
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch updates carry a 4–6 hr lag before GDS distribution; auditing a stale snapshot generates false-positive violations and wastes analyst investigation time

l4_steps.name: Validate fare basis codes against tariff rules
l4_steps.input: Raw fare filing extract
l4_steps.output: Fare basis code validation report — matched, mismatched, and missing entries
l4_steps.kpi: Validation processing time <2 hrs per 10,000 fare records; error detection rate ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with complex fare families (50+ basis codes per market) generate thousands of rule combinations; automated rule parsing frequently misinterprets footnote exceptions (ATPCO Category 15/25) requiring manual override

l4_steps.name: Cross-check fare coverage against active route inventory
l4_steps.input: Fare basis validation report, active route and schedule inventory from SkyWORKS
l4_steps.output: Market coverage gap report — routes with missing or expired filed fares
l4_steps.kpi: Market coverage completeness ≥98% of active O&D pairs with valid filed fares
l4_steps.pain_point: New routes activated in SkyWORKS may lack corresponding ATPCO filings within the required 24-hr effective-date window, causing inventory to distribute without valid fares and triggering GDS pricing errors

l4_steps.name: Apply IATA fare construction and combinability rules
l4_steps.input: Validated fare extract from Phase 1
l4_steps.output: Combinability violation log — fares failing IATA Resolution 722 checks
l4_steps.kpi: Fare construction error rate <0.5% of total filed fares per audit cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 722 combinability rules for international itineraries interact unpredictably with carrier-specific footnotes in multi-carrier routings, producing false-positive violations that require manual SME adjudication

l4_steps.name: Validate routing and stopover rule compliance
l4_steps.input: Combinability violation log
l4_steps.output: Routing compliance assessment — Category 3/4 rule adherence per fare
l4_steps.kpi: Routing rule compliance rate ≥99.2% of fare records processed
l4_steps.pain_point: Legacy routing rule structures in ATPCO Category 3 (Combinations) and Category 4 (Flight Application) produce ambiguous interpretations when codeshare partners operate a segment, leading to disputed ticketing and potential BSP billing errors

l4_steps.name: Check tax and surcharge applicability per market
l4_steps.system: Vertex Tax Engine / ATPCO Tax Filing
l4_steps.input: Fare records by O&D pair, current tax table extract
l4_steps.output: Tax applicability matrix — correct YQ/YR/ZP codes and amounts per market
l4_steps.kpi: Tax calculation accuracy ≥99.9%; YQ/YR surcharge compliance 100% within 2 hrs of ATPCO tax update
l4_steps.pain_point: Fuel surcharge (YQ) and carrier-imposed fee (YR) changes in volatile fuel markets require weekly ATPCO refile cycles; GDS distribution lag of 2–8 hrs post-change causes live mispricing and potential DOT consumer-protection violations (14 CFR Part 399)

l4_steps.name: Validate NUC and local-currency conversion compliance
l4_steps.system: ATPCO / IATA BSP Rate of Exchange (ROE) tables
l4_steps.input: International fare records, current IATA ROE monthly publication
l4_steps.output: Currency compliance report — fares breaching local-currency price caps or ROE thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: NUC conversion error rate <0.1% of international fare records; local-currency price cap breach detection within 48 hrs of IATA ROE update
l4_steps.pain_point: Monthly IATA ROE table updates can cause international fares to breach local-currency price caps in regulated markets (India DGCA, China CAAC) if automated re-pricing is not triggered within 48 hrs of the ROE effective date

l4_steps.name: Audit GDS-distributed fares against ATPCO filed records
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO fare extract, real-time GDS fare availability feeds across all three GDS
l4_steps.output: GDS parity audit report — mismatched fares, stale cache entries, missing availability
l4_steps.kpi: GDS fare parity compliance ≥99.5% of sampled fare records across all three GDS channels
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare cache refresh cycles (typically 4–6 hrs) mean stale fares remain bookable after ATPCO updates, creating revenue leakage, customer disputes, and potential IATA passenger protection liability

l4_steps.name: Verify NDC channel fare parity vs. filed fares
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Airline Direct Connect
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO fares, real-time NDC channel pricing API responses
l4_steps.output: NDC parity deviation report — fares where NDC pricing diverges from GDS/ATPCO
l4_steps.kpi: NDC–GDS price parity within ±$5 for equivalent fare conditions; parity deviations resolved within 24 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API responses bypass ATPCO rule validation for some offers, making automated compliance checking impossible; pricing inconsistencies between NDC and GDS are invisible to standard GDS audit tools and surface only through traveller complaints

l4_steps.name: Check interline fare settlement compliance via IATA BSP
l4_steps.input: Interline ticketing data, jointly filed ATPCO fares, partner proration agreements
l4_steps.output: BSP settlement compliance report — disputed interline fares and proration variances
l4_steps.kpi: Interline proration error rate <0.3%; BSP reconciliation variance within ±0.1% of billed amount
l4_steps.pain_point: Joint fare agreements with codeshare partners may not be synchronised with ATPCO filings; discrepancies surface only at monthly IATA BSP settlement, generating disputed interline billings that average 45 days to resolve

l4_steps.name: Log and categorise fare violations by severity
l4_steps.input: GDS parity report, routing compliance assessment, tax matrix, NDC deviation report, BSP settlement report
l4_steps.output: Violation register — all issues categorised Critical / High / Low with revenue impact estimate
l4_steps.kpi: Violation triage completion within 4 hrs of audit run; critical issues escalated within 30 min of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: No single platform aggregates violations across ATPCO, GDS, NDC, and BSP channels; analysts maintain parallel spreadsheets, creating version-control risk, delayed escalation, and fragmented audit evidence for regulatory review

l4_steps.name: Escalate critical violations to Director of Pricing
l4_steps.input: Violation register — Critical severity entries with revenue impact >$10,000
l4_steps.output: Correction order — approved refile instruction or GDS cache flush request
l4_steps.kpi: Critical violation resolution SLA ≤4 hrs from detection to correction order issued
l4_steps.pain_point: Pricing team refile authority requires dual-sign-off for fares above the materiality threshold; approval bottleneck averages 2.5 hrs, exceeding SLA during peak booking windows where revenue leakage compounds each hour

l4_steps.name: Refile corrected fares to ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Approved correction order, original fare record reference
l4_steps.output: ATPCO refile confirmation with effective date/time and filing receipt
l4_steps.kpi: ATPCO refile processing time ≤2 hrs (standard) / ≤30 min (emergency filing window)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO emergency filing window has limited daily capacity; peak-period conflicts when multiple carriers file simultaneously cause queue delays that extend GDS mispricing exposure and increase DOT violation risk

l4_steps.name: Flush GDS cache and verify re-distributed fare accuracy
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS API / Travelport Universal API / Amadeus Web Services
l4_steps.input: ATPCO refile confirmation
l4_steps.output: GDS cache flush confirmation; post-flush spot-check audit report
l4_steps.kpi: Post-flush fare parity restoration within 2 hrs across all three GDS; spot-check sample ≥50 O&D pairs per GDS
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache flush APIs differ by provider — Sabre requires separate requests per point-of-sale market; Travelport legacy ATPCO feeds lack API hooks and require manual cache refresh, extending mispricing window to 6+ hrs in some markets

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly compliance audit report with trend analysis
l4_steps.input: Violation register, resolution log, GDS parity data, tax compliance matrix, BSP settlement data
l4_steps.output: Monthly fare audit compliance report — violation counts, resolution rates, revenue impact, MoM trend charts
l4_steps.kpi: Report delivered by 5th business day of following month; violation trend growth ≤2% MoM
l4_steps.pain_point: Audit data from ATPCO, GDS feeds, BSP, and NDC channels is not integrated in a single data warehouse; manual consolidation requires 2–3 analyst-days per month and increases error risk in board-level reporting

l4_steps.name: Archive audit trail for DOT and IATA regulatory review
l4_steps.system: AWS S3 (encrypted archive) / SAP S/4HANA Finance document management
l4_steps.input: Audit report, violation register, ATPCO refile confirmations, correction orders, GDS flush receipts
l4_steps.output: Regulatory-grade audit archive with 7-year retention per DOT/IATA requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Archive completeness 100%; document retrieval SLA ≤48 hrs for regulatory or legal requests
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT consumer protection regulations (14 CFR Part 399) require documented evidence of fare display accuracy; incomplete or unstructured archives expose the carrier to civil penalties up to $37,500 per violation per day during DOT enforcement actions

l4_steps.name: Review audit KPIs in pricing governance committee
l4_steps.role: Director of Pricing / VP Revenue Management
l4_steps.input: Monthly fare audit compliance report, open violation backlog, action items from prior period
l4_steps.output: Approved corrective action plan; updated audit frequency thresholds for high-risk markets
l4_steps.kpi: Governance review completed within 10 business days of report delivery; 100% of action items assigned with named owner and due date
l4_steps.pain_point: Audit findings from international and interline markets require cross-functional alignment with Legal, Finance, and partner airlines; average alignment time of 3–4 weeks delays the corrective roadmap and allows repeat violations in the same audit cycle

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor ancillary fee schedule
l4_steps.input: Competitor ATPCO OS filings, industry ancillary revenue reports
l4_steps.output: Competitor ancillary benchmarking report — bags, seats, meals by carrier
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage of ≥10 competitive carriers; report delivered within 5 business days of cycle start
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO OS data does not always reflect actual displayed fees — airlines use waivers and loyalty exemptions that are not filed, understating true competitive price levels

l4_steps.name: Analyse ancillary revenue performance by category
l4_steps.input: PSS ancillary sales data, EMD settlement extracts from BSP/ARC
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue dashboard: revenue per passenger by category (bags, seats, meals), route, fare class, and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per passenger ≥$35 (IATA industry benchmark); dashboard refreshed daily
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD settlement data from GDS channels lags 24–48 hrs; real-time ancillary revenue visibility is unavailable, complicating intra-cycle performance management

l4_steps.name: Define ancillary pricing strategy and targets
l4_steps.input: Benchmarking report, revenue dashboard, corporate revenue plan
l4_steps.output: Approved ancillary pricing strategy document with targets by category, route group, and channel
l4_steps.kpi: Strategy approved by Revenue Committee within 5 business days; targets set for all three ancillary categories
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary pricing strategy must align with fare bundle strategy — misalignment (e.g., raising bag fees while lowering bundle price) causes customer confusion and internal revenue dilution

l4_steps.name: Define ancillary product catalogue
l4_steps.input: Approved ancillary pricing strategy, ATPCO OS sub-code reference table
l4_steps.output: Product catalogue: checked bags (1st/2nd/oversize/overweight), seat tiers (standard/preferred/exit row), meal options by route
l4_steps.kpi: Product catalogue covers ≥95% of ancillary revenue categories; catalogue configuration change lead time ≤7 calendar days
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Service Catalogue configuration changes require IT change-request tickets — average lead time of 5–7 days restricts rapid ancillary product launches or emergency price corrections

l4_steps.name: Configure dynamic seat pricing tiers
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM) / Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Seat map data, historical seat selection patterns, load factor forecasts by flight
l4_steps.output: Seat pricing tiers: exit row $25–$45, preferred front $15–$30, standard $0–$10 — linked to fare class and days-to-departure bands
l4_steps.kpi: Seat ancillary attach rate ≥30% of eligible bookings; seat revenue uplift ≥5% vs prior pricing cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Dynamic seat pricing rules in Altéa are statically mapped per fare class — true O&D-based dynamic seat pricing requires NRM integration that is not available across all GDS distribution channels, creating channel price inconsistency

l4_steps.name: Design ancillary bundle offers (fare + ancillary)
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Fare bundle definitions, ancillary product catalogue, competitor bundle analysis
l4_steps.output: Bundle definitions: e.g., Value Bundle (fare + 1 checked bag + seat selection); configuration loaded in PSS and NDC offer schema
l4_steps.kpi: Bundle attach rate ≥20% of total bookings; bundle revenue uplift ≥8% vs unbundled equivalent
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC bundle content is not consistently rendered in legacy GDS channels — Sabre and Travelport display gaps force manual workarounds and create a two-tier customer experience that advantages direct channel

l4_steps.name: Prepare ATPCO Optional Services (OS) filing
l4_steps.input: Approved ancillary fee schedule, ATPCO OS sub-code taxonomy (S5/S7/T183 tables)
l4_steps.output: ATPCO OS filing records: S5 carrier-defined sub-codes, S7 service definitions, T183 carrier fee tables per product
l4_steps.kpi: ATPCO OS filing accuracy ≥99.5% (zero mis-filed sub-codes); filing submitted ≥3 business days before effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO OS sub-code taxonomy covers 500+ codes; incorrect sub-code selection causes downstream EMD settlement failures, revenue leakage, and potential debit memos from GDS interline partners

l4_steps.name: Validate OS filing for GDS EMD compatibility
l4_steps.role: Fare Filing Analyst / IT Distribution Analyst
l4_steps.input: ATPCO OS filing records, GDS EMD issuance test scripts
l4_steps.output: EMD issuance test results confirming OS codes display, price correctly, and settle in Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: EMD test pass rate 100% across all three GDS environments before production go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD settlement rules differ between Sabre and Travelport — an OS code that settles correctly in Sabre may require a separate S7 record variant in Travelport, requiring duplicate filing effort and extended test cycles

l4_steps.name: Publish ancillary OS records to effective date
l4_steps.input: Validated OS filing records, approved effective date
l4_steps.output: Live ATPCO OS records distributed to all subscribing GDS and OTA channels
l4_steps.kpi: Effective date accuracy 100%; publication lead time compliance 100% (minimum 3-day ATPCO advance notice)
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO publish-to-effective minimum lead time is 3 business days — last-minute commercial decisions (e.g., flash promotional bag fee waivers) cannot be accommodated through standard ATPCO filing, requiring PSS-side workarounds

l4_steps.name: Configure ancillary upsell flows on .com and app
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS / NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Approved ancillary product catalogue, UI/UX design specifications, A/B test plan
l4_steps.output: Live ancillary upsell screens on airline.com and mobile app — bags, seat selection, meal pre-order — integrated with PSS booking flow
l4_steps.kpi: .com ancillary attach rate ≥45% of web bookings; mobile app attach rate ≥35%
l4_steps.pain_point: A/B testing ancillary upsell placement requires a separate web analytics platform — correlation with PSS ancillary sales data is manual, making attribution of revenue lift to specific UX changes unreliable

l4_steps.name: Load ancillary offers via NDC API for OTA/TMC
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: Ancillary product catalogue, NDC IATA 21.3 offer/order schema definitions
l4_steps.output: NDC ancillary offers available to NDC-connected OTAs, TMCs, and aggregators
l4_steps.kpi: NDC ancillary offer API response time ≤800 ms p95; NDC ancillary availability to connected agencies ≥90%
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC adoption by TMCs remains below 30% industry-wide — the majority of corporate bookings still flow via EDIFACT GDS with limited ancillary display, creating a structural ancillary revenue gap in the corporate channel

l4_steps.name: Configure EMD-S/A settlement in BSP and ARC
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / ARC (US domestic) / Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO OS records, EMD settlement rules by channel and ancillary type
l4_steps.output: Configured EMD-S (standalone) and EMD-A (associated) settlement records in BSP/ARC for all ancillary categories
l4_steps.kpi: EMD settlement error rate <0.1% of issued EMDs; EMD reconciliation completed within 48 hrs of issuance
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD-A (associated with a ticket coupon) vs EMD-S (standalone) distinction is frequently misconfigured — incorrect type selection causes revenue leakage, reimbursement disputes with travel agents, and regulatory non-compliance with IATA Resolution 722f

l4_steps.name: Monitor ancillary attach rates and revenue daily
l4_steps.input: Daily EMD sales data, PSS ancillary booking extracts, channel sales feeds
l4_steps.output: Daily ancillary revenue report by category, route, channel, fare class vs target
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per passenger ≥$35; bag attach rate ≥55%; seat attach rate ≥30%; meal pre-order attach rate ≥10% on eligible routes
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD data reconciliation between PSS and BSP/ARC settlement takes 48–72 hrs — ancillary revenue reporting is not real-time, delaying detection of attach rate drops or pricing anomalies until the following business day

l4_steps.name: Apply dynamic seat pricing adjustments by flight
l4_steps.input: Real-time load factor data, seat selection rates by cabin zone, days-to-departure bands
l4_steps.output: Dynamically updated seat price recommendations applied to open inventory — higher prices as departure approaches and seat scarcity increases
l4_steps.kpi: Seat ancillary revenue per ASM uplift ≥5% vs static pricing baseline; dynamic rule execution latency ≤15 min post load-factor update
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM dynamic seat pricing recommendations require manual implementation in Altéa for live flights — automated rule execution is not available, creating a lag between RM recommendation and price update that reduces revenue capture on high-demand departures

l4_steps.name: Conduct quarterly ancillary price review
l4_steps.role: Head of Ancillary Revenue / Pricing Analyst
l4_steps.system: AWS Redshift / Tableau / ATPCO Filing Portal
l4_steps.input: Quarterly ancillary revenue performance vs targets, competitor price monitoring, customer NPS feedback on ancillary fees
l4_steps.output: Updated ancillary fee schedule and new ATPCO OS filings where price changes are approved; revised targets for next quarter
l4_steps.kpi: Quarterly review completed within 10 business days of quarter end; approved price changes implemented within 5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent ancillary price changes require repeated individual ATPCO OS sub-code filings — no bulk-update mechanism exists, making large-scale fee restructures (e.g., repricing all 500+ OS sub-codes) operationally prohibitive within standard review cycles

l4_steps.name: Receive and log corporate RFP in CRM
l4_steps.input: RFP document from corporate travel manager or TMC (BCD, Amex GBT, CWT)
l4_steps.output: Logged account record with RFP details, TMC affiliation, and route footprint
l4_steps.kpi: RFP acknowledged within 2 business days; 100% of RFPs logged before pricing work begins
l4_steps.pain_point: RFPs arriving via TMC intermediaries create version-control conflicts when the corporate client also engages the airline directly, leading to duplicate records in Salesforce

l4_steps.name: Assess historical travel volume and route fit
l4_steps.input: Account travel history, O&D booking data from Sabre PRISM, prior contract performance (if renewal)
l4_steps.output: Volume assessment report with top-10 O&Ds, revenue contribution, and route coverage score
l4_steps.kpi: Minimum qualifying annual spend $250K; route overlap ≥60% of account top-10 O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST O&D data attributes bookings to agency PCC rather than corporate ID, making true account volume difficult to isolate without PRISM reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Determine account tier and eligibility decision
l4_steps.input: Volume assessment report, account strategic value flags
l4_steps.output: Tier assignment (Tier 1 / Tier 2 / Tier 3) or formal decline notification
l4_steps.kpi: ≥95% of eligible accounts tiered within 2 business days of volume assessment
l4_steps.pain_point: Tier thresholds are static annual targets and do not account for seasonal concentration; high-value accounts with strong Q4 travel patterns may be under-tiered mid-year

l4_steps.name: Model discount scenarios by O&D and cabin
l4_steps.input: Tier assignment, baseline fare inventory by booking class, O&D demand curves from SkyCAST
l4_steps.output: Discount scenario matrix (3–5 discount options per cabin class per contracted O&D)
l4_steps.kpi: Modelled revenue dilution <3% vs unconstrained network revenue on contracted routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM inventory controls on high-demand routes may cap discount depth without manual override by the Revenue Manager, creating tension between corporate sales targets and RM policy

l4_steps.name: Validate discount against yield floor — gate
l4_steps.input: Discount scenario matrix, route-level yield floor thresholds
l4_steps.output: Approved discount bands per O&D; rejected scenarios returned for rework
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue dilution from corporate contract ≤2% on constrained routes; ≤5% on off-peak routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Yield floors are set seasonally and may not reflect intra-season demand shifts; approving discounts in low-demand periods can conflict with late-breaking demand spikes not yet captured in SkyCAST forecasts

l4_steps.name: Draft and issue corporate pricing proposal
l4_steps.input: Approved discount bands, account tier, standard contract terms template
l4_steps.output: Formal pricing proposal document with fare basis codes, discount levels, and volume commitments
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal issued within 3 business days of yield approval; 100% of proposals include ATPCO-compatible fare basis code references
l4_steps.pain_point: Proposal templates are maintained separately from ATPCO rule structures; manual reconciliation is needed before filing, introducing errors when templates are not updated after ATPCO rule changes

l4_steps.name: Negotiate terms with corporate client or TMC
l4_steps.input: Pricing proposal, client travel policy requirements, TMC contracting requirements
l4_steps.output: Negotiation log with revised terms, version-controlled counter-proposal
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle completed in ≤3 rounds; average cycle time ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: TMC-represented clients (BCD, Amex GBT) frequently introduce non-standard contract clauses (guaranteed availability, cap-on-surcharges) outside the airline's standard ATPCO framework, requiring legal review that extends cycle time

l4_steps.name: Assess commercial impact of counter-proposal
l4_steps.input: Client counter-proposal terms, updated O&D volume commitment data
l4_steps.output: Updated revenue impact model with go/no-go recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Counter-proposal modelled and responded to within 1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Frequent counter-proposals on routes shared with alliance partners or interline agreements require additional proration impact analysis not automated in NRM, adding 2–3 days to cycle time

l4_steps.name: Obtain pricing committee sign-off
l4_steps.input: Final negotiated terms, revenue impact model, legal review outcome
l4_steps.output: Signed approval record with contract reference number
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracts with annual value >$1M approved at VP level; approval latency ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval workflows are largely email-based with no enforced audit trail in Salesforce; negotiated terms can deviate from the approved scenario without detection, creating post-execution disputes

l4_steps.name: File negotiated fares in ATPCO (Cat-15)
l4_steps.input: Approved contract terms, fare basis codes, routing rules, advance-purchase conditions
l4_steps.output: ATPCO-filed private fares with Category 15 (Accompanied Travel) or Category 25 (Fare By Rule) entries
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing completed ≥2 business days before contract effective date; 0% mis-pricing incidents on go-live day
l4_steps.pain_point: Category 15 private fare rule coding errors (incorrect routing restrictions or permitted combinations) surface only at booking engine pricing, causing customer-facing mis-pricing and requiring urgent ATPCO re-filing

l4_steps.name: Load and activate private fares in PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO-filed fare reference, booking class allocation, contract effective dates
l4_steps.output: Fare basis codes activated in Altéa inventory with correct booking class and date validity
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracted fare basis codes active in PSS ≥24 hours before go-live; zero booking-class mismatches
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS fare activation requires a manual QA step by a separate Revenue Management team; handoff gaps between Tariff and RM teams cause last-minute activation failures discovered only when test bookings are attempted

l4_steps.name: Configure corporate access in distribution channels
l4_steps.input: Contract activation record, corporate account code, TMC GDS subscriber IDs
l4_steps.output: Corporate account code active in NDC, Sabre GDS, Travelport GDS, and direct booking channels
l4_steps.kpi: Corporate traveller can book contracted fare within 24 hours of go-live; NDC channel coverage ≥80% of contracted fare conditions
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API Gateway does not support all Category 15 private fare rule conditions (e.g. negotiated blackout dates); non-compliant fares fall back to GDS-only distribution, limiting direct channel adoption targets

l4_steps.name: Validate end-to-end booking flow — gate
l4_steps.input: Test PNRs across all contracted O&Ds, channels (GDS, NDC, direct), and cabin classes
l4_steps.output: Booking validation report; confirmed go-live sign-off or defect list for remediation
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of test bookings price correctly across all channels before live date; defects remediated within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS test environment does not always replicate live Altéa inventory state; a clean test result can still produce pricing failures in production if RM inventory availability differs from the test snapshot

l4_steps.name: Monitor monthly volume commitment attainment
l4_steps.input: Monthly booking data from Sabre PRISM, direct and NDC booking feeds, contract volume schedule
l4_steps.output: Monthly volume attainment dashboard with trajectory vs annual commitment
l4_steps.kpi: Volume reporting latency ≤3 business days after month-end; attainment variance flagged if >10% below commitment trajectory
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM captures GDS-originated bookings only; direct channel and NDC bookings require separate reconciliation from Altéa PSS, causing systematic under-reporting of attainment and triggering false at-risk alerts

l4_steps.name: Identify and intervene on at-risk accounts
l4_steps.input: Monthly volume attainment dashboard, account-level booking trend analysis from AWS Redshift
l4_steps.output: At-risk account list with root-cause annotation and recommended intervention actions
l4_steps.kpi: ≥80% of accounts on-track to meet annual commitment by month 6; at-risk accounts contacted within 5 business days of flag
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboards are refreshed from AWS Redshift nightly; intra-month booking surges or drops are invisible until the next refresh cycle, delaying intervention and jeopardising end-of-year rebate qualification

l4_steps.name: Calculate and process annual rebates
l4_steps.input: Final annual volume attainment data, contract rebate tier schedule, reconciled booking records
l4_steps.output: Rebate payment or credit note issued to corporate account
l4_steps.kpi: Rebate processed within 30 days of contract year-end; 100% of rebate calculations independently verified against PRISM and Altéa data
l4_steps.pain_point: Rebate calculations depend on reconciled volume data across PRISM (GDS), Altéa PSS (direct/NDC), and SAP AR; discrepancies between sources cause disputes that delay payment and damage account relationships

l4_steps.name: Conduct annual contract performance review
l4_steps.input: Full-year performance scorecard, market rate benchmarks, account strategic value assessment
l4_steps.output: Contract performance scorecard with renewal recommendation and proposed revised terms
l4_steps.kpi: Review initiated ≥90 days before contract expiry; 100% of Tier 1 accounts reviewed in person
l4_steps.pain_point: Account managers carrying portfolios of >50 corporate contracts lack automated renewal-pipeline visibility in Salesforce; late review initiation (within 30 days of expiry) forces rushed renegotiation and weakens the airline's commercial position

l4_steps.name: Trigger renewal, renegotiation, or termination
l4_steps.input: Contract performance scorecard, renewal recommendation, updated market discount benchmarks
l4_steps.output: Renewal instruction (loops back to Phase 2) or notice of termination issued to account
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of contracts actioned ≥60 days before expiry; zero contracts lapsing without a documented decision
l4_steps.pain_point: Accounts flagged for termination due to low volume often have strategic route dependencies (e.g. government contracts on thin markets) that override commercial logic; no system-enforced escalation path exists to flag strategic override decisions for VP review

l4_steps.name: Ingest Competitor Fare Data Feeds
l4_steps.input: Scheduled OAG fare feed subscription; ATPCO tariff updates
l4_steps.output: Raw competitor fare matrix by O&D and cabin class
l4_steps.kpi: Feed freshness ≤4 hours from ATPCO filing event
l4_steps.pain_point: OAG data reflects filed fares, not real-time availability — lowest bookable fare may differ; requires GDS cross-check

l4_steps.name: Pull GDS Availability & Lowest Bookable Fare
l4_steps.input: O&D list flagged for monitoring; date range parameters
l4_steps.output: Live availability snapshot with lowest bookable fare per carrier
l4_steps.kpi: GDS poll coverage ≥95% of monitored O&Ds per cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS screen-scraping agreements restrict query frequency; high-volume polling risks Sabre rate-limit suspension

l4_steps.name: Validate and Cleanse Incoming Fare Data
l4_steps.input: Raw OAG and GDS fare extracts
l4_steps.output: Validated fare dataset with duplicate, null, and currency-normalised records
l4_steps.kpi: Data quality score ≥98% (nulls + duplicates < 2% of records)
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-currency fare records require real-time FX normalisation; stale FX rates distort price-index calculations

l4_steps.name: Gate: Assess Data Quality Threshold
l4_steps.input: Data quality score from validation step
l4_steps.output: Pass / Fail decision; failed batches re-queued for re-ingestion
l4_steps.kpi: Re-ingestion rate <5% of daily batches
l4_steps.pain_point: Repeated feed failures during ATPCO filing windows (Mon/Fri peaks) delay competitive response by 24-48 hours

l4_steps.name: Map Competitor Fare Families to Own Fare Basis
l4_steps.input: Validated competitor fare matrix; own fare basis code library
l4_steps.output: Normalised competitor-to-own fare family crosswalk table
l4_steps.kpi: Crosswalk coverage ≥90% of active competitor fare codes
l4_steps.pain_point: Unbundled competitor fares (ancillary-stripped) inflate apparent price gap; true total-price comparison requires ancillary fee modelling

l4_steps.name: Calculate Competitive Price Index by O&D
l4_steps.input: Normalised fare crosswalk; own published fares from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Price index report: own fare as % of competitor median and lowest
l4_steps.kpi: Price index within ±5% of strategic target band for ≥80% of monitored O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM price-index module requires manual refresh when own fares are updated mid-cycle; automated trigger not yet configured

l4_steps.name: Identify O&Ds with Material Competitive Fare Gap
l4_steps.input: Price index report; gap threshold parameters (e.g. >10% above market)
l4_steps.output: Shortlist of O&Ds requiring pricing review, ranked by revenue exposure
l4_steps.kpi: Shortlist generated within 2 hours of data ingestion cycle completion
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS RM gap detection relies on static threshold rules; dynamic thresholds by market maturity and load factor are not natively supported

l4_steps.name: Segment Demand Elasticity by O&D and Cabin
l4_steps.input: O&D shortlist; historical booking curves; own and competitor load factors
l4_steps.output: Elasticity coefficient per O&D segment; price-sensitivity classification (elastic/inelastic)
l4_steps.kpi: Elasticity model R² ≥0.80 for top-50 revenue O&Ds
l4_steps.pain_point: SkyCAST elasticity models are calibrated on historical data; post-pandemic travel pattern shifts reduce model accuracy on recently-opened routes

l4_steps.name: Model Revenue Impact of Fare Repositioning
l4_steps.input: Elasticity coefficients; proposed fare adjustment scenarios; current inventory by booking class
l4_steps.output: Revenue impact model: expected incremental revenue, load factor shift, and yield impact per scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Model run time ≤30 minutes per O&D scenario batch
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM scenario modelling does not automatically account for competitor retaliation; analyst must manually layer in retaliation assumptions

l4_steps.name: Gate: Revenue Uplift Exceeds Approval Threshold
l4_steps.input: Revenue impact model output; threshold: net yield improvement ≥1.5% or incremental revenue ≥$50K/quarter per O&D
l4_steps.output: Approved repricing candidates list; sub-threshold O&Ds shelved or monitored
l4_steps.kpi: Repricing candidates with confirmed positive revenue case ≥85% of submissions
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold calibration is manual and reviewed only quarterly; rapidly-changing competitive environments render thresholds stale within weeks

l4_steps.name: Build Fare Repositioning Recommendation Package
l4_steps.input: Approved repricing candidates; revenue impact model; elasticity data
l4_steps.output: Recommendation deck: proposed fare levels, filing strategy, effective dates, and risk summary
l4_steps.kpi: Recommendation package completed within 1 business day of gate approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual deck preparation in Tableau/PowerPoint is time-intensive; no templated recommendation workflow exists, leading to inconsistent submission quality

l4_steps.name: Route Recommendation to Pricing Committee
l4_steps.input: Recommendation package; pricing committee calendar; approval authority matrix
l4_steps.output: Committee review session scheduled; recommendation circulated for pre-read
l4_steps.kpi: Committee review turnaround ≤2 business days from submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Pricing committee quorum requirements delay time-sensitive competitive responses; competitors can re-price in hours while approval takes days

l4_steps.name: Gate: Pricing Committee Approval Decision
l4_steps.input: Recommendation package; competitive context brief
l4_steps.output: Approved fare levels and filing parameters; rejected recommendations returned for rework
l4_steps.kpi: First-pass approval rate ≥70% of submitted recommendations
l4_steps.pain_point: Committee rejections due to incomplete competitor context require analyst rework, consuming 1-2 days and potentially missing the competitive window

l4_steps.name: File Approved Fare Changes via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Approved fare levels; filing parameters (fare basis, rules, Cat-25 conditions, effective date)
l4_steps.output: ATPCO filing confirmation; fare effective date set (typically T+1 or T+7 per ATPCO filing cycle)
l4_steps.kpi: Filing accuracy rate ≥99.5%; zero Cat-15/Cat-25 rule errors
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO filing cycles (Mon and Thu effective dates) constrain competitive response agility; urgent off-cycle filings require ATPCO expedite fee

l4_steps.name: Load and Validate Fares in Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: ATPCO-filed fare data; Altéa fare loader configuration
l4_steps.output: Fares active in PSS; booking-flow validation completed across all selling channels
l4_steps.kpi: Fare loading SLA ≤2 hours post-ATPCO effective date; booking-flow validation pass rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa fare loader occasionally misinterprets complex Cat-25 combinability rules, producing phantom availability or incorrect pricing at booking — requires manual QA

l4_steps.name: Monitor Post-Change Booked-Fare Mix
l4_steps.input: Newly-loaded fares; booking velocity by class; competitor availability signals
l4_steps.output: Post-change performance dashboard: booked yield vs. target, load factor by class, competitor sell-down rate
l4_steps.kpi: Monitoring dashboard refreshed every 4 hours; booked yield vs. target tracked from day 1 post-filing
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM post-change monitoring requires manual dashboard setup per O&D; no automated alert when booked yield deviates >5% from forecast

l4_steps.name: Gate: Evaluate Competitive Position Restoration
l4_steps.input: Post-change price index; booked yield trend; competitor response actions detected
l4_steps.output: Position restored: cycle closed. Position not restored: O&D re-entered into repricing queue
l4_steps.kpi: Target: competitive price index within ±5% of strategic band within 14 days of fare change effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: Competitor retaliation (matching or undercutting) triggers a second repricing cycle; rapid tit-for-tat fare wars erode yield for all carriers with no passenger benefit

l4_steps.name: Publish Intelligence Report and Close Cycle
l4_steps.input: Full cycle data: gap detected, recommendation, approval, filing, post-change outcome
l4_steps.output: Competitive fare intelligence cycle report; lessons-learned log; updated monitoring watch-list
l4_steps.kpi: Cycle report published within 5 business days of position-restored confirmation
l4_steps.pain_point: Institutional knowledge from closed cycles is rarely captured systematically; repeated competitive patterns go unrecognised across analyst handovers

l4_steps.name: Benchmark competitor bundle structures
l4_steps.input: Competitor fare filings, ATPCO branded fare data, OAG market intelligence
l4_steps.output: Competitor bundle benchmarking report with component matrix
l4_steps.kpi: Coverage of top 10 competing carriers ≥100%; refresh cycle ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO branded fare data can lag 48–72 hrs post-filing; indirect bundle components (lounge, hotels) not visible in GDS fare displays

l4_steps.name: Analyse ancillary revenue by product category
l4_steps.input: Ancillary sales transactions, EMD issuance data, booking class mix reports
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue heatmap by route, cabin, and product type
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary revenue per passenger ≥$28; data completeness ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD-A revenue attributed to originating flight only; connecting itinerary ancillary splits require custom Redshift query logic

l4_steps.name: Model bundle demand & willingness-to-pay scenarios
l4_steps.input: Ancillary revenue heatmap, competitor benchmark, customer survey data
l4_steps.output: WTP model with recommended bundle price bands per tier and market
l4_steps.kpi: Model R² ≥0.85; scenario output covers ≥3 price points per tier
l4_steps.pain_point: PROS WTP modelling requires minimum 12 months of ancillary transaction history; new routes have insufficient training data

l4_steps.name: Approve bundle business case for launch
l4_steps.input: WTP model output, incremental revenue projection, implementation cost estimate
l4_steps.output: Signed business case approval with target launch date and bundle tier scope
l4_steps.kpi: Projected ancillary revenue uplift ≥12% within 6 months of launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Approval cycles involving Revenue Management, IT, and Distribution teams average 3–5 weeks; misaligned incentives between RM (yield) and Pricing (volume) can stall sign-off

l4_steps.name: Define bundle tier hierarchy and component matrix
l4_steps.input: Approved business case, ancillary service catalogue, cabin class mapping
l4_steps.output: Bundle tier design document: tier names, included services, exclusions, upgrade rules
l4_steps.kpi: Component matrix covers ≥3 distinct tiers (e.g. Basic, Standard, Flex)
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS service catalogue constraints limit ancillary bundling to pre-defined EMD-A service types; custom inclusions (e.g. lounge access) require workaround fare conditions text

l4_steps.name: Assign fare basis codes per bundle tier and cabin
l4_steps.input: Bundle tier design document, existing fare basis code registry
l4_steps.output: Fare basis code matrix mapped to each bundle tier, cabin, and market group
l4_steps.kpi: Zero duplicate fare basis code conflicts; code assignment completed within 3 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare basis codes limited to 8 alphanumeric characters; encoding tier, cabin, and market group within this constraint requires strict naming convention governance

l4_steps.name: Configure EMD-A ancillary service codes in PSS
l4_steps.input: Fare basis code matrix, IATA PADIS service type codes, bundle component list
l4_steps.output: EMD-A service definitions activated in Altéa, linked to fare basis codes
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of bundle ancillary components mapped to valid IATA PADIS service codes; zero orphaned EMD records
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA PADIS service type catalogue does not cover all airline-specific bundle inclusions; non-standard services require free-text SubCode which is not machine-readable in GDS displays

l4_steps.name: Validate bundle configuration in Altéa staging
l4_steps.input: EMD-A service definitions, fare basis codes, test booking scenarios
l4_steps.output: Staging validation report: pass/fail per test case, defect list
l4_steps.kpi: Test pass rate ≥95% before promotion to production; critical defects = 0
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa staging environment refresh lags production data by up to 7 days; edge cases involving interline itineraries cannot be fully simulated in staging

l4_steps.name: File bundle fares and conditions in ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Validated fare basis codes, price points from WTP model, market scope
l4_steps.output: ATPCO fare filing submission: fare amounts, Cat 1–35 conditions, market applicability
l4_steps.kpi: Filing submission-to-activation time ≤24 hrs; zero rejected categories on first submission
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat 15 (sales restrictions) and Cat 25 (fare combinations) rules for bundles are complex to encode; errors trigger GDS pricing failures that are difficult to trace back to specific category conflicts

l4_steps.name: Configure branded fare rule categories in ATPCO
