l4_steps.input: Bundle tier names, service inclusions/exclusions, brand attributes
l4_steps.output: ATPCO branded fare programme records with attribute icons and tier labels
l4_steps.kpi: Branded fare attributes display correctly in ≥95% of GDS certified pricing responses
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Branded Fares standard (BF categories) adoption varies by GDS; Travelport and Amadeus GDS render branded attributes differently, requiring separate QA validation per channel

l4_steps.name: Validate GDS fare display and auto-pricing accuracy
l4_steps.input: Filed ATPCO fares, branded fare records, GDS test booking scripts
l4_steps.output: GDS fare display validation report across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Pricing accuracy ≥99.9% vs. filed fare; branded attribute display rate ≥95% across all three GDS
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fare calculation engines interpret ATPCO combination rules differently; a rule that prices correctly in Sabre may misprice in Travelport due to differing Cat 25 implementation

l4_steps.name: Build NDC offer templates with bundle attributes
l4_steps.input: Bundle tier design, IATA NDC 21.3 offer schema, fare basis code matrix
l4_steps.output: NDC OfferItem definitions with BundleAttributeList populated per tier
l4_steps.kpi: NDC offer response time ≤800 ms (p95); bundle attributes present in 100% of eligible offer responses
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC 21.3 schema's BundleAttributeList does not support dynamic bundle composition at booking time; real-time ancillary availability (seat maps, bag slots) must be pre-fetched and cached, creating staleness risk on high-load routes

l4_steps.name: Configure bundle merchandising on direct booking channel
l4_steps.input: NDC offer templates, brand asset library, A/B test configuration
l4_steps.output: Direct channel bundle upsell flows live in staging: tier comparison UI, bundle highlights
l4_steps.kpi: Bundle comparison widget load time ≤1.2 s; A/B test variant coverage ≥20% of eligible sessions
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline.com front-end rendering of bundle tier comparisons requires bespoke UI development outside NDC scope; coordination between Pricing, IT, and UX teams is a recurring bottleneck

l4_steps.name: Execute end-to-end booking regression tests
l4_steps.input: Staging NDC offer templates, direct channel UI, GDS test scripts
l4_steps.output: Regression test report: full booking-to-ticket flow per tier across all channels
l4_steps.kpi: Zero P1/P2 defects in booking-to-ticket flow; regression suite ≥150 test cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Regression suite must cover GDS, NDC, and direct channel permutations; manual test execution across three GDS takes 4–6 days without automation; automation tooling investment often deprioritised

l4_steps.name: Activate bundle offer across all channels
l4_steps.input: Signed go-live approval, regression test sign-off, change management notice
l4_steps.output: Bundle tiers live in production: ATPCO fares active, NDC offers published, GDS updated
l4_steps.kpi: Channel activation completed within 4-hour go-live window; rollback plan tested
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordinated go-live across ATPCO (batch distribution), NDC API (real-time), and Altéa (inventory) is error-prone; ATPCO distribution to all GDS can take up to 48 hrs, creating pricing inconsistency window

l4_steps.name: Monitor bundle attach rate and incremental revenue
l4_steps.input: Live booking transactions, EMD-A issuance feed, channel attribution data
l4_steps.output: Daily bundle performance dashboard: attach rate by tier, channel, market, and cabin
l4_steps.kpi: Bundle attach rate ≥18% within 30 days of launch; incremental ancillary revenue uplift ≥12%
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD issuance data and PNR booking data arrive in Redshift via different ETL pipelines with up to 6-hour latency mismatch; attribution of bundle revenue to specific marketing or pricing actions is imprecise

l4_steps.name: Review bundle performance vs. targets at 30/60/90 days
l4_steps.input: Bundle performance dashboard, competitive intelligence update, customer NPS data
l4_steps.output: Performance review memo: targets met/missed, root cause analysis, recommended actions
l4_steps.kpi: Review cadence: D+30, D+60, D+90; action items assigned within 5 business days of review
l4_steps.pain_point: Causal attribution is difficult — attach rate changes may reflect pricing, competitor moves, or seasonal demand shifts; Tableau dashboards lack statistical significance testing natively

l4_steps.name: Adjust bundle composition or pricing based on performance
l4_steps.input: Performance review memo, updated WTP model, revised competitive benchmark
l4_steps.output: Change order: updated ATPCO filing, revised NDC offer templates, amended EMD-A config
l4_steps.kpi: Change cycle time from decision to live ≤10 business days; pricing adjustments within ±15% of original price points without full re-approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Minor bundle component changes (e.g. swap checked bag for seat selection) require re-filing in ATPCO, Altéa EMD config update, and NDC offer template revision — three separate systems with no single orchestration layer

l4_steps.name: Define LFG eligibility scope & fare rules
l4_steps.input: Annual pricing strategy review, commercial policy mandate
l4_steps.output: Documented eligibility criteria (route scope, booking class, advance-purchase limits, fare conditions)
l4_steps.kpi: Policy configuration cycle ≤5 business days; zero ambiguous eligibility clauses flagged by Legal
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare rule structures make same-fare-basis comparisons across carriers difficult; mismatched fare conditions (e.g. refundability, baggage) trigger spurious customer claims that are hard to reject

l4_steps.name: Configure claim window & compensation tiers
l4_steps.input: LFG policy document, approved compensation tiers (refund / travel credit / miles)
l4_steps.output: Configured claim submission window (e.g. 24 h post-booking) and compensation rule tables in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration accuracy ≥99% — zero erroneous payouts in first 30 days post-launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS compensation rule tables require manual maintenance; there is no native LFG workflow module, so each rule change must be scripted separately for web, call-centre, and API channels

l4_steps.name: Validate policy against DOT tariff requirements
l4_steps.input: Configured LFG policy parameters
l4_steps.output: Compliance sign-off or revision request with specific ATPCO rule references
l4_steps.kpi: Compliance review completion ≤3 business days; zero DOT tariff violations at launch
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT price advertising rules (14 CFR Part 399) require precise disclosure of LFG terms in all channels; a mismatch between the ATPCO-filed rule and the website copy has triggered enforcement action at peer carriers

l4_steps.name: Schedule automated competitor fare data feeds
l4_steps.input: LFG-eligible route and market list
l4_steps.output: Scheduled fare monitoring jobs; competitor fare baseline dataset refreshed ≤4 h
l4_steps.kpi: Market coverage ≥95% of LFG-eligible routes; data freshness ≤4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Screen-scraping competitor OTA prices violates most carrier terms of service and is legally risky; ATPCO-published fares lag real-time OTA dynamic pricing by several hours, creating a window where a competitor's low fare expires before the airline can verify a claim

l4_steps.name: Capture immutable reference fare at time of booking
l4_steps.input: Customer booking transaction
l4_steps.output: Fare snapshot stored in PNR history: fare basis, amount, booking class, applicable conditions
l4_steps.kpi: Fare snapshot latency ≤2 s per booking; capture rate ≥99.9% of LFG-eligible transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Dynamic pricing means the fare quoted to a customer can change within minutes of booking; the snapshot must be cryptographically signed or write-once to prevent retroactive manipulation by either party

l4_steps.name: Classify competitor fare for LFG comparability
l4_steps.input: Customer's booked fare snapshot; competitor fare from ATPCO feed
l4_steps.output: Comparability flag (eligible / ineligible) with structured rationale stored against PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Correct comparability classification ≥97%; false-positive ineligibility rate ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: Bundled fares (seat + bag + flexibility) vs. unbundled competitor fares create apples-to-oranges comparisons that PROS cannot resolve automatically; a manual adjudication queue exists but has no SLA, causing consumer complaints

l4_steps.name: Receive LFG claim via digital or voice channel
l4_steps.input: Customer claim submission: booking reference, competitor fare evidence, claimed price
l4_steps.output: CRM claim ticket with booking reference linked, channel source, and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Claim intake acknowledgement ≤4 business hours; self-service digital claim completion rate ≥55%
l4_steps.pain_point: High volume of ineligible claims (expired competitor fares, wrong route or date) creates manual review burden; Salesforce has no automated fraud-scoring integration, so every claim enters the same queue regardless of obvious ineligibility signals

l4_steps.name: Verify booking eligibility against LFG policy rules
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.input: CRM claim ticket; PNR booking history from Altéa
l4_steps.output: Eligibility determination (eligible / ineligible) with policy rule reference; rejection letter if ineligible
l4_steps.kpi: Eligibility verification turnaround ≤2 business hours; accuracy ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: PNR modification history in Altéa is often incomplete for bookings made through OTA intermediaries; the original-fare field is overwritten by post-booking changes, making verification ambiguous and requiring manual GDS history extraction

l4_steps.name: Authenticate competitor fare evidence via GDS/ATPCO
l4_steps.system: ATPCO OTA Transparency + Sabre GDS (fare display)
l4_steps.input: Customer-submitted competitor fare screenshot or URL; ATPCO feed for the claimed market and date
l4_steps.output: Authenticated competitor fare record with airline, booking class, conditions, and availability timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Evidence authentication turnaround ≤1 business hour; false-positive acceptance rate ≤3%
l4_steps.pain_point: Screenshots can be manipulated or show fares that were never genuinely bookable; the airline must independently verify via Sabre or ATPCO that the fare was published and seat was available at the claimed price at the time the customer booked

l4_steps.name: Calculate fare differential & compensation amount
l4_steps.system: PROS RM (compensation calculation module) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Authenticated competitor fare; customer's booked fare from PNR snapshot
l4_steps.output: Calculated net differential; proposed compensation type (refund / travel credit / miles) and amount
l4_steps.kpi: Calculation accuracy ≥99.9%; average compensation computation time ≤30 min
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency conversion for international routes and fare conditions (change fees, carrier-imposed surcharges, taxes) complicate net-fare differential calculations; PROS does not natively handle ATPCO tax stripping, requiring manual adjustments

l4_steps.name: Escalate large-differential claims for manager approval
l4_steps.input: Compensation calculation where differential exceeds authority threshold (e.g. >$300)
l4_steps.output: Approved or denied compensation decision with manager sign-off and rationale
l4_steps.kpi: Escalated claim approval turnaround ≤4 business hours; escalation rate documented monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: Salesforce has no native pricing-authority approval workflow; escalations route via email, causing delays above threshold and creating an audit gap where manager decisions are not formally captured in the CRM record

l4_steps.name: Issue compensation decision notification to customer
l4_steps.system: Salesforce Service Cloud + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved (or denied) compensation decision
l4_steps.output: Multi-channel customer notification (email, app push) with compensation type, amount, and redemption instructions
l4_steps.kpi: Notification delivery ≤15 min of decision; post-claim CSAT ≥4.2/5.0
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-channel customer communication (email, app push, SMS) requires manual coordination across Salesforce and a separate ESP; there is no unified outbound notification service, so message duplication and inconsistent status language are recurring issues

l4_steps.name: Process refund or travel credit to customer account
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/CO) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved compensation decision; customer payment method on file
l4_steps.output: Refund posted to original payment method or travel credit added to customer wallet
l4_steps.kpi: Refund processing ≤7 business days (per DOT requirement); travel credit issuance ≤24 hours; zero incorrect postings
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP refund processing requires the Altéa PNR to be in a settled state; open itineraries with future segments block automated refund initiation, requiring manual intervention by Revenue Accounting and causing SLA breaches

l4_steps.name: Award frequent flyer miles compensation if applicable
l4_steps.input: Compensation decision specifying miles award type and quantity
l4_steps.output: Miles credited to customer frequent flyer account with transaction reference
l4_steps.kpi: Miles credit turnaround ≤24 hours; posting accuracy ≥99.99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles compensation valuation vs. cash refund creates accounting complexity — Loyalty posts miles at face value but Finance recognises liability at estimated redemption cost; batch reconciliation between the two systems introduces a T+1 lag that delays audit sign-off

l4_steps.name: Update PNR & CRM record with claim disposition
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa PSS + Salesforce Service Cloud
l4_steps.input: Completed settlement confirmation from SAP and/or Loyalty
l4_steps.output: PNR OSI remark with LFG claim reference number; CRM ticket closed with structured disposition code
l4_steps.kpi: Record update completeness ≥99.5%; full audit trail retained for 24-month regulatory period
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa OSI remarks are free-text fields; there is no structured LFG claim field in the PNR, so data extraction for analytics requires brittle regex parsing that breaks when agents use non-standard remark formats

l4_steps.name: Aggregate LFG claim volume & payout metrics
l4_steps.input: Salesforce CRM claim exports; SAP settlement records; Altéa PNR data
l4_steps.output: Monthly LFG dashboard: claim volume, approval rate, average payout, market distribution, denial reasons
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh ≤T+1 business day; cross-system data completeness ≥98%
l4_steps.pain_point: Claims data sits in Salesforce, financial settlements in SAP, and booking records in Altéa — no native cross-system ETL pipeline exists; manual exports introduce reconciliation errors and a recurring 3–5% data gap between Finance and Operations views

l4_steps.name: Benchmark program cost against revenue retention
l4_steps.input: LFG payout totals; revenue from retained bookings; customer churn analysis
l4_steps.output: Program ROI assessment; markets where LFG drives positive retention vs. net cost centres
l4_steps.kpi: LFG program ROI ≥2.5× (revenue retained per $1 paid out); cost-per-claim ≤$45
l4_steps.pain_point: Counterfactual analysis (would the customer have cancelled without the guarantee?) cannot be measured without A/B test infrastructure; ROI is estimated using proxy metrics rather than observed behaviour, limiting confidence in market-level policy decisions

l4_steps.name: Recommend & implement LFG policy adjustments
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Automated Pricing + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Program ROI assessment; competitive fare environment trends from OAG
l4_steps.output: Revised LFG policy parameters (eligibility scope, claim window, compensation tiers) filed to ATPCO and updated in Altéa
l4_steps.kpi: Policy revision cycle ≤30 days; zero lapse in published guarantee terms during transition; ATPCO filing lead time ≥7 days before effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare rule amendments require a minimum 7-day advance notice period for GDS distribution; when a competitor launches an aggressive promotion, the airline cannot rapidly narrow LFG eligibility to limit liability — it is locked in for at least a week

l4_steps.name: Negotiate and renew GDS participation agreements
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: Annual contract review trigger; GDS segment fee schedule; competitive benchmark data
l4_steps.output: Signed GDS participation agreement; segment incentive thresholds; preferred agency incentive schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Blended GDS cost per segment ≤ $8.50; contract renewal completed ≥ 60 days before expiry
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS segment fees exceed direct booking cost by 3–5x; renegotiation leverage is weak without a credible NDC alternative to threaten channel shift

l4_steps.name: Configure airline inventory and booking classes in GDS
l4_steps.system: Amadeus GDS / Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Signed GDS agreement; booking class structure from Revenue Management; IATA airline code
l4_steps.output: Live airline profile in each GDS; RBD (reservation booking designator) map configured; availability feed active
l4_steps.kpi: GDS profile accuracy 100%; go-live within 5 business days of agreement signing
l4_steps.pain_point: RBD misalignment between RM inventory buckets and GDS booking class display causes sell-up failures and unintended availability leakage

l4_steps.name: Validate GDS neutral display compliance
l4_steps.input: Live GDS airline profile; IATA neutral display rules (Resolution 787)
l4_steps.output: Neutral display compliance report; exception list for escalation
l4_steps.kpi: Neutral display compliance 100%; exceptions resolved within 48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS display algorithm rankings can deprioritise non-alliance carriers; limited contractual recourse under IATA display rules for low-frequency routes

l4_steps.name: File published fares to ATPCO for GDS distribution
l4_steps.input: Approved fare structures from Pricing team; competitive market fare intelligence
l4_steps.output: Filed fares in ATPCO database; automated distribution to all subscribed GDSs
l4_steps.kpi: Fare filing lead time ≤ 24 hours from approval; filing accuracy rate ≥ 99.5%; fares live in GDS within 6 hours of ATPCO sync
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO distribution windows are time-boxed (4× daily sync cycles); last-minute competitive fare responses are delayed by up to 6 hours, costing revenue on price-sensitive O&Ds

l4_steps.name: Distribute ancillary content via GDS Rich Content & Branding
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS (Rich Content & Branding)
l4_steps.input: Ancillary product catalogue (seat upgrades, checked bags, meals); branded fare family definitions
l4_steps.output: Branded fare families and ancillary options visible in participating GDS terminals and OTA search displays
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attachment rate via GDS ≥ 18%; branded content display coverage ≥ 95% of GDS-connected terminals supporting RCB
l4_steps.pain_point: Many TMCs still use legacy green-screen GDS terminals with no RCB rendering capability; ancillary revenue opportunity is entirely lost for these bookings without an NDC fallback

l4_steps.name: Validate fare parity across all GDS channels
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM / AltéaRM) / Sabre AirVision Revenue Manager
l4_steps.input: Filed fares in ATPCO; live GDS availability and fare display data; direct channel pricing
l4_steps.output: Fare parity compliance report; exception log with root cause and remediation actions
l4_steps.kpi: Fare parity compliance ≥ 99%; parity exceptions resolved within 2 hours of detection
l4_steps.pain_point: Discrepancies between GDS fare display and website pricing trigger OTA meta-search penalties and TMC complaints; manual reconciliation across three GDSs is resource-intensive

l4_steps.name: Onboard travel agency and assign GDS PCC
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.input: Agency IATA accreditation certificate; agency booking tool selection; requested GDS access level
l4_steps.output: Active GDS pseudo-city code (PCC) for agency; booking access enabled; welcome pack issued
l4_steps.kpi: Agency onboarding cycle time ≤ 3 business days; zero unauthorised PCC provisioning incidents per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA agency accreditation lapses (bankruptcy, fraud, deregistration) require rapid GDS access revocation; absence of real-time IATA status feed creates compliance exposure windows

l4_steps.name: Configure corporate account discount in Sabre PRISM
l4_steps.input: Executed corporate contract; negotiated discount tiers; eligible fare classes
l4_steps.output: Corporate account code active in GDS; automated discount application rules configured; deal tracking enabled
l4_steps.kpi: Corporate account setup within 5 business days of contract execution; discount application accuracy 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: PRISM corporate deal tracking requires manual reconciliation with GDS booking data; unclaimed corporate discounts cause revenue leakage and contract compliance disputes with corporates

l4_steps.name: Set up automated booking data feed to TMC back-office
l4_steps.input: TMC back-office system specifications (Concur Travel, Cytric, Serko); booking data feed format requirements
l4_steps.output: Automated GDS booking data feed to TMC; PNR data mapping confirmed; feed latency within SLA
l4_steps.kpi: Data feed latency ≤ 4 hours; booking record completeness ≥ 99.5%; zero PNR data truncation incidents
l4_steps.pain_point: TMC back-office platforms require GDS-specific data field mappings; mapping errors cause incomplete trip records, failed expense reporting, and TMC SLA breaches

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS channel booking performance and cost
l4_steps.input: Daily GDS booking extracts; segment fee invoices; PSS booking data from Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.output: Channel performance dashboard; cost-per-booking by GDS; GDS vs. direct channel share trend report
l4_steps.kpi: GDS channel share of total bookings ≤ 40%; weekly channel cost variance report delivered every Monday
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS booking data arrives with 24–48 hour lag in standard feeds; real-time channel shift detection requires a separate streaming pipeline from Amadeus Altéa PSS not available in standard GDS reports

l4_steps.name: Audit and reconcile monthly GDS segment fee invoice
l4_steps.input: Monthly GDS segment fee invoice; actual booked segment count from PSS; previous month dispute log
l4_steps.output: Reconciled invoice posted in SAP FI/CO; dispute claim submitted to GDS for billing errors
l4_steps.kpi: Invoice reconciliation accuracy ≥ 99%; GDS billing disputes filed within 30 days of invoice receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS fee invoices aggregate millions of micro-transactions across three channels; manual audit is error-prone and GDS contracts impose 30–60 day dispute windows, causing irrecoverable revenue leakage on late discoveries

l4_steps.name: Identify and prioritise agencies for NDC migration
l4_steps.input: Agency GDS booking volume; NDC certification registry (IATA); agency technology roadmap data
l4_steps.output: NDC migration priority tier list; agency communication and incentive plan; migration timeline
l4_steps.kpi: NDC-enabled agencies ≥ 30% of total GDS booking volume within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: Large TMCs resist NDC migration due to back-office integration costs; differential incentive structures (EDIFACT vs. NDC surcharges) create agency channel conflict and risk booking diversion to competing carriers

l4_steps.name: Onboard certified agency to NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway / Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: IATA NDC-certified agency; API credentials; agreed IATA NDC schema version
l4_steps.output: Agency live on NDC channel; NDC booking, servicing, and ancillary capability confirmed in UAT
l4_steps.kpi: NDC onboarding cycle time ≤ 10 business days; NDC API error rate < 1% at go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API versioning fragmentation (IATA 17.2 vs. 21.3) creates compatibility issues; agency aggregators (Verteil, Travelfusion) introduce response latency and data field truncation that breaks ancillary flows

l4_steps.name: Monitor NDC adoption rate and distribution cost savings
l4_steps.input: NDC booking data; GDS segment fee data; direct channel booking data
l4_steps.output: NDC share report; distribution cost savings analysis vs. GDS; content gap register for NDC fallback scenarios
l4_steps.kpi: NDC booking share ≥ 25% of total distribution within 18 months; NDC cost per booking ≤ $2.50 vs. ≥ $8.50 for GDS
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC content gaps for group bookings, interline itineraries, and ticket reissuance force fallback to GDS for complex itineraries; true channel cost comparison is distorted by these forced GDS segments

l4_steps.name: Define direct channel KPI targets and benchmarks
l4_steps.input: Annual commercial plan; prior-year direct channel share report; GDS cost-per-segment benchmark
l4_steps.output: Direct channel scorecard with targets: share %, conversion rate, cost per booking, ancillary attach rate
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel share of total bookings ≥ 65%; cost per direct booking ≤ $3.50 vs. GDS ≥ $8.50
l4_steps.pain_point: No industry-standard benchmark for direct channel share forces reliance on internal year-on-year trend; low-cost carrier targets (70%+) may not be achievable without eliminating GDS completely

l4_steps.name: Select distribution schema — NDC 21.3 vs. EDIFACT
l4_steps.input: Agency and TMC capability survey; NDC adoption roadmap; current EDIFACT booking engine contract
l4_steps.output: Distribution schema decision: NDC 21.3 Offer/Order or legacy EDIFACT booking engine per channel segment
l4_steps.kpi: NDC-capable agency coverage ≥ 40% of managed travel volume within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: TMC and OTA NDC readiness varies widely; dual-schema support (NDC + EDIFACT) doubles integration maintenance burden and can create fare display inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Configure NDC API Gateway offer and order schemas
l4_steps.input: NDC 21.3 IATA standard schema; fare family definitions from Pricing team; ancillary service catalog
l4_steps.output: Published IATA NDC AirShopping, OfferPrice, and OrderCreate API endpoints; certified schema documentation
l4_steps.kpi: API response time ≤ 800ms at p95; schema validation pass rate 100% on IATA conformance test suite
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API latency degrades when Amadeus Altéa PSS availability calls chain through multiple O&D legs; caching strategy must balance freshness vs. response speed

l4_steps.name: Integrate Amadeus Altéa PSS real-time availability feed
l4_steps.input: NDC API Gateway offer request; Altéa inventory host connection parameters; RBD availability map
l4_steps.output: Live availability feed confirmed; booking class availability visible in web and app booking engines
l4_steps.kpi: Availability feed uptime ≥ 99.95%; stale availability incidents < 2 per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa PSS availability polling under peak traffic (holiday season surges) can cause throttling; CDN-layer availability caching introduces risk of selling closed inventory

l4_steps.name: Load fare products and ancillary catalog to web engine
l4_steps.input: ATPCO filed fares; ancillary service catalog (baggage, seat selection, meals, lounge); fare family branding rules
l4_steps.output: Published fare product tiles in web and app; ancillary catalog with pricing loaded; fare family descriptions live
l4_steps.kpi: Fare loading accuracy 100%; catalog sync from ATPCO to web engine ≤ 4 hours after fare filing
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filing cycle (Cat 25 / branded fare rules) requires manual QA against web display; discrepancies between filed rules and displayed conditions create regulatory and consumer protection risk

l4_steps.name: Apply dynamic pricing rules for direct channel uplift
l4_steps.input: RM inventory O&D availability; direct channel booking cost differential vs. GDS; promotional calendar
l4_steps.output: Direct-only fare incentives configured; dynamic pricing rules active in booking engine; GDS parity exceptions documented
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel average fare premium over GDS ≥ 0% (parity floor); promotional uplift in direct conversions ≥ 8% during campaign windows
l4_steps.pain_point: Fare parity clauses in GDS contracts prohibit offering lower fares on direct channel without also lowering GDS fares; undermines direct channel cost advantage and reduces RM flexibility

l4_steps.name: Validate fare display and regulatory compliance
l4_steps.input: Loaded fare products; DOT full-fare advertising rules (14 CFR Part 399); ancillary disclosure requirements
l4_steps.output: Compliance sign-off on fare display; all-in pricing confirmed; tax and fee disclosure checklist completed
l4_steps.kpi: Zero DOT full-fare advertising violations; fare display QA pass rate 100% pre-launch
l4_steps.pain_point: DOT Part 399 all-in pricing rules require taxes and fees displayed at first point of fare quotation; dynamic fee structures (carrier-imposed surcharges) change frequently and must be synced in real time

l4_steps.name: Monitor booking funnel conversion metrics in real time
l4_steps.input: Live web and app session data; funnel stage events (search → select → payment → confirm); device and channel segmentation
l4_steps.output: Real-time funnel dashboard; drop-off stage identification; conversion rate by device type and market
l4_steps.kpi: Overall booking conversion rate ≥ 3.5% (search-to-book); mobile app conversion ≥ 4.2%; funnel abandonment at payment ≤ 18%
l4_steps.pain_point: Session stitching across device and login state is unreliable without a persistent customer ID; anonymous user journeys cannot be attributed to downstream revenue, skewing funnel analysis

l4_steps.name: Run A/B tests on booking flow UX variants
l4_steps.input: Funnel drop-off report; UX hypothesis backlog; statistical significance threshold (95% confidence, n ≥ 5,000 sessions)
l4_steps.output: A/B test results report; winning variant identified or inconclusive flag; engineering backlog item for implementation
l4_steps.kpi: A/B test cycle time ≤ 3 weeks; conversion lift from winning variants ≥ 0.5% per test cycle
l4_steps.pain_point: Low-frequency route markets have insufficient traffic to reach A/B test statistical significance within acceptable test windows, forcing pooled analysis that dilutes route-specific behavioural insights

l4_steps.name: Optimise ancillary upsell prompts at checkout
l4_steps.input: Booking engine checkout step; passenger and itinerary data; ancillary pricing rules; upsell placement A/B test results
l4_steps.output: Configured upsell modules (seat upgrade, extra bag, EarlyBird equivalent, travel insurance); personalised offer rendering by traveller segment
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary attach rate ≥ 45% of direct bookings; average ancillary revenue per direct booking ≥ $28
l4_steps.pain_point: Overly aggressive ancillary prompts increase checkout friction and raise abandonment; tension between ancillary revenue maximisation and conversion rate requires continual tuning of prompt timing and frequency

l4_steps.name: Submit payment to CyberSource gateway and tokenise card
l4_steps.input: Customer payment details (card or digital wallet); booking total; 3-D Secure 2.0 authentication trigger
l4_steps.output: Payment authorisation response; tokenised card stored for future purchases; transaction ID linked to PNR
l4_steps.kpi: Payment authorisation success rate ≥ 97%; 3DS2 frictionless flow rate ≥ 85%; gateway downtime ≤ 0.05% monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: 3-D Secure challenge flows increase checkout abandonment by 12–18%; SCA (Strong Customer Authentication) mandates in EU/UK apply when serving international routes and require issuer cooperation beyond airline control

l4_steps.name: Screen transaction for fraud risk with Accertify
l4_steps.input: Payment authorisation token; device fingerprint; IP geolocation; booking velocity signals; passenger name
l4_steps.output: Fraud risk score; approve / review / decline decision; case flagged for manual review if score 60–80
l4_steps.kpi: Fraud chargeback rate ≤ 0.05% of transaction value; false positive decline rate ≤ 0.8%; manual review queue cleared within 2 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Flight booking fraud patterns (mule accounts, card-not-present abuse on international routes) evolve faster than rule-update cycles; model retraining lag creates a window of elevated fraud exposure during new attack patterns

l4_steps.name: Confirm booking and issue PNR in Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Successful payment authorisation; passenger data (APIS fields); fare and ancillary items; flight inventory segment
l4_steps.output: Confirmed PNR with all segments, ancillaries, and payment record; booking confirmation email triggered
l4_steps.kpi: PNR creation success rate ≥ 99.9%; confirmation email delivery within 60 seconds of booking; seat inventory decremented correctly 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Race conditions between simultaneous bookings on the last seat in an RBD bucket can cause duplicate sells before Altéa inventory lock propagates; requires seat re-offer logic and customer compensation workflow

l4_steps.name: Accrue Rapid Rewards miles for direct booking
l4_steps.input: Confirmed PNR; Rapid Rewards member number; base fare paid; fare class earning multiplier rules
l4_steps.output: Miles posted to member account; bonus miles for direct channel booking applied; accrual confirmation in member portal
l4_steps.kpi: Miles posting accuracy 100%; accrual posted within 72 hours of booking; direct channel bonus miles correctly applied ≥ 99.5% of eligible transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Miles accrual rules for ancillary spend (seat upgrades, bags) are inconsistently applied when ancillaries are added post-booking via app; loyalty platform integration requires separate API call that can fail silently

l4_steps.name: Generate direct channel performance dashboard
l4_steps.input: Booking transaction data; channel attribution; ancillary revenue; fraud loss data; conversion funnel metrics; Rapid Rewards accrual volumes
l4_steps.output: Weekly direct channel performance dashboard: share %, booking volume, revenue per booking, ancillary attach, cost per booking, fraud rate
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard refresh latency ≤ 4 hours; direct channel share reported to VP-level weekly; data completeness ≥ 99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Channel attribution is contested between direct and indirect when customers research on GDS/OTA then book direct; last-click attribution overstates direct channel contribution and misguides media spend decisions

l4_steps.name: Review direct channel share vs. target and escalate gaps
l4_steps.input: Weekly direct channel performance dashboard; annual KPI scorecard; commercial strategy review cadence
l4_steps.output: Gap analysis report; corrective action plan (promotions, UX fixes, NDC push, agency incentive review) if share < 65% target
l4_steps.kpi: Direct channel share ≥ 65%; month-over-month share growth ≥ 0.5pp when below target; corrective action plan issued within 5 business days of confirmed underperformance
l4_steps.pain_point: Structural direct channel share ceiling exists for airlines with large managed travel / TMC-dependent corporate customer base; share targets set for leisure mix may not apply to corporate-heavy routes without a distinct corporate portal strategy

l4_steps.name: Validate IATA/ARC Accreditation Status
l4_steps.system: IATA Customer Portal / ARC Agency Reporting Corporation
l4_steps.input: New agency application, submitted IATA or ARC number
l4_steps.output: Accreditation status confirmation with expiry date and bond coverage details
l4_steps.kpi: Accreditation validation completed within 2 business days of application receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: No API integration with IATA Customer Portal; analysts perform manual lookups causing 2–5 day delays and risk of using stale accreditation data

l4_steps.name: Conduct Credit Risk & Financial Assessment
l4_steps.input: Agency financial statements, IATA bond or ARC surety bond documentation
l4_steps.output: Credit risk score and recommended payment terms (cash upfront / credit limit)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of new agency applications assessed before contract execution; zero post-activation credit defaults
l4_steps.pain_point: Small TMCs may carry insufficient bond coverage for peak-period ticketing volumes; ARC debit memo recovery can take 60+ days, creating significant AR exposure

l4_steps.name: Create Agency & TMC Master Profile in PSS
l4_steps.input: Approved accreditation record, credit assessment outcome, agency legal entity details
l4_steps.output: Active agency profile with IATA number, PCC/office ID, ticketing authority, and GDS linkage
l4_steps.kpi: PSS profile activation within 1 business day of credit approval; profile accuracy rate ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: Duplicate IATA numbers across multiple GDS office IDs (PCCs) cause mis-attributed booking data and commission calculation errors that require manual reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Negotiate Preferred Agency Agreement Terms
l4_steps.input: Agency profile, historical booking volume, market share data from OAG Schedule Analyser
l4_steps.output: Signed preferred agency agreement with commission structure, volume incentive tiers, and performance thresholds
l4_steps.kpi: Contract cycle time ≤15 business days from first proposal to execution; ≥90% of tier-1 TMCs under signed agreement
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 814 caps base commission at 0% in most markets, forcing complex incentive structures that are difficult to model and audit; legal review backlogs extend cycle times

l4_steps.name: Configure Commission & Incentive Tiers in GDS Backend
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS (Agency Private Fares) / Travelport GDS (SmartFares)
l4_steps.input: Signed preferred agency agreement, commission rate schedule, incentive tier thresholds
l4_steps.output: GDS incentive configuration active across Sabre, Travelport, and Amadeus GDS for the agency PCC
l4_steps.kpi: Configuration live within 3 business days of contract signing; incentive calculation accuracy ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Incentive tier configuration must be replicated independently across three GDS platforms (Sabre, Travelport, Amadeus), tripling the manual workload and creating divergence risk if one platform update is missed

l4_steps.name: File Agency-Specific Private Fares via ATPCO
l4_steps.input: Negotiated net rates, rules, and fare basis codes from preferred agency agreement
l4_steps.output: ATPCO-filed private fare records with agency fare category (Category 35) applied
l4_steps.kpi: Private fare filing completed within 24 hours of contract activation; zero Category 35 fare rule violations on ATPCO audit
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 35 private fare rules are complex and proprietary; misconfigured rules can expose negotiated rates to the public GDS display, a contractual breach that can result in agency clawback demands

l4_steps.name: Configure GDS Agency Access & Booking Rules
l4_steps.system: Amadeus GDS / Sabre GDS / Travelport GDS
l4_steps.input: Active PSS agency profile, agreement ticketing restrictions, fare display permissions
l4_steps.output: GDS booking rules configured: point-of-sale restrictions, ticketing time limits, void and refund authorities
l4_steps.kpi: GDS rule configuration completed within 2 business days of agreement activation; zero unauthorised fare-display incidents in 90-day post-activation audit
l4_steps.pain_point: Maintaining consistent booking rule sets across three GDS environments is manual and error-prone; a mis-set point-of-sale rule in one GDS can allow an agency to ticket on an expired or wrong-market fare

l4_steps.name: Provision NDC API Credentials for TMC Self-Serve
l4_steps.input: TMC technical onboarding request, API integration specification, agreed content scope
l4_steps.output: NDC API credentials issued, sandbox test results passed, production channel activated
l4_steps.kpi: NDC channel live within 10 business days of TMC API onboarding request; NDC booking share ≥15% of managed corporate channel within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: Many mid-market TMCs lack in-house API development capability, stalling NDC adoption; OBT (online booking tool) compatibility with NDC ancillaries (seat, bag, lounge) varies widely, fragmenting the corporate traveller experience

l4_steps.name: Validate Fare Display Accuracy Across All Channels
l4_steps.system: Sabre GDS / Amadeus GDS / Travelport GDS / NDC API Gateway
l4_steps.input: Published and private fare inventory, real-time GDS fare display queries
l4_steps.output: Channel parity report confirming consistent fare display; discrepancy log for remediation
l4_steps.kpi: Fare parity across GDS and NDC channels ≥98%; critical parity failures (public rate shown as private) resolved within 4 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS cache refresh cycles (typically 20–30 minutes) mean new fare filings are not immediately visible, causing short-term channel inconsistency that generates agent complaints and mis-sells

l4_steps.name: Track Agency Booking Volume & Channel Mix
l4_steps.input: GDS booking transaction feeds, NDC booking logs, PSS ticketing records
l4_steps.output: Monthly agency performance dashboard: segment count, revenue, GDS vs NDC mix, market share
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly reporting cycle completed by day 5 of following month; GDS booking data completeness ≥99.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM captures Sabre bookings natively but requires manual data aggregation for Travelport and Amadeus segments, creating a consolidated view that is typically 5–7 days stale

l4_steps.name: Monitor GDS Segment Fee Exposure
l4_steps.input: GDS booking volume by channel, contracted segment fee rates per GDS
l4_steps.output: Monthly GDS cost analysis: segment fee accrual vs budget, shift-to-NDC savings model
l4_steps.kpi: GDS segment fee cost as % of distribution revenue ≤3.5%; NDC deflection saving ≥$1.20 per deflected segment
l4_steps.pain_point: GDS full-content agreements (FCAs) lock the airline into fee-per-segment structures even when NDC alternatives exist; renegotiating FCAs mid-term requires regulatory approval in some markets (EU, Australia)

l4_steps.name: Generate TMC Quarterly Scorecard & QBR Pack
l4_steps.input: Performance dashboard, incentive tier thresholds, customer satisfaction data
l4_steps.output: Quarterly Business Review (QBR) deck with booking trends, incentive attainment, and action plans
l4_steps.kpi: QBR delivered to top-20 TMCs within 15 days of quarter-end; ≥80% of TMCs achieve at least Tier 1 incentive threshold
l4_steps.pain_point: Corporate travel managers increasingly demand NDC-sourced data in QBR reports; Sabre PRISM does not natively include NDC transaction data, requiring manual data joining that adds 2–3 days to production cycle

l4_steps.name: Process BSP/ARC Weekly Settlement Run
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/AR) / IATA BSP Link
l4_steps.input: Weekly GDS ticketing transactions, BSP remittance files, ARC IAR reports
l4_steps.output: Settled ticket revenue posted to GL; BSP/ARC remittance confirmed and reconciled
l4_steps.kpi: BSP settlement reconciliation completed within 2 business days of remittance receipt; reconciliation accuracy ≥99.8%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP processing timelines vary by country (weekly in most markets, bi-weekly in some); multi-currency remittances create FX exposure that must be hedged in SAP — hedging mismatches can misstate revenue by 0.5–1%

l4_steps.name: Resolve Debit Memo Disputes with Agencies
l4_steps.system: IATA BSP Link / SAP S/4HANA Finance (FI/AR)
l4_steps.input: Raised debit memos (ADMs) for fare errors, refund violations, or commission overclaims
l4_steps.output: ADM accepted by agency or escalated to IATA Resolution panel; AR balance updated
l4_steps.kpi: ADM dispute resolution cycle ≤30 days; ADM acceptance rate ≥85% without IATA panel escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 850 requires airlines to issue ADMs within strict time windows (typically 9 months of ticket issue); late ADMs are automatically rejected by agencies, creating unrecoverable revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Calculate & Disburse Incentive Commission Payments
l4_steps.input: Quarterly performance data, incentive tier attainment report, agency bank details
l4_steps.output: Incentive commission payment disbursed; AP posting recorded against agency contract
l4_steps.kpi: Incentive payments disbursed within 30 days of quarter-end; payment accuracy ≥99.9% vs contracted incentive schedule
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual incentive tier calculations in spreadsheets are audit-vulnerable; tier attainment disputes with agencies delay payment and strain commercial relationships, particularly for top-50 TMCs during year-end close

l4_steps.name: Conduct Annual Agency Performance Review
l4_steps.input: Full-year scorecard, incentive attainment history, market share trends, agency feedback
l4_steps.output: Annual review findings report with contract renewal recommendation (renew / renegotiate / terminate)
l4_steps.kpi: Annual reviews completed for 100% of preferred agency contracts before contract expiry; ≥90% of top-20 TMCs retained at renewal
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline-TMC relationships are increasingly contested as TMCs push for NDC surcharges to offset GDS revenue loss; failure to renew top TMC agreements risks losing 8–15% of managed corporate revenue overnight

l4_steps.name: Renegotiate Terms or Execute Contract Termination
l4_steps.input: Annual review recommendation, revised commercial terms proposal, legal sign-off
l4_steps.output: Renewed agreement filed in SAP Ariba; or PSS profile deactivated and GDS access revoked for terminated agencies
l4_steps.kpi: Contract renewal executed ≥30 days before expiry to avoid lapse; termination-to-deactivation cycle ≤5 business days to prevent unauthorised ticketing
l4_steps.pain_point: Terminated agencies may continue issuing tickets against an active PSS profile if deactivation is delayed, creating ticketing liability; multi-GDS deactivation must be coordinated simultaneously to prevent exploits through alternate channels

l4_steps.name: Extract corporate travel-spend leads from market data
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP/ARC agency sales data, OAG traffic statistics, third-party spend intelligence reports
l4_steps.output: Ranked prospect list with estimated annual air spend by company
l4_steps.kpi: Pipeline coverage ratio ≥ 3× annual revenue target; ≥ 50 qualified prospects per quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP spend data lags 6–8 weeks, making real-time competitive displacement difficult to detect; no direct feed from GDS booking data into CRM

l4_steps.name: Score and qualify accounts by revenue potential
l4_steps.input: Prospect list, Salesforce opportunity scoring model, OAG Schedule Analyser competitive overlap data
l4_steps.output: Tier-classified account list (Strategic / Key / SME) with assigned sales owner
l4_steps.kpi: Account qualification cycle ≤ 5 business days; ≥ 80% of Strategic-tier accounts contacted within 10 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Scoring model relies on estimated spend; actual managed-travel programme size only revealed during RFP — leads to misallocation of senior sales resources

l4_steps.name: Assign account to sales rep and log in CRM
l4_steps.input: Tier-classified account list, territory alignment map, rep capacity dashboard
l4_steps.output: Account owner record in Salesforce; first-contact task created with due date
l4_steps.kpi: Account assignment completed within 2 business days of qualification; CRM data completeness ≥ 95%
l4_steps.pain_point: Territory conflicts arise when a corporate HQ and subsidiary are in different rep territories — no automated duplicate-account detection in Salesforce configuration

l4_steps.name: Receive and register incoming corporate RFP
l4_steps.input: Client RFP document (email / Ariba Sourcing / direct submission), account record
l4_steps.output: Opportunity record created in Salesforce; RFP deadline and decision date logged
l4_steps.kpi: RFP acknowledgement to client within 24 hours; 100% of RFPs logged in CRM on day of receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Large corporates increasingly issue RFPs via e-sourcing platforms (SAP Ariba, Jaggaer) that require separate supplier portals — manual data re-entry into Salesforce increases error risk

l4_steps.name: Analyse client O&D patterns and incumbent carrier share
l4_steps.input: Client-provided travel data (PNR extract or spend report), OAG Schedule Analyser, Sabre PRISM market share reports
l4_steps.output: O&D coverage matrix showing airline overlap, average fare paid, and load-factor seasonality
l4_steps.kpi: Analysis completed within 3 business days of RFP receipt; ≥ 90% of client O&D pairs matched to served routes
l4_steps.pain_point: Clients on unmanaged or partially managed programmes cannot provide clean PNR data — analyst must reconcile multiple credit-card and agency feeds, adding 1–2 days to analysis cycle

l4_steps.name: Build tiered discount and incentive fare proposal
l4_steps.input: O&D coverage matrix, current public fare inventory from Amadeus Altéa PSS, revenue floor guidelines from Revenue Management
l4_steps.output: Draft corporate agreement term sheet with tiered discount schedule, volume thresholds, and soft-dollar incentives (upgrades, lounge access)
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal build cycle ≤ 4 business days; proposed fares within ±5% of approved discount floor
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Cat-35 private fare filing requires airline-side ATPCO access and a structured ticketing agreement — errors in Cat-35 setup can expose private fares publicly, creating revenue leakage

l4_steps.name: Validate proposal profitability against revenue floor
l4_steps.input: Draft term sheet, route-level contribution margin thresholds from NRM, forecast load factors
l4_steps.output: Approved proposal (or revised discount structure) with sign-off from Revenue Management
l4_steps.kpi: Review turnaround ≤ 2 business days; 100% of proposals above revenue floor before submission
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM optimises individual O&D segments — corporate block commitments can conflict with open-market yield maximisation, requiring manual override negotiation between Sales and RM teams

l4_steps.name: Negotiate discount tiers and volume commitments with client
l4_steps.input: Approved proposal, client counter-proposal, competitive bid intelligence from Sabre PRISM
l4_steps.output: Agreed commercial term sheet with final discount schedule, volume thresholds, and performance ratchets
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation cycle ≤ 15 business days from proposal submission; win rate on competitive bids ≥ 35%
l4_steps.pain_point: Lack of alliance membership (not Star Alliance / Oneworld / SkyTeam) limits ability to offer interline or codeshare benefits demanded by globally travelling corporates — significant competitive disadvantage vs. network carriers

l4_steps.name: Route contract for legal and compliance review
l4_steps.input: Agreed commercial term sheet, standard corporate master agreement template, data privacy requirements (GDPR if EU travellers)
l4_steps.output: Reviewed and redlined contract draft with legal approval annotation
l4_steps.kpi: Legal review cycle ≤ 5 business days for standard agreements; 100% of contracts reviewed before execution
l4_steps.pain_point: EU-headquartered corporates require GDPR-compliant data processing addenda; PNR data sharing with Sabre PRISM must be covered by DPA — legal review backlog can delay contract execution by 2–4 weeks

l4_steps.name: Execute signed corporate agreement and archive
l4_steps.input: Legal-approved contract, client countersigned document, effective date confirmation
l4_steps.output: Fully executed corporate agreement stored in Ariba Contracts; Salesforce opportunity marked Closed-Won
l4_steps.kpi: Contract execution within 5 business days of legal approval; 100% of executed contracts uploaded to Ariba within 24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: DocuSign/wet-signature mismatches delay effective date confirmation; contract start date in Ariba must align exactly with PSS fare validity window to avoid fare not found (FNF) errors at ticketing

l4_steps.name: File corporate private fare codes in PSS
l4_steps.input: Executed contract, approved discount schedule, ATPCO Cat-35 fare filing template
l4_steps.output: Private corporate fare codes active in Altéa and distributed via Sabre / Travelport / Amadeus GDS
l4_steps.kpi: Fare codes live within 3 business days of contract execution; zero FNF errors in first 30 days post-launch
l4_steps.pain_point: Cat-35 private fare distribution requires individual negotiated agreements with each GDS — if a corporate TMC uses a non-preferred GDS, fares may not be visible, forcing off-channel bookings

l4_steps.name: Onboard corporate travellers to booking portal
l4_steps.input: Executed contract, corporate client IT contact, list of eligible travellers or SSO domain
l4_steps.output: Corporate booking portal access provisioned; NDC connection tested with sample booking
l4_steps.kpi: Portal onboarding completed within 5 business days; ≥ 90% of eligible travellers active within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC adoption by corporate booking tools (Concur Travel, Cytric) remains uneven — some OBT versions do not support full NDC offer/order flow, forcing fallback to GDS PNR path and losing ancillary upsell capability

l4_steps.name: Brief designated TMC on account parameters and reporting
l4_steps.input: Executed contract, TMC contact list, corporate reporting requirements (PRISM report schedule)
l4_steps.output: TMC briefing document; Sabre PRISM account code configured for monthly data extraction
l4_steps.kpi: TMC briefing completed before contract effective date; PRISM reporting activated within 5 days of go-live
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM only captures GDS-booked segments — direct NDC and website bookings are excluded from standard market-share reports, understating channel performance and inflating apparent GDS share

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly performance report vs. volume commitment
l4_steps.input: Sabre PRISM booking data, Amadeus Altéa PSS revenue data, AWS Redshift data lake (direct-channel bookings)
l4_steps.output: Monthly performance dashboard: actual vs. contracted volume, fare yield, channel mix, segment count
l4_steps.kpi: Report published by day 5 of following month; data reconciliation variance ≤ 1% between PRISM and PSS
l4_steps.pain_point: Multi-source data reconciliation (PRISM + Altéa PSS + AWS Redshift) is manual and error-prone — discrepancies between GDS-reported and PSS-confirmed revenue take up to 10 days to resolve, delaying remediation action

l4_steps.name: Conduct quarterly business review with client
l4_steps.input: Monthly performance reports (last 3 months), client travel policy, competitive market share data from Sabre PRISM
l4_steps.output: QBR presentation deck; agreed action plan logged in Salesforce; escalation cases (if any) created
l4_steps.kpi: QBR completed within 30 days of quarter end; ≥ 85% of Strategic accounts reviewed each quarter
l4_steps.pain_point: Clients increasingly demand real-time sustainability reporting (CO₂ per segment) — airline CO₂ data is not yet standardised across CORSIA and IATA Clean Flying framework, making accurate reporting manually intensive

l4_steps.name: Evaluate contract renewal, renegotiation, or exit
l4_steps.input: Full-term performance summary, renewal pricing analysis from ATPCO, competitive re-bid intelligence
l4_steps.output: Renewal decision (renew as-is / renegotiate terms / allow lapse); Salesforce renewal opportunity created if proceeding
l4_steps.kpi: Renewal decision made ≥ 90 days before contract expiry; corporate account retention rate ≥ 80% for Strategic tier
l4_steps.pain_point: Volume shortfall remediation clauses (clawback provisions) are difficult to enforce when underperformance is caused by airline schedule changes or cancellations — legal disputes can strain client relationship and delay renewal

l4_steps.name: Enrol airline in IATA NDC Registry
l4_steps.input: Board approval to implement NDC, IATA two-letter airline designator, company registration data
l4_steps.output: IATA NDC Registration Certificate; airline listed in public NDC Registry at target certification level
l4_steps.kpi: IATA NDC Level 4 certification achieved; registration completed within 10 business days of approval
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC certification is tiered (Levels 1–4) — most airlines must iterate through lower tiers before reaching Level 4 (full offer & order), adding 3–6 months to NDC launch timelines

l4_steps.name: Select NDC API schema version and message set
l4_steps.input: IATA NDC schema release notes, aggregator compatibility matrix, PSS NDC support assessment
l4_steps.output: Confirmed NDC schema version (e.g. NDC 21.3); approved message set — AirShopping, OfferPrice, OrderCreate, OrderRetrieve, OrderChange, OrderCancel
l4_steps.kpi: Selected schema version covers ≥80% of target aggregator ecosystem by booking volume
l4_steps.pain_point: Schema version fragmentation — Amadeus, Sabre, and Travelport aggregators each support different NDC versions; a version covering the full ecosystem may not yet exist, forcing the airline to maintain parallel schema support

l4_steps.name: Configure NDC API endpoint and authentication
l4_steps.input: Confirmed NDC schema version, approved message set, cloud infrastructure specification
l4_steps.output: Live NDC API endpoint URL, OAuth 2.0 client credential flow, rate-limiting rules per aggregator tier
l4_steps.kpi: API endpoint availability SLA ≥99.9%; OAuth token issuance latency ≤200ms
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with legacy PSS (non-NDC-native Amadeus Altéa or Sabre) must build an EDIFACT-to-NDC translation middleware layer — this adapter introduces latency and is a single point of failure between NDC offer requests and live inventory

l4_steps.name: Submit NDC API for IATA certification testing
l4_steps.input: Live NDC staging endpoint, IATA test scenario scripts, OAuth credentials for test harness
l4_steps.output: IATA Certification Report with pass/fail per message type; certification badge at target level
l4_steps.kpi: Certification pass rate ≥95% of mandatory test scenarios on first submission; resubmission cycle ≤15 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA certification test harness does not cover all real-world aggregator edge cases — airlines frequently pass IATA tests but encounter message interpretation failures in live aggregator connectivity, requiring post-certification fixes

l4_steps.name: Build ancillary services catalogue for NDC
l4_steps.input: Ancillary product inventory (seats, bags, meals, lounge access, priority boarding), retail pricing strategy
l4_steps.output: NDC ServiceList catalogue, ancillary SKU definitions, rich content assets (images, descriptions, T&Cs)
l4_steps.kpi: Ancillary catalogue completeness ≥90% of available products accessible via NDC ServiceList; content refresh cycle ≤48 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary catalogue updates in PSS do not auto-sync to NDC ServiceList — product pricing or availability changes in Amadeus Altéa must be manually reflected in the NDC layer, causing offer inconsistency during peak sale windows

l4_steps.name: Configure branded fare families in NDC OfferPrice
l4_steps.system: ATPCO Routehappy Rich Content (UPA / Ancillary Optimizer)
l4_steps.input: Fare family definitions (Basic, Standard, Flex, Business), fare conditions, ATPCO filed fare rules
l4_steps.output: NDC BrandedFare objects, ATPCO UPA (Universal Passenger Ancillary) content packages, fare family display rules
l4_steps.kpi: Branded fare NDC display parity with GDS content ≥98% of fare families; ATPCO UPA filing-to-NDC sync ≤24 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO UPA content must be filed separately from NDC fare data — dual-filing increases operational overhead and creates version drift between GDS branded fare display and NDC OfferPrice responses, exposing the airline to consumer-facing inconsistencies

l4_steps.name: Map RM dynamic pricing to NDC AirShopping response
l4_steps.input: O&D inventory availability, demand forecast, RBD thresholds from RM system, OfferPrice API call
l4_steps.output: Real-time availability matrix and dynamic prices embedded in NDC AirShopping response
l4_steps.kpi: AirShopping API response time ≤800ms at p95; dynamic pricing accuracy vs RM system ≥99.5%; availability sync lag ≤30 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC AirShopping calls trigger real-time RM inventory lookups — aggregator shopping bots generating >500 req/sec can saturate RM system capacity if not rate-limited, causing availability query failures that surface as blank NDC offer grids to agencies

l4_steps.name: Validate NDC offer-to-order round trip in staging
l4_steps.system: Postman / SoapUI (API testing); NDC API Gateway staging environment
l4_steps.input: Full NDC message set, test booking scenarios (return, ancillaries, exchange, refund), staging PSS environment
l4_steps.output: QA validation report, defect log, go/no-go recommendation for aggregator onboarding
l4_steps.kpi: Zero P0/P1 defects before aggregator onboarding gate; ≤5 P2 defects accepted with documented workaround
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC OrderCreate-to-PSS PNR translation errors cause silent booking failures — bookings appear confirmed in the NDC order layer but no PNR is created in Amadeus Altéa, resulting in passengers presenting at check-in with no reservation

l4_steps.name: Register NDC aggregator in API gateway
l4_steps.system: AWS API Gateway (API key and usage plan management)
l4_steps.input: Aggregator IATA NDC certification proof, signed commercial agreement, IP whitelist, rate tier classification
l4_steps.output: Aggregator API credentials (client ID, client secret), whitelisted endpoints, rate-limit profile assigned
l4_steps.kpi: Aggregator API credentials provisioned within 5 business days of commercial agreement execution
l4_steps.pain_point: Aggregator onboarding requires simultaneous legal, commercial, and technical sign-off across three separate airline departments — cross-team coordination delays average 15–20 business days beyond the contractual 5-day SLA in practice

l4_steps.name: Conduct end-to-end NDC booking flow UAT with aggregator
l4_steps.system: NDC API Gateway; Amadeus Travel API (aggregator side)
l4_steps.input: Aggregator test environment credentials, test booking scenarios (one-way, return, multi-ancillary, exchange)
l4_steps.output: Aggregator connectivity test report; confirmed booking flow — AirShopping → OfferPrice → OrderCreate → OrderRetrieve
l4_steps.kpi: End-to-end booking flow success rate ≥99% in UAT; ancillary attachment and retrieval validated across all test scenarios
l4_steps.pain_point: Even IATA-certified aggregators interpret NDC message schemas differently — the airline must maintain aggregator-specific message transformation rules in a compatibility layer, increasing maintenance cost linearly with the number of connected aggregators

l4_steps.name: Configure NDC agency incentive and cost model
l4_steps.input: Agency productivity data, GDS segment fee benchmarks, NDC adoption targets, commercial agreement terms
l4_steps.output: NDC booking incentive rate card, agency tier classification, cost-per-segment comparison model
l4_steps.kpi: NDC booking share of total indirect bookings ≥25% within 12 months of aggregator go-live; NDC cost-per-segment <GDS segment fee by ≥30%
l4_steps.pain_point: Airlines with GDS 'full content' agreements face contractual penalties for offering NDC-exclusive fares — withholding content from traditional GDS to drive NDC adoption may trigger financial penalties that exceed short-term NDC savings

l4_steps.name: Monitor NDC API transaction health and SLA compliance
l4_steps.input: NDC API transaction logs, HTTP error codes, response time metrics by aggregator and message type
l4_steps.output: Real-time API health dashboard, automated SLA breach alerts, daily SLA compliance report
l4_steps.kpi: NDC API uptime ≥99.9%; AirShopping p95 latency ≤800ms; transaction error rate ≤0.5% of all NDC calls
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC API errors are not always surfaced to booking agents — silent failures in AirShopping or OfferPrice cause agency tools to silently fall back to GDS EDIFACT content, masking NDC availability problems from operations teams until SLA reports are reviewed

l4_steps.name: Investigate and resolve NDC booking exceptions
l4_steps.system: AWS CloudWatch Logs; Amadeus Altéa PSS (order reconciliation module)
l4_steps.input: NDC error alert, failed OrderCreate transaction log, PSS PNR status query
l4_steps.output: Root cause analysis report, incident ticket, corrected booking or passenger compensation workflow initiated
l4_steps.kpi: NDC booking exception resolution ≤4 hours for P1 (passenger impacted at airport); ≤24 hours for P2 (booking error, no immediate travel)
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC OrderCreate failures that partially commit to PSS create 'ghost bookings' — passenger holds payment confirmation but no PNR exists, requiring manual reconciliation between the NDC order layer and Amadeus Altéa that can take hours during high-traffic periods

l4_steps.name: Plan and execute NDC schema version migration
l4_steps.system: Accelya Offer & Order Management; IATA NDC Change Log
l4_steps.input: IATA schema deprecation notice, aggregator readiness assessment, PSS compatibility matrix, dual-version support window
l4_steps.output: Schema migration plan, aggregator communication pack, rollback procedure, updated API endpoint supporting new version
l4_steps.kpi: Schema migration completed within 6 months of IATA deprecation notice; ≤2 aggregators requiring extended dual-version support beyond migration deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA NDC schema versions are deprecated on 18-month cycles — airlines with large aggregator ecosystems must coordinate simultaneous upgrades across 10+ partners, each with their own development calendars, creating a migration window where both old and new schemas must be supported in parallel at significant infrastructure cost

l4_steps.name: Report NDC adoption metrics to commercial leadership
l4_steps.system: Tableau / Power BI; AWS Redshift (data warehouse)
l4_steps.input: NDC transaction logs, GDS PNR booking data, agency adoption reports, incentive payment records
l4_steps.output: NDC vs GDS booking share report, revenue-per-booking comparison, agency adoption scorecard, ROI calculation vs GDS segment fees
l4_steps.kpi: NDC booking cost-per-segment <GDS segment fee; NDC ancillary attach rate ≥GDS equivalent; report delivered monthly within 5 business days of month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline NDC analytics require joining data from the NDC order management layer, GDS PNR feeds, and PSS — absence of a unified booking data model means NDC performance is routinely understated or double-counted, undermining the business case for continued NDC investment

l4_steps.name: Receive group travel request via agency or portal
l4_steps.input: Agency/corporate RFQ specifying route, date, pax count, and fare class preference
l4_steps.output: Group Request Record (GRR) with unique reference number
l4_steps.kpi: Request acknowledgement within 4 business hours; ≥95% SLA adherence
l4_steps.pain_point: Group requests arriving via email bypass PSS, creating untracked shadow bookings outside Altéa Groups

l4_steps.name: Qualify group size and policy eligibility
l4_steps.input: GRR with pax count, route, and travel dates
l4_steps.output: Eligibility decision — group qualifies (≥10 pax) or redirected to individual booking
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of groups below policy threshold redirected within 1 business hour
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent group-size thresholds across markets (10 pax domestic vs. 15 pax international) cause misrouting

l4_steps.name: Check flight seat availability for group block
l4_steps.input: Qualified GRR with flight/date combination
l4_steps.output: Available seat count by fare class; provisional block hold placed
l4_steps.kpi: Seat availability response time <30 seconds; provisional hold valid for 72 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: Provisional holds consume open inventory without commitment, degrading yield; no automated hold expiry in Altéa Groups without manual follow-up

l4_steps.name: Calculate group fare and applicable discount tier
l4_steps.system: ATPCO (Group Fare Rules) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Provisional seat block, travel dates, origin/destination market
l4_steps.output: Group fare proposal with applicable discount tier (e.g. 10%, 15%, 20%)
l4_steps.kpi: Fare calculation accuracy 100%; group fare ≥85% of equivalent published Y/B/M fare
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO group fare rule updates (filed twice per IATA season) can invalidate in-progress quotes; agents must manually cross-check effective dates

l4_steps.name: Apply contracted agency or corporate override discount
l4_steps.input: Agency/corporate profile, group fare proposal
l4_steps.output: Net group fare with contracted override applied
l4_steps.kpi: Contract compliance rate ≥98%; override correctly applied to all contracted accounts
l4_steps.pain_point: Sabre PRISM contract data can be out of sync with Altéa fare filing if corporate account team updates rates bilaterally outside PRISM

l4_steps.name: Assess yield impact against revenue plan
l4_steps.input: Group fare proposal, seat block size, flight load factor forecast
l4_steps.output: Yield impact assessment — approved / refer / decline
l4_steps.kpi: Group segment revenue contribution ≥ displacement cost; load factor impact <3 pp on high-demand flights
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM displacement cost models use O&D demand curves that may undervalue high-yield late-booking individual traffic displaced by early group blocks

l4_steps.name: Negotiate revised terms if yield threshold not met
l4_steps.input: Declined yield assessment, agency/corporate contact
l4_steps.output: Revised fare or reduced seat block accepted by agency; or request declined
l4_steps.kpi: Negotiation-to-acceptance rate ≥60% of referred cases; cycle time ≤2 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: No structured counter-offer workflow in Altéa Groups — negotiation conducted off-system via email, losing audit trail

l4_steps.name: Issue formal group quotation to agency
l4_steps.input: Approved fare, seat count, deposit schedule, contract conditions
l4_steps.output: Formal group quote document with 7-day acceptance deadline
l4_steps.kpi: Quote issued within 24 hours of pricing approval; quote acceptance rate ≥70%
l4_steps.pain_point: Quote documents generated outside Altéa as manual PDFs; version control errors lead to agency booking on superseded fare terms

l4_steps.name: Execute group contract and capture deposit obligation
l4_steps.input: Agency-signed group quote acceptance
l4_steps.output: Executed group contract with deposit amount and due date logged in PSS
l4_steps.kpi: Contract creation within 4 hours of acceptance; 100% of deposit deadlines captured in PSS
l4_steps.pain_point: Altéa Groups does not send automated deposit due-date reminders to agencies; agents must maintain manual chase calendars

l4_steps.name: Confirm deposit receipt and activate group booking
l4_steps.system: SAP S/4HANA Finance (AR) + Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.input: Deposit payment from agency (wire/BSP/ARC settlement)
l4_steps.output: Group booking status changed to Confirmed in Altéa; deposit recorded in SAP AR
l4_steps.kpi: Deposit-to-confirmation cycle ≤1 business day; 100% deposit reconciliation with SAP AR
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP/ARC settlement remittance data arrives with 24–48 hour lag, delaying booking confirmation and creating inventory limbo

l4_steps.name: Release unconfirmed seat block if deposit overdue
l4_steps.input: Expired deposit deadline with no payment received
l4_steps.output: Seat block released to open inventory; agency notified
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of overdue blocks released within 2 hours of deadline; zero revenue leakage from zombie holds
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual release process dependent on agent availability; after-hours expirations accumulate until next business day, blocking revenue optimisation

l4_steps.name: Collect passenger name list from agency
l4_steps.input: Agency-submitted passenger name list (CSV or API)
l4_steps.output: Individual PNRs created within group booking; name manifest complete
l4_steps.kpi: PNL submission by T−21 days; name completion rate ≥90% by T−14 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Agencies frequently submit names in non-standard formats requiring manual re-keying into Altéa; APIS-compliant data (passport, DOB) often missing at initial submission

l4_steps.name: Validate name count against contracted seat block
l4_steps.input: Submitted PNL, contracted pax count
l4_steps.output: Variance report — shortfall or excess names flagged
l4_steps.kpi: Name-count discrepancy <5% of group size; chase cycle completed within 48 hours of deadline
l4_steps.pain_point: Groups with >10% shortfall after T−7 days create difficult trade-off between releasing revenue-generating seats and maintaining client relationship

l4_steps.name: Process name changes within contractual tolerance
l4_steps.input: Agency change request; contracted name-change policy
l4_steps.output: Updated PNR with revised passenger details; change fee invoice if applicable
l4_steps.kpi: Name changes processed within 4 hours of request; change fee collection rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: Post-ticketing name changes require ticket reissue via ATPCO exchange rules; agents unfamiliar with involuntary vs. voluntary reissue procedures generate MCO errors

l4_steps.name: Trigger final ticketing and collect balance payment
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Altéa Ticketing + SAP S/4HANA Finance (AR)
l4_steps.input: Complete PNL, T−7 days ticketing deadline trigger
l4_steps.output: Electronic tickets (ET) issued for all pax; balance collected via BSP/ARC
l4_steps.kpi: 100% ticket issuance by T−5 days; balance collection within 48 hours of ticketing
l4_steps.pain_point: Ticketing queue backlogs during peak season (summer, holidays) cause missed deadlines; auto-ticketing rules in Altéa are not universally configured for group bookings

l4_steps.name: Cancel non-ticketed seats and release to inventory
l4_steps.input: Outstanding unticketed seats at T−5 days
l4_steps.output: Excess seats returned to open inventory; cancellation fees invoiced
l4_steps.kpi: Seat release within 2 hours of deadline; revenue recovery via reopen sale ≥80% of released seats
l4_steps.pain_point: Last-minute seat release on high-load flights can trigger yield recalculation in NRM, causing overbooking alerts that require manual adjudication

l4_steps.name: Reconcile group revenue against sales forecast
l4_steps.system: Amadeus Revenue Management (NRM) + AWS Redshift (data warehouse)
l4_steps.input: Final ticketed revenue, group contract value, displacement cost model output
l4_steps.output: Group revenue performance report; variance to forecast logged
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue variance within ±5% of group forecast; report delivered within 3 business days of departure
l4_steps.pain_point: NRM revenue accounting and Altéa ticketing revenue figures frequently diverge due to currency rounding and BSP reporting timing differences; manual reconciliation required

l4_steps.name: Update group sales KPI dashboard and close record
l4_steps.input: Reconciled group revenue report, cancellation rate, change fee revenue
l4_steps.output: Closed group booking record; KPIs updated in group sales performance dashboard
l4_steps.kpi: Group conversion rate ≥65%; average group booking lead time ≥45 days; change-fee revenue tracked monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau dashboard relies on Altéa data extracts with T+1 latency; real-time group sales performance is not visible to management during the booking window

l4_steps.name: Receive and log charter inquiry in CRM
l4_steps.input: Inbound charter enquiry via email, broker portal, or direct call
l4_steps.output: Charter opportunity record with client, route, date, and pax count
l4_steps.kpi: Inquiry-to-quote response time ≤4 hours for Group >50 pax
l4_steps.pain_point: Unstructured enquiry intake (email/phone) causes data loss and delays; no dedicated charter request portal integrated with Salesforce

l4_steps.name: Validate client credit standing and compliance
l4_steps.input: Client entity name and billing details from opportunity record
l4_steps.output: Credit risk tier (Low / Medium / High) and compliance clearance flag
l4_steps.kpi: Credit check completed within 2 hours of inquiry receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual credit verification via third-party tools not embedded in Salesforce; repeat credit checks for known clients due to lack of CRM integration

l4_steps.name: Check aircraft and crew availability in schedule
l4_steps.input: Requested departure date, route, and aircraft type from CRM opportunity
l4_steps.output: Available tail numbers and crew pairing windows for requested date
l4_steps.kpi: Availability check completed within 1 business hour; fleet utilisation conflict rate <5%
l4_steps.pain_point: Charter requests compete with scheduled service rotations; SkyWORKS schedule locks can prevent real-time availability reads during peak planning cycles

l4_steps.name: Calculate block-hour cost and fuel uplift estimate
l4_steps.input: Route distance (nautical miles), aircraft type, block hours, fuel price index
l4_steps.output: Direct operating cost estimate (fuel, crew, overflight fees, handling)
l4_steps.kpi: Cost model accuracy vs actuals ≤5% variance on completed charters
l4_steps.pain_point: Amadeus NRM is O&D-optimised for scheduled service; charter block-hour cost models are maintained in offline Excel workbooks outside the RM system, creating version control risk

l4_steps.name: Assess displaced scheduled revenue opportunity cost
l4_steps.input: Requested aircraft and dates, scheduled service forecast for same rotation
l4_steps.output: Opportunity cost figure (displaced revenue from scheduled pax) and net charter value
l4_steps.kpi: Charter net margin ≥15% above displaced scheduled service yield
l4_steps.pain_point: Displaced revenue calculation requires manual extraction of RM forecast data; no automated what-if tool to compare charter vs scheduled revenue in real time

l4_steps.name: Obtain Revenue Management approval for charter pricing
l4_steps.input: Block-hour cost estimate and displaced revenue opportunity cost
l4_steps.output: Approved floor price, target price, and negotiation band for the charter
l4_steps.kpi: RM approval turnaround ≤4 hours; pricing approval SLA breach rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: No formal workflow routing for charter pricing approvals in Amadeus NRM; approvals handled via email, creating audit trail gaps for regulatory and financial compliance

l4_steps.name: Build and transmit formal charter proposal to client
l4_steps.input: Approved pricing band, route details, aircraft type, and service inclusions
l4_steps.output: Charter proposal document (PDF) with pricing, terms, validity period, and deposit schedule
l4_steps.kpi: Proposal issued within 6 hours of RM approval; proposal acceptance rate ≥40%
